❯ /permissions


❯ Repositories in scope for this work: bagatelle, infusion-6, howe-sound-mapping-2026, saanich-peninsula-flora. A first round port of the visualisation framework hosted in src/client here from Infusion 4 to Infusion 6 is largely complete, but unidiomatic, at src/client/js/i6 - we now need to complete this port, decomposing the components here into an idiomatic set of SFC .vue files as described at https://ponder.org.uk/docs/fluid-view/ . There are various drivers holding functionality which need to be preserved, particularly the newer "Beas" drivers such as indexBeasBCBA.html but also indexBlitz.html and indexDiatoms.html, but also the overal "bioreportr" framework which runs howe-sound-mapping-2026 and saanich-peninsula-flora. There is a first pass port at indexBeasBCBA.html but this is unidiomatic since it continues with the "static templating" notion inherited from Infusion 4. Instead the app should construct using a "hydrating" approach in which a minimal template is written with placeholder markup and dependencies, which can be rendered either statically using hydrate.js to opportunistically fill in markup and injected code dependencies, or through a slower dynamic path which discovers these during the process of component instantiation. The statically rendered version of the page, hydrated using hydrate.js, where there are data dependencies in the real app such as the CSV files will be presented with placeholder versions of these, very short but valid datafiles with the same shape as the real ones, to allow the app to statically instantiate and discover all its code and asset dependencies. Also in scope is replacing the opportunistic build systems both in bagatelle and in howe-sound-mapping-2026 in favour of <fluid-import> tags which declare relative dependencies, and a simple system which inspects the set of imports demanded by in-place hydration and copies them out to local copies in subsidiary projects such as howe-sound-mapping-2026. Any kind of efficient bundling is out of scope for this work, for this round, the ultimate client will consume them as separate .vue files resolved by possibly recursive imports. A final helpful work package will be to enhance the SFC format operated in infusion-6 to include an SVG symbols block which will allow an SFC to advertise and export the symbols which are currently aggregated by hand at top level in the drivers. These will need new injection types within FluidView.js.

     ## Code style
     
      - Plain JavaScript with JSDocs
      - All strings double-quoted
      - No one-line if or else blocks - e.g. always use
     ```
        if (condition) {
        ...
        } else {
        ...
        }
     ```
       - Do not return early from functions, use long if instead.
       - If possible, first branch of if statement condition should not be negated.
       - JSDocs using @return, with capitalised built-ins, e.g. String, Number, Any, with [] for array syntax
       - Do not use Void return type
       - Assume an eslint environment, and begin all node.js files with
     ```
        /* eslint-env node */
        "use strict";
     ```
     
     ## Testing instructions
      - Run npm test in node to run virtually all view tests
      - A couple of view-specific tests (e.g. verifying that CSS rules have applied) require running in a real browser - run
     npm run test:browser-qunit to run the same test pages in headless Chromium, or pass it particular pages, e.g.
     tests/framework-tests/core/html/FluidViewTests.html
      - Run npm run test:browser to run the demo scripts listed in infusion.tests.browser of package.json
      - Run, e.g. node tests/test-core/qunit/js/fqunit-cli.js tests/framework-tests/core/html/FluidILTests.html to run a single test file
     
     ## Code workflow
      - Agents do not commit code, all updates reviewed by humans
      - Don't issue commands changing git state
     
     ## Commit messages
      - Mention issue closed in form FLUID-7003 (fluid-project/infusion-6#3) - this will be passed on as reminder. The FLUID ID is 7000 plus the GitHub issue number, and the parenthesised reference lets GitHub close the issue

     `$component`) and on [`fluid.cell`](/docs/fluid-signals) (signals, effects, source tracking).
     
     The raw markdown underlying these docs is available on [GitHub](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/amb26/ponder/refs/heads/main/content/docs/fluid-view.md),
     suitable for direct ingestion by your friendly local neighbourhood intelligence.

     14	
     15	## A first component
     16	
     17	A Single File Component is a `.vue` file holding a `<script>` defining one layer, a `<template>` holding its markup,
     18	and optionally `<style>`. Here is a complete counter, in a file named `my-counter.vue`:
     19	
     20	```html
     21	<script>
     22	fluid.def("my.counter", {
     23	    count: 0,
     24	    increment: {
     25	        $method: {
     26	            func: self => self.count++,
     27	            args: "{self}"
     28	        }
     29	    }
     30	});
     31	</script>
     32	
     33	<template>
     34	    <div class="counter">
     35	        <span>Clicked @{count} times</span>
     36	        <button @onclick="{self}.increment()">+1</button>
     37	    </div>
     38	</template>
     39	
     40	<style>
     41	.counter {
     42	    display: flex;
     43	    gap: 12px;
     44	}
     45	</style>
     46	```
     47	
     48	* `@{count}` in text or an attribute value binds live to the component's `count` member.

● Read /home/amb26/Source/gits/infusion-6/a-scratch/reports/requirements-imerss.md
  ⎿  1	# Requirements of the IMERSS visualisations on Infusion 6
     2	
     3	This report inventories the framework features used by the IMERSS biodiversity visualisations, so that they can be
     4	ported from Infusion 4 to Infusion 6. It records how each feature maps onto Infusion 6, and which gaps remain. Two
     5	code bases are covered:
     6	
     7	- **bagatelle** (imerss-bioinfo), in particular the BBEA driver `indexBeasBCBA.html` and its scripts
     8	  `src/client/js/new/fluidNew.js`, `imerss-new.js`, `filters.js`, `newChecklist.js`, `polygon-draw.js`,
     9	  `dual-range-input.js`, `imerss-bbea.js` and `src/client/js/autocomplete.js`. This is about 6,000 lines.
     10	- **howe-sound-mapping-2026**, whose local "reknitr" framework is the list of files in `copyFrameworkOut.sh`. Its
     11	  client runtime is `static/js/reknit-client.js`, `imerss-viz-reknit.js`, `paneHandlers.js` and `solowControls.js`,
     12	  about 2,500 lines. It also consumes the bagatelle bundles `imerss-viz-new-core.js`, `imerss-viz-new.js`,
     13	  `imerss-viz.js`, `imerss-blitz.js` and `imerss-plants.js` through its `copyJobs`. These add `taxonDisplay.js`,
     14	  `data-table.js`, `resize-bar.js` and the "standard" viz loader to the inventory.
     15	
     16	Each claim about Infusion 6 behaviour marked **(probed)** was checked by running a small script against the working
     17	tree at commit `fc1f099`. The probes are listed in the [appendix](#appendix-probes).
     18	
     19	## Starting point: a half-way house

● I've finished surveying, and I haven't changed anything in any repo yet. This is a multi-stage job, so I'd like you to confirm the order before I start writing code.
  
  **What I found:**
  - The first-pass port is in `indexBeasBCBA-6.html` plus `src/client/js/i6/*.js`, about 5,000 lines in 11 files. `indexBeasBCBA.html` itself still runs on Infusion 4. The i6 driver keeps all the markup in the page and finds its containers with `hortis.selectorContainerView` (gap G8 in the requirements report), which is the "static templating" you want to replace.
  - The i6 driver loads its scripts from `../fluid-infusion-6/`, but the checkout here is `../infusion-6`. I'll move this to `<fluid-module id="infusion-6">` paths.
  - `hydrate.js` already boots a page under node, waits for it to settle and writes it out. What's missing is a way to swap in placeholder data, and a record of which imports were resolved during hydration. The copy-out tool needs both.
  - `FluidModules.js` and the SFC loader already support `%module` paths and `<fluid-import>`, so the dependency side mostly exists.
  
  **Proposed order:**
  1. **BBEA as SFCs.** Split the i6 files into `src/client/sfc/*.vue`: one per filter, the checklist, the map, the shell pieces (concertina, tabs, grips) and each view. A `hortis-bea-viz-loader.vue` root template replaces the page markup, using `@id` in place of the selectors. The driver shrinks to a few `<fluid-import>` tags and a `fluid-layers` element.
  2. **Placeholder data and hydration.** Add short placeholder `.viz`/`.csv` files with the same shape as the real ones, and a way to point the loader at them when hydrating. `hydrate.js` then renders the page statically.
  3. **Dependency copy-out.** Hydration writes a manifest of the imports and assets it resolved. A small script copies them into a subsidiary project. This replaces `build.js` and `copyFrameworkOut.sh` in bagatelle and howe-sound.
  4. **The other drivers.** `indexBlitz.html` and `indexDiatoms.html`, then the bioreportr story map in howe-sound and saanich. These still need the standard loader, taxon display, data table and resize bars ported.
  5. **SVG symbols in SFCs.** Add a `<symbols>` block to the SFC format in infusion-6, with a new injection type in `FluidView.js` that pools the symbols into one `<svg><defs>` in the document. The hand-written symbol blocks in the drivers then go away.
  
  **Decision for you:**
  - **Order:** should I start on step 1 with BBEA? I'd check that it runs in Chromium and passes the existing 155 tests before moving on.
  - **Symbols:** should step 5 come first instead? The BBEA SFCs would then carry their own icons from the start, and I wouldn't port the hand-written symbol block and then undo it.

● The `<symbols>` support is written, but I haven't run any tests because I can't find `node` in my shell. What would you like to clarify about the Node setup?
  
  **What's in place in infusion-6 (untested):**
  - **The block:** an SFC can now have a top-level `<symbols>` block holding `<symbol>` elements. Its markup is taken verbatim from the SFC text, so the SVG survives intact.
  - **The injection type:** a new `"symbols"` variety in `FluidView.js`. Each SFC's block becomes a `<defs id="fl-symbols-<layer>-<n>">` inside one shared hidden `<svg id="fl-symbols-host">` at the start of `<body>`. The host is prepended rather than appended so that it stays ahead of anything a body template renders. An edit to the block updates the `<defs>` in place without re-running the SFC's script.
  - **Rendering:** both the host and the `<defs>` count as injected nodes, so re-rendering the body leaves them alone.
  - **Output documents:** these get the symbols as well as the styles.
  - **Tests:** the test SFC `fluid-tests-sfc-component.vue` now has a chevron symbol. `FluidViewSFCTests.js` has a new test checking that the host is created in the SVG namespace, the symbol can be found by id, its content is preserved, and an in-place edit works.
  
  The open question is whether linkedom parses `innerHTML` on an SVG element correctly when this runs under node. Running the suite will show that.

     * Resolve a path written in a Single File Component, e.g. the `src` of a `<script>`, `<style>` or `<fluid-import>`
     * block. A path beginning with a module reference `%module/`, or which is absolute, is returned unchanged. Any other
     * path is relative to the SFC itself, and is resolved against its URL, so that a set of SFCs and the files they
     * refer to may be moved together, e.g. by copying them into another project.
     * @param {String} [sfcUrl] - The absolute URL of the SFC. If it is not supplied, the path is returned unchanged
     * @param {String} path - The path to be resolved
     * @return {String} The resolved path
     */
    fluid.resolveSFCPath = function (sfcUrl, path) {
        return sfcUrl && !path.startsWith("%") && !fluid.isAbsolutePath(path) ? new URL(path, sfcUrl).href : path;
    };

    /**
     * Collect the imports declared by the top-level `<fluid-import src="..." [layer="..."]>` blocks of a Single File
     * Component, whose paths are resolved by `fluid.resolveSFCPath`. As for a `<fluid-import>` in a document, the
     * layer name defaults to the name of the imported file - see `fluid.pathToLayerName`.
     * @param {VNode} vTree - The parsed SFC
     * @param {String} [sfcUrl] - The absolute URL of the SFC
     * @return {Object<String, Object>} An import map, suitable for `fluid.loadImportMap`, keyed by layer name
     */
    fluid.sfcImportMap = function (vTree, sfcUrl) {
        const importMap = {};
        fluid.sfcBlocks(vTree, "fluid-import").forEach(node => {
            const path = fluid.resolveSFCPath(sfcUrl, node.attrs.src);
            const layerName = node.attrs.layer || fluid.pathToLayerName(path);
            if (!layerName) {
                fluid.log(fluid.logLevel.FAIL, "Error in SFC structure: couldn't determine layer name from import ", node);
            } else if (!fluid.importMap[layerName]) {
                importMap[layerName] = {path, node};
            }
        });
        return importMap;
    };

rep('''    /**
     * Bind injections from the specified SFC layer to the supplied document.''','''    /**
     * @typedef {Object} SharedScriptClaim
     * @property {String} layerName - The layer whose SFC first claimed the script
     * @property {Promise} done - A promise which resolves once the claiming SFC's injections have been committed
     * @property {Function} resolve - Resolves `done`
     */

    /** @type {WeakMap<Document, Map<String, SharedScriptClaim>>} */
    fluid.sharedScriptClaims = new WeakMap();

    /**
     * Arrange that a script referred to by its `src` from several Single File Components, e.g. a library such as a
     * map widget, or a file of utilities and base layers shared by a family of SFCs, is executed only once in a
     * document. The first SFC whose injections reach the script claims it, and injects it. Any other SFC refers to the
     * script as resolved through `fluid.resolveSFCPath` and `fluid.module.resolvePath`, so a script referred to by
     * different relative paths is still recognised, and omits it - instead committing its own injections only once
     * those of the claiming SFC are committed, so that its scripts may rely on the shared one having executed.
     * @param {Document} dokkument - The document into which injections are being made
     * @param {String} layerName - The layer whose SFC's injections are being made
     * @param {DocInjectionRecord[]} docInjRecs - The injections to be made
     * @return {Object} Members `docInjRecs`, the injections which are to be made, `claimed`, the claims made by this
     * SFC, to be resolved once its injections are committed, and `awaited`, promises for those of other SFCs
     */
    fluid.claimSharedScripts = function (dokkument, layerName, docInjRecs) {
        let claims = fluid.sharedScriptClaims.get(dokkument);
        if (!claims) {
            claims = new Map();
            fluid.sharedScriptClaims.set(dokkument, claims);
        }
        const claimed = [], awaited = [];
        const togo = docInjRecs.filter(docInjRec => {
            const {injRec} = docInjRec;
            let keep = true;
            if (injRec.variety === "script" && injRec.url) {
                const key = fluid.module.resolvePath(injRec.url);
                const existing = claims.get(key);
                if (existing && existing.layerName !== layerName) {
                    awaited.push(existing.done);
                    keep = false;
                } else if (!existing) {
                    let resolve;
                    const done = new Promise(resolveDone => resolve = resolveDone);
                    const claim = {layerName, done, resolve};
                    claims.set(key, claim);
                    claimed.push(claim);
                }
            }
            return keep;
        });
        return {docInjRecs: togo, claimed, awaited};
    };

    /**
     * Bind injections from the specified SFC layer to the supplied document.''')

p="imerss-core.js"
s=open(p).read()
start=s.index("/** Views **/")
end=s.index("/** DOM listeners **/")
new='''/** Views **/

// A slot rendering markup computed as a string, e.g. a long list for which a component per row would be too costly.
// The markup is rendered verbatim, so that it is not scanned for bindings - any events within it should be delegated
// to a handler on an enclosing element of a template. It is reconciled against the DOM as for any other template
fluid.def("hortis.verbatimSlot", {
    $layers: "fluid.component",
    markup: "",
    view: {
        $component: {
            $layers: "fluid.templateViewComponent",
            verbatim: true,
            template: "{$parent}.markup"
        }
    }
});

'''
s=s[:start]+new+s[end:]
open(p,"w").write(s)

<script src="../js/i6/imerss-core.js"></script>
<script src="../js/i6/filters.js"></script>
<script>
"use strict";

// Filters observations by the sex of the bee
fluid.def("hortis.sexFilter", {
    $layers: "hortis.obsFilter",
    // Bound two-way to the checkboxes in the template
    filterState: {
        $reactiveRoot: {
            male: false,
            female: false
        }
    },
    filterSummary: "$compute:hortis.sexFilter.summarise({self}.filterState)",
    doFilter: "$method:hortis.sexFilter.doFilter({0}:obsRows, {1}:filterState)",
    reset: "$method:hortis.sexFilter.reset({self})"
});

hortis.sexFilter.reset = function (that) {
    that.filterState = {male: false, female: false};
};

/**
 * Summarise the sex filter by the number of sexes selected.
 * @param {Object} filterState - The filter state, with Boolean members `male` and `female`
 * @return {FilterSummary} The summary of the filter
 */
hortis.sexFilter.summarise = function (filterState) {
    return hortis.countSummary((filterState.male ? 1 : 0) + (filterState.female ? 1 : 0), ["sex", "sexes"]);
};

hortis.sexFilter.doFilter = function (obsRows, filterState) {
    const all = !(filterState.female || filterState.male);
    return all ? obsRows : obsRows.filter(row => row.sex === "F" && filterState.female || row.sex === "M" && filterState.male);
};
</script>

<template>
    <div class="imerss-sex-filter mf-inline">
        <span class="mf-inline-label">Sex</span>

<script>
"use strict";

hortis.months = ["January", "February", "March", "April", "May", "June", "July", "August", "September", "October",
    "November", "December"];

// Filters observations by the month in which they were made
fluid.def("hortis.phenologyFilter", {
    $layers: "hortis.obsDrivenFilter",
    // One record per month - each month's row is a subcomponent whose checkbox is bound two-way to its record's
    // `checked`, which it writes through to this array since the $for source is sited
    filterState: {
        $reactiveRoot: hortis.months.map(month => ({month, checked: false}))
    },
    // Month of each observation, cached by row rather than written onto it
    monthCache: "$compute:hortis.phenologyFilter.monthCache({self}.obsRows)",
    filterSummary: "$compute:hortis.phenologyFilter.summarise({self}.filterState)",
    doFilter: "$method:hortis.phenologyFilter.doFilter({0}:obsRows, {1}:filterState, {self}.monthCache)",
    reset: "$method:hortis.phenologyFilter.reset({self})",
    monthRows: {
        $component: {
            $layers: "hortis.phenologyFilter.row",
            $for: {
                source: "{phenologyFilter}.filterState",
                valueAs: "range",
                keyAs: "index"
            }
        }
    }
});

/**
 * Compute the month of each observation.
 * @param {Object[]} obsRows - The observations, each with an `eventDate`
 * @return {Map<Object, Number>} Map of each observation row to its month, from 0 to 11
 */
hortis.phenologyFilter.monthCache = function (obsRows) {
    return new Map(obsRows.map(row => [row, new Date(row.eventDate).getMonth()]));
};

hortis.phenologyFilter.reset = function (that) {
    that.filterState = hortis.months.map(month => ({month, checked: false}));
};

/**
 * Summarise the phenology filter by the number of months selected.
 * @param {Object[]} filterState - The filter state, holding a record with Boolean member `checked` for each month
 * @return {FilterSummary} The summary of the filter
 */
hortis.phenologyFilter.summarise = function (filterState) {
    return hortis.countSummary(filterState.filter(range => range.checked).length, ["month", "months"]);
};

hortis.phenologyFilter.doFilter = function (obsRows, filterState, monthCache) {
    const selected = new Set(filterState.map((range, index) => range.checked ? index : -1).filter(index => index !== -1));
    return selected.size === 0 ? obsRows : obsRows.filter(row => selected.has(monthCache.get(row)));
};
</script>

<template>
    <div class="imerss-phenology-filter">
        <div class="imerss-filter-title">Phenology:</div>
        <div class="imerss-filter-body imerss-region-filter-rows" @id="monthRows"></div>
    </div>
</template>

/**
 * Move the selection between tabs with the arrow keys.
 * @param {KeyboardEvent} event - A keydown event within the tab list
 * @param {hortis.viewTabs} that - The tabs
 */
hortis.viewTabs.keyDown = function (event, that) {
    const step = event.key === "ArrowRight" ? 1 : event.key === "ArrowLeft" ? -1 : 0;
    const tab = event.target.closest(".mf-tab");
    if (step !== 0 && tab) {
        event.preventDefault();
        const tabs = [...event.currentTarget.querySelectorAll(".mf-tab")];
        const next = tabs[(tabs.indexOf(tab) + step + tabs.length) % tabs.length];
        that.selectedTab = next.dataset.tab;
        next.focus();
    }
};

/** Markup of the taxon lists **/

/**
 * Render the counts in a taxon list's bar.
 * @param {Boolean} active - `true` if the list's tab is selected - otherwise nothing is rendered
 * @param {Object[]} listRows - The rows of the list, as computed by `hortis.taxonListView.computeRows`
 * @param {String} noun - "bee" or "plant"
 * @return {String} The markup of the counts
 */
hortis.taxonListView.countMarkup = function (active, listRows, noun) {
    let togo = "";
    if (active) {
        // Totals count every observation, including those of intermediate taxa which have no row of their own
        const total = listRows.reduce((sum, listRow) => sum + listRow.count, 0);
        const shownCount = listRows.filter(listRow => listRow.listed).length;
        togo = `<span title="Number of distinct ${noun} taxa listed - species, or coarser where nothing more specific was recorded">${hortis.plural(shownCount, "taxon", "taxa")}</span>` +
            ` &middot; <span title="Number of observation records in the current selection, including those identified only to genus or subgenus">${hortis.plural(total, "observation")}</span>`;
    }
    return togo;
};

/**
 * Render the body of a taxon list.
 * @param {Boolean} active - `true` if the list's tab is selected - otherwise nothing is rendered
 * @param {String} arrange - "family" to arrange the list by family, or "flat" to list it alphabetically
 * @param {Object[]} listRows - The rows of the list, as computed by `hortis.taxonListView.computeRows`
 * @param {String} noun - "bee" or "plant"
 * @param {Boolean} colourByFamily - Whether family headings carry a colour chip
 * @return {String} The markup of the list
 */
hortis.taxonListView.bodyMarkup = function (active, arrange, listRows, noun, colourByFamily) {
    let togo = "";
    if (active) {
        const listed = rows => rows.filter(listRow => listRow.listed);
        let markup;
        if (listRows.length === 0) {
            markup = `<p class="mf-empty">No ${noun}s match the current filters and selections.</p>`;
        } else if (arrange === "family") {
            markup = hortis.taxonListView.byFamily(listRows).map(family => {
                const familyRows = listed(family.rows);
                const colour = hortis.pollColours.family[family.family];
                const chip = colourByFamily ? `<b style="background: ${colour || "#999"}"></b>` : "";
                const tip = `${hortis.plural(familyRows.length, noun + " taxon", noun + " taxa")} listed, with ${hortis.plural(family.count, "observation")} in ${family.family}`;
                return `<div class="mf-famhead">${chip}<span>${hortis.encodeHTML(family.family)}</span><i title="${tip}">${hortis.plural(familyRows.length, "taxon", "taxa")}</i></div>` +
                    familyRows.map(listRow => hortis.taxonListView.rowMarkup(listRow, noun)).join("");
            }).join("");
        } else {
            markup = listed(listRows).sort((a, b) => a.label.localeCompare(b.label))
                .map(listRow => hortis.taxonListView.rowMarkup(listRow, noun)).join("");
        }
        togo = `<div class="mf-taxa">${markup}</div>`;
    }
    return togo;
};

hortis.taxonListView.arrangeOn = arrange => ({family: arrange === "family", flat: arrange === "flat"});

/**
 * Show a tooltip for the taxon whose name is under the pointer, if any.
 * @param {Event} event - A mouse event within the list
 * @param {hortis.taxonListView} that - The list
 */
hortis.taxonListView.hover = function (event, that) {
    const name = event.type === "mouseleave" ? null : event.target.closest?.(".mf-taxon-name");
    that.hoverAt(name ? name.dataset.rowId : null, event);
};

/** Markup of bee abundance **/

hortis.beeAbundance.colourOf = row => hortis.pollColours.family[row.family] || "#999";

/**
 * Render the key of family colours above the bee abundance charts.
 * @param {Boolean} active - `true` if the view's tab is selected - otherwise nothing is rendered
 * @param {Object} abundance - The abundance of bees, as computed by `hortis.beeAbundance.compute`
 * @return {String} The markup of the key
 */
hortis.beeAbundance.keyMarkup = function (active, abundance) {
    return active ? abundance.family.map(row =>
        `<span><b style="background: ${hortis.beeAbundance.colourOf(row)}"></b><span>${hortis.encodeHTML(row.label)}</span></span>`).join("") : "";
};

/**
 * Render the bee abundance charts.
 * @param {hortis.beeAbundance} that - The view, holding its chart configuration
 * @param {Boolean} active - `true` if the view's tab is selected - otherwise nothing is rendered
 * @param {Number} width - The width available to the charts
 * @param {Object} abundance - The abundance of bees, as computed by `hortis.beeAbundance.compute`
 * @return {String} The markup of the charts
 */
hortis.beeAbundance.chartsMarkup = function (that, active, width, abundance) {
    let togo = "";
    if (active) {
        const limits = that.chartLimits;
        const chart = (key, plural, foot, angle) => {
            const all = abundance[key];
            const rows = all.slice(0, limits[key]);
            // Fill the pane, but don't spread a few bars too thinly, nor squeeze many bars below their minimum width
            const chartWidth = Math.max(Math.min(Math.floor(width), 70 + rows.length * that.maxBand), 70 + rows.length * that.minBand);
            const shown = rows.length < all.length ? `top ${rows.length} of ${all.length}` : `${all.length} total`;
            return hortis.barChartMarkup(rows, {
                width: chartWidth,
                height: 150 + foot,
                foot,
                angle,
                title: `Bee ${plural} (${shown})`,
                titleTip: `Number of distinct bee ${plural} in the current selection` +
                    (rows.length < all.length ? `, of which the ${rows.length} most observed are shown` : ""),
                xLabel: hortis.capitalize(key),
                xTip: `Bee ${plural}, coloured by family and ordered by number of observations`,
                yLabel: "Observations",
                yTip: "Number of observation records in the current selection",
                colourOf: hortis.beeAbundance.colourOf,
                rowTip: row => `${row.label} (${row.family}): ${hortis.plural(row.count, "observation")}`
            });
        };
        togo = abundance.family.length === 0 ? "<p class=\\"mf-empty\\">No bees match the current filters and selections.</p>" :
            chart("family", "families", 110, -40) + chart("genus", "genera", 120, -45) + chart("species", "species", 190, -55);
    }
    return togo;
};

/** Markup of the seed mix evaluator **/

hortis.seedMix.keySet = hash => new Set(Object.keys(hash));

/**
 * Describe how the seed mix evaluator treats the site.
 * @param {Set<String>} established - The ids of the plants established on the site
 * @return {String} The description
 */
hortis.seedMix.note = function (established) {
    return established.size > 0 ?
        "Plants recorded under the current filters are treated as already established on the site, and start ticked - " +
        "untick any which will be removed. Tick further plants to model a seed mix." :
        "No site is defined. Use the Region filter, draw a polygon on the map or click a map cell to define one, " +
        "and plants recorded there will be listed as already established. Meanwhile, tick plants to model a seed mix.";
};

/**
 * Render the list of plants which may be ticked into the seed mix.
 * @param {hortis.seedMix} that - The evaluator
 * @param {Boolean} active - `true` if the view's tab is selected - otherwise nothing is rendered
 * @param {Object} network - The plant-pollinator network, as computed by `hortis.seedMix.computeNetwork`
 * @param {Set<String>} established - The ids of the plants established on the site
 * @param {String} query - The contents of the search box
 * @param {Boolean} showAll - `true` if every candidate plant is to be listed
 * @return {String} The markup of the list
 */
hortis.seedMix.listMarkup = function (that, active, network, established, query, showAll) {
    let markup = "";
    if (active) {
        // Read the user's ticks without depending on them, so that ticking a plant doesn't rerender the list beneath the
        // pointer - the list is rerendered with them when it is reset, since listVersion is one of our arguments
        const {removed, added} = fluid.cell.untracked(() => ({removed: hortis.seedMix.keySet(that.removed), added: hortis.seedMix.keySet(that.added)}));
        const words = hortis.queryWords(query);
        const matches = plant => words.every(word => plant.label.toLowerCase().includes(word));
        const byBees = (a, b) => b.bees.size - a.bees.size || a.label.localeCompare(b.label);
        const establishedPlants = [...established].map(id => network.plants.get(id)).filter(plant => plant && matches(plant)).sort(byBees);
        const candidates = [...network.plants.values()].filter(plant => !established.has(plant.id) && matches(plant)).sort(byBees);
        const limit = showAll || words.length > 0 ? candidates.length : that.shortListLength;
        const groupHead = (title, tip) => `<p class="mf-seedgroup" title="${tip}">${title}</p>`;
        if (establishedPlants.length > 0) {
            markup += groupHead(`Already established on site (${establishedPlants.length})`,
                `${hortis.plural(establishedPlants.length, "plant species", "plant species")} recorded under the current filters`) +
                `<div class="mf-taxa mf-taxa-cols">${establishedPlants.map(plant => hortis.seedMix.plantMarkup(plant, !removed.has(plant.id))).join("")}</div>`;
        }
        markup += groupHead(`Available for seed mixes (${candidates.length})`,
            `${hortis.plural(candidates.length, "further plant species", "further plant species")} recorded in the dataset, ordered by the number of bee species visiting them`) +
            `<div class="mf-taxa mf-taxa-cols">${candidates.slice(0, limit).map(plant => hortis.seedMix.plantMarkup(plant, added.has(plant.id))).join("")}</div>`;
        if (limit < candidates.length) {
            markup += `<button type="button" class="mf-linkbtn imerss-seed-more">Show all ${hortis.formatInt(candidates.length)} plants</button>`;
        }
    }
    return markup;
};

/**
 * Evaluate the habitat provided by the seed mix.
 * @param {Boolean} active - `true` if the view's tab is selected - otherwise nothing is rendered
 * @param {Object} network - The plant-pollinator network, as computed by `hortis.seedMix.computeNetwork`
 * @param {Set<String>} established - The ids of the plants established on the site
 * @param {Object<String, Boolean>} removedHash - The established plants which the user has unticked
 * @param {Object<String, Boolean>} addedHash - The further plants which the user has ticked
 * @return {Object} Members `share`, the percentage of the dataset's bee species supported, `meterTitle`, describing it,
 * and `readMarkup` and `chartMarkup`, the markup of the readout and the chart of support by bee family
 */
hortis.seedMix.output = function (active, network, established, removedHash, addedHash) {
    let togo = {share: 0, meterTitle: null, readMarkup: "", chartMarkup: ""};
    if (active) {
        const mix = hortis.seedMix.mix(established, hortis.seedMix.keySet(removedHash), hortis.seedMix.keySet(addedHash));
        const supported = new Set();
        mix.forEach(id => network.plants.get(id)?.bees.forEach(bee => supported.add(bee)));
        const all = network.beeFamily.size;
        const share = all > 0 ? Math.round(supported.size / all * 100) : 0;
        const totals = new Map();
        network.beeFamily.forEach(family => totals.set(family, (totals.get(family) || 0) + 1));
        const reached = new Map();
        supported.forEach(bee => {
            const family = network.beeFamily.get(bee);
            reached.set(family, (reached.get(family) || 0) + 1);
        });
        const families = [...totals.keys()].sort((a, b) => totals.get(b) - totals.get(a));
        togo = {
            share,
            meterTitle: `${share}% of the bee species recorded on plants in this dataset visit a plant in the mix`,
            readMarkup: `<b title="Bee species recorded visiting at least one plant in the mix">${hortis.formatInt(supported.size)}</b> of ` +
                `<span title="All bee species recorded visiting plants anywhere in this dataset">${hortis.formatInt(all)}</span> bee species supported` +
                ` &mdash; <span title="Share of the dataset's bee species supported by the mix">${share}%</span>` +
                `<br/><span title="Number of plant species currently ticked">${hortis.plural(mix.size, "plant species", "plant species")} in the mix</span>`,
            chartMarkup: hortis.seedMix.familyChart(families, totals, reached)
        };
    }
    return togo;
};

/**
 * Respond to a change within the seed mix evaluator - a plant being ticked or unticked.
 * @param {Event} event - The change event
 * @param {hortis.seedMix} that - The evaluator
 */
hortis.seedMix.change = function (event, that) {
    const input = event.target.closest("input[data-seed]");
    if (input) {
        const id = input.dataset.seed;
        if (that.established.has(id)) {
            that.removed = hortis.seedMix.updateHash(that.removed, id, !input.checked);
        } else {
            that.added = hortis.seedMix.updateHash(that.added, id, input.checked);
        }
    }
};

/**
 * Respond to a click within the seed mix evaluator - on the buttons showing every plant or resetting the mix.
 * @param {Event} event - The click event
 * @param {hortis.seedMix} that - The evaluator
 */
hortis.seedMix.click = function (event, that) {
    if (event.target.closest(".imerss-seed-more")) {
        that.showAll = true;
    } else if (event.target.closest(".imerss-seed-reset")) {
        that.removed = {};
        that.added = {};
        that.listVersion = that.listVersion + 1;
        // The list's markup may be unchanged by the reset, and so not rerendered - restore the ticks the user has changed
        event.currentTarget.querySelectorAll("input[data-seed]").forEach(input => {
            input.checked = that.established.has(input.dataset.seed);
        });
    }
};
'''

<script>
"use strict";

// Reports how many observations survive the filters and selections
fluid.def("hortis.recordReporter", {
    $layers: "fluid.component",
    // filteredRows: Object[]
    // allRows: Object[]
    counts: "$compute:hortis.recordReporter.renderModel({self}.filteredRows, {self}.allRows)"
});

hortis.recordReporter.renderModel = function (filteredRows, allRows) {
    return {
        filteredRows: hortis.formatInt(filteredRows.length),
        allRows: hortis.formatInt(allRows.length)
    };
};
</script>

<template>
    <div class="mf-reporter imerss-record-reporter">
        <p>Displaying <b title="Observation records matching every filter and the current bee and plant selections">@{counts.filteredRows}</b>
            of <span title="Total number of observation records in this dataset">@{counts.allRows}</span> records</p>
    </div>
</template>

QUnit.test("Event assignment to a path passing through a subcomponent writes into the subcomponent", function (assert) {
    const container = qs(".container");
    const that = fluid.tests.assignThroughSubcomponent({container});
    fluid.cell.stabilize();
    const click = selector => {
        qs(selector, container).dispatchEvent(new MouseEvent("click", {bubbles: true}));
        fluid.cell.stabilize();
    };
    click(".show");
    assert.equal(that.panel.shown, true, "Assignment written into the subcomponent");
    assert.equal(qs(".shown", container).textContent, "true", "Binding to the subcomponent's member updated");
    click(".toggle");
    assert.equal(that.panel.shown, false, "Negated assignment through the subcomponent toggles its member");
    click(".own");
    assert.equal(that.open, true, "Assignment to a member of the component itself is unaffected");
    click(".colour");
    assert.equal(that.state.colour, "crimson", "Assignment beneath a reactive root is unaffected");
    that.destroy();
});

/**

 * `fluid-client`, e.g. a widget library. The script is written into the document as a link to its source, as the
 * browser would load it, but is not evaluated.

 * @param {InjectRecord} injRec - The injection record
 * @param {Object} material - The injection's material, whose `sourceUrl` is the script's URL

    fresh.setAttribute("fluid-client", "");
    fresh.id = injRec.nodeId;

    extra="".join("        "+l.strip()+"\n" for l in re.findall(r'<script src="\.\./js/[^"]*"></script>',s))
    open("html/"+f,"w").write(head_tmpl.replace("%TITLE%",title).replace("%FILE%",f).replace("%EXTRA%",extra))
EOF

● SVG symbols and step 1 are both done. The BCBA page (`indexBeasBCBA-6.html`) now builds itself from SFCs, and everything I clicked through in headless Chrome behaves as before the conversion. Nothing is committed.
  
  **Symbols (step 5), in infusion-6**
  - An SFC can carry a `<symbols>` block. Its symbols are injected into one hidden `<svg>` at the start of the page body, and editing the block updates them in place.
  - The page's hand-written symbol block is gone. Each component's SFC carries its own icons, and icons used by several components live in a small shared layer, `hortis.mfIcons`.
  - Four symbols in the old page (`filter-reset`, `copy-clipboard`, `copy-check`, `download`) weren't used by the new code, so I dropped them.
  
  **BBEA as SFCs (step 1), in bagatelle**
  - 23 SFCs in `src/client/sfc/`. The page imports only `hortis-beaVizLoader.vue`, whose template is now the whole page markup, and defines a three-line config layer for its data files.
  - Each SFC declares the SFCs it needs and the scripts and stylesheets it uses, all with relative paths (including into `node_modules`).
  - Logic shared by several components stays in `src/client/js/i6/*.js` and is pulled in by the SFCs that need it.
  - The selector-based containers are gone: components render into `@id` slots. The concertina, tabs, grips and full screen are bound in templates instead of being patched by hand.
  - Lists, abundance charts and the seed mix used to write `innerHTML` into elements; they now build markup as computed values.
  - The filters and checklists now sit directly under the loader instead of under `obsFilters`. So the BCBA override is now `regionFilter: {$component: {leadingFields: [...]}}`.
  
  **Framework changes in infusion-6**, each with tests:
  - A relative path inside an SFC resolves against the SFC itself, and an SFC can import other SFCs with `<fluid-import>`.
  - A script listed by several SFCs, such as maplibre, runs once per page.
  - `<script fluid-client>` in an SFC marks browser-only libraries, which aren't run under node. Step 2 will rely on this.
  - An event assignment such as `{self}.shell.fullScreen = true` now writes into the subcomponent. Before, it silently wrote the value onto the parent.
  - The docs in `ponder/content/docs/fluid-view.md` are updated.
  
  **Tests**
  - infusion-6: all 2,166 tests pass under node, and the view and SFC pages pass in Chrome.
  - bagatelle: all 155 tests pass under node, the same count as before the conversion. The core and views suites also pass in Chrome.
  - The map suite fails in Chrome. Real browser layout errors break it, and the test's fake map library isn't being used there. I left it, since it was written for node.
  
  **Decision for you:** when a template's root is merged onto its `@id` element, the template's `class` replaces the element's class rather than merging with it. No CSS was affected, and I worked around it by putting the classes in the templates. Should infusion-6 merge the classes instead?

    /**
     * Determine which of the writers of an element's classes a VNode is - see `fluid.applyClassTokens`
     * @param {VNode} vnode - The VNode
     * @return {String} "root" if the VNode is the root of a template rendered onto the element, otherwise "joint"
     */
    fluid.classWriterOf = vnode => vnode.renderedAsRoot ? "root" : "joint";

    /**
     * Write the classes which one writer contributes to an element's class attribute. An element serving as the
     * container of a view whose template's root is elided onto it is written by two templates - its own as the
     * element bearing @id in its parent's template, and the template rendered into it. Either may re-render without
     * the other, in either order, so rather than each writing the whole attribute, each contributes a set of classes,
     * and the attribute holds their union. A writer removes only those of its classes which it no longer writes, and
     * which no other writer holds. Classes written by no template, e.g. added by a widget, are kept, ahead of the
     * written ones, which follow in the order of `fluid.classWriters` - so the attribute is the same whatever the
     * order in which the writers rendered.
     * An element claimed from existing markup, e.g. rendered by a static build, records no writers - its classes are
     * taken to have been written by the templates which are about to render it, and so are dropped once any writer
     * writes, unless written again.
     * @param {Element} element - The element
     * @param {String} writer - The writer, one of `fluid.classWriters`
     * @param {String|null|undefined} text - The classes the writer contributes, separated by whitespace - none if absent
     */
    fluid.applyClassTokens = function (element, writer, text) {
        const tokens = value => (value ?? "").split(/\\s+/).filter(token => token);
        let writers = element.flClassWriters;
        const current = tokens(element.getAttribute("class"));
        if (!writers) {
            // Whatever the element holds before any writer has written was written by them, e.g. in a static build
            writers = element.flClassWriters = {claimed: new Set(current)};
        }
        delete writers.claimed;
        writers[writer] = new Set(tokens(text));
        const written = new Set(fluid.classWriters.flatMap(oneWriter => [...(writers[oneWriter] ?? [])]));
        const previous = element.flClassWritten ?? new Set();
        // Classes neither written now nor previously by any writer were added by some other agent
        const foreign = current.filter(token => !written.has(token) && !previous.has(token) && !element.flClassClaimed?.has(token));
        const updated = [...new Set([...foreign, ...written])].join(" ");
        element.flClassWritten = written;
        element.flClassClaimed = element.flClassClaimed ?? new Set(current.filter(() => element.flClassWritten === written && !previous.size));
        if (updated === "") {
            if (element.hasAttribute("class")) {
                element.removeAttribute("class");
            }
        } else if (element.getAttribute("class") !== updated) {
            element.setAttribute("class", updated);
        }
    };

// Merging of the classes of a container written both by the element bearing @id in its parent's template, and by the
// root of its own template elided onto it - either may re-render without the other, in either order

fluid.tests.classMerge = {
    parentTemplate: variant => `<div class="wrap"><span @id="child" class="slot slot-${variant}" @class="p-on:@{pOn}"></span><i>${variant}</i></div>`,
    childTemplate: variant => `<span class="kid kid-${variant}" @class="c-on:@{cOn}">${variant}</span>`
};

fluid.def("fluid.tests.classMerge", {
    $layers: "fluid.component",
    variant: "a",
    pOn: false,
    child: {
        $component: {
            $layers: "fluid.component",
            variant: "a",
            cOn: false,
            view: {
                $component: {
                    $layers: "fluid.templateViewComponent",
                    template: "$compute:fluid.tests.classMerge.childTemplate({$parent}.variant)"
                }
            }
        }
    },
    view: {
        $component: {
            $layers: "fluid.templateViewComponent",
            template: "$compute:fluid.tests.classMerge.parentTemplate({$parent}.variant)"
        }
    }
});

/**
 * Render a fresh instance in a given state, and report the class attributes of its elements
 * @param {Object} state - Members `variant`, `pOn`, and `child`, holding `variant` and `cOn`
 * @return {Object} Members `slot` and `wrap`, the class attributes of the container of the child and of the root
 */
fluid.tests.classMerge.freshClasses = function (state) {
    const container = document.createElement("div");
    qs(".container").appendChild(container);
    const that = fluid.tests.classMerge({container, variant: state.variant, pOn: state.pOn,
        child: {$component: {variant: state.child.variant, cOn: state.child.cOn}}});
    fluid.cell.stabilize();
    const togo = {slot: qs(".slot", container).getAttribute("class"), wrap: container.getAttribute("class")};
    that.destroy();
    container.remove();
    return togo;
};

QUnit.test("Classes of a container are merged from its parent's template and its own, in any order of rendering", function (assert) {
    const container = qs(".container");
    const that = fluid.tests.classMerge({container});
    fluid.cell.stabilize();
    const slot = () => qs(".slot", container);
    const slotClass = () => slot().getAttribute("class");
    assert.equal(slotClass(), "slot slot-a kid kid-a", "Classes of the parent's template and the child's root merged");
    assert.equal(container.getAttribute("class"), "container wrap", "Container's own class kept beside its template root's");
    const element = slot();

    that.variant = "b";
    fluid.cell.stabilize();
    assert.equal(slotClass(), "slot slot-b kid kid-a", "Parent re-rendering alone keeps the child's classes");
    assert.equal(slot(), element, "Container element kept");

    that.child.variant = "b";
    fluid.cell.stabilize();
    assert.equal(slotClass(), "slot slot-b kid kid-b", "Child re-rendering alone keeps the parent's classes");

    that.pOn = true;
    fluid.cell.stabilize();
    assert.equal(slotClass(), "slot slot-b p-on kid kid-b", "Bound class of the parent's template merged");
    that.child.cOn = true;
    fluid.cell.stabilize();
    assert.equal(slotClass(), "slot slot-b p-on kid kid-b c-on", "Bound class of the child's root merged");

    slot().classList.add("widget");
    that.variant = "c";
    that.child.variant = "c";
    fluid.cell.stabilize();
    assert.equal(slotClass(), "widget slot slot-c p-on kid kid-c c-on", "Class added by another agent kept through re-rendering of both");

    that.pOn = false;
    fluid.cell.stabilize();
    that.child.cOn = false;
    that.variant = "d";
    fluid.cell.stabilize();
    assert.equal(slotClass(), "widget slot slot-d kid kid-c", "Classes no longer written are removed, and others kept");
    assert.equal(slot(), element, "Container element kept throughout");

    // The same final state reached by the opposite order of changes
    const other = document.createElement("div");
    container.appendChild(other);
    const reversed = fluid.tests.classMerge({container: other});
    fluid.cell.stabilize();
    reversed.child.cOn = true;
    reversed.child.variant = "c";
    fluid.cell.stabilize();
    reversed.pOn = true;
    reversed.variant = "d";
    fluid.cell.stabilize();
    reversed.child.cOn = false;
    fluid.cell.stabilize();
    reversed.pOn = false;
    fluid.cell.stabilize();
    assert.equal(qs(".slot", other).getAttribute("class"), "slot slot-d kid kid-c", "Opposite order of re-rendering gives the same classes");
    reversed.destroy();
    other.remove();

    const fresh = fluid.tests.classMerge.freshClasses({variant: "d", pOn: false, child: {variant: "c", cOn: false}});
    assert.equal(fresh.slot, "slot slot-d kid kid-c", "A fresh rendering in the same state gives the same classes");
    that.destroy();
});

QUnit.test("Classes of claimed markup from an earlier rendering are rewritten, dropping any no longer written", function (assert) {
    const container = qs(".container");
    const first = fluid.tests.classMerge({container, pOn: true, child: {$component: {cOn: true}}});
    fluid.cell.stabilize();
    const markup = container.innerHTML;
    first.destroy();
    assert.ok(markup.includes("class=\"slot slot-a p-on kid kid-a c-on\""), "Earlier rendering holds the bound classes");

    // As for a page written by a static build, then booted in a state in which the bound classes are off
    const host = document.createElement("div");
    host.setAttribute("class", "host");
    host.innerHTML = markup;
    container.appendChild(host);
    const staticSlot = qs(".slot", host);
    const that = fluid.tests.classMerge({container: host});
    fluid.cell.stabilize();
    assert.equal(qs(".slot", host), staticSlot, "Container of the child claimed from the markup");
    assert.equal(staticSlot.getAttribute("class"), "slot slot-a kid kid-a", "Classes no longer written dropped from claimed markup");
    assert.equal(host.getAttribute("class"), "host wrap", "Own class of a container appearing in no template kept");
    that.child.variant = "b";
    fluid.cell.stabilize();
    assert.equal(staticSlot.getAttribute("class"), "slot slot-a kid kid-b", "Claimed container merges thereafter");
    that.destroy();
    host.remove();
});

     /**
      * Removes a leading slash from a Windows-style drive path.
      * For example, "/E:/things" becomes "E:/things".
      * Other paths remain unchanged.
      *
      * @param {String} path - The path to normalize
      * @return {String} - The normalized path
      */
     const deDrivePath = function(path) {
         return path.replace(/^\/([a-zA-Z]:)/, "$1");
     };
     
     module.exports = async function fetchWrapper(url, options) {
         const parsedUrl = new URL(url);
     
         if (parsedUrl.protocol === "file:") {
             const filePath = deDrivePath(decodeURIComponent(parsedUrl.pathname));
     
             if (!fs.existsSync(filePath)) {
                 return new Response(null, {
                     status: 404,
                     statusText: "NOT FOUND"
                 });
             }
     
             // Construct a readable stream – valid Response body type in node-fetch@2
             const stream = fs.createReadStream(filePath);
     
             return new Response(stream, {
                 status: 200,
                 statusText: "OK"
                 // node-fetch@2 doesn't support explicit `url` here, but we can set it after
             });
         } else {
             // Normal HTTP fetch
             return fetch(url, options);
         }

s=s.replace(a,'''/**
 * Resolve a URL fetched under node as a browser would - a relative URL is resolved against the location of the
 * document most recently booted by `fluid.loadAndBootDocument`, and is then subject to any placeholder substituted for
 * it - see `fluid.acquirePlaceholders`
 * @param {String|URL} url - The URL to be fetched
 * @return {String} The absolute URL to be fetched
 */
fluid.resolveServerFetchUrl = function (url) {
    const absolute = fluid.serverFetchBase ? new URL(url, fluid.serverFetchBase).href : String(url);
    const placeholder = fluid.placeholderUrls[absolute];
    if (placeholder) {
        fluid.log("Fetching placeholder " + placeholder + " in place of " + absolute);
    }
    return placeholder ?? absolute;
};

// The document against which relative URLs fetched under node are resolved - see fluid.resolveServerFetchUrl
fluid.serverFetchBase = null;

// Map of absolute URL to the absolute URL of a placeholder fetched in its place under node - see fluid.acquirePlaceholders
fluid.placeholderUrls = {};

/**
 * Acquire the placeholders declared in a document by `<fluid-placeholder for="..." src="...">` elements. When the
 * document is rendered under node, e.g. statically by hydrate.js, data fetched from the URL `for` is instead fetched
 * from `src`, a short file of the same shape - so that the document's components can be instantiated, and their code
 * and markup discovered and rendered, without loading data which is only of interest to a live page. In the browser,
 * the elements have no effect. Both URLs are relative to the document.
 * @param {Document} dokkument - The document
 */
fluid.acquirePlaceholders = function (dokkument) {
    dokkument.querySelectorAll("fluid-placeholder").forEach(node => {
        const forUrl = new URL(node.getAttribute("for"), dokkument.location).href;
        fluid.placeholderUrls[forUrl] = new URL(node.getAttribute("src"), dokkument.location).href;
    });
};

fluid.loadAndBootDocument = function (filename) {
    const text = fluid.readTextFile(filename);

    const dokkument = fluid.serverDocumentParser(text);
    dokkument.location = new URL("file://" + filename);
    fluid.serverFetchBase = dokkument.location;
    fluid.acquirePlaceholders(dokkument);
''')
open(p,"w").write(s)

# relativeUrl + markup adoption helpers, placed before hostEvaluatesClientScripts
('''    /**
     * Determine whether the host evaluates scripts which are payload for the browser alone, bearing `fluid-client`. A''','''    /**
     * Express a URL relative to a base URL, e.g. that of a document, if they share an origin - so that a document
     * written to a file, e.g. by a static build, refers to its resources wherever it is served from
     * @param {String|URL} base - The base URL
     * @param {String} target - The URL to be expressed, which may itself be relative to the base
     * @return {String} The relative URL, or the absolute URL if the two have different origins
     */
    fluid.relativeUrl = function (base, target) {
        const baseUrl = new URL(base);
        const targetUrl = new URL(target, baseUrl);
        let togo;
        if (baseUrl.protocol === targetUrl.protocol && baseUrl.host === targetUrl.host) {
            const baseSegs = baseUrl.pathname.split("/").slice(0, -1);
            const targetSegs = targetUrl.pathname.split("/");
            let common = 0;
            while (common < baseSegs.length && common < targetSegs.length - 1 && baseSegs[common] === targetSegs[common]) {
                ++common;
            }
            togo = [...new Array(baseSegs.length - common).fill(".."), ...targetSegs.slice(common)].join("/") + targetUrl.search + targetUrl.hash;
        } else {
            togo = targetUrl.href;
        }
        return togo;
    };

    /**
     * Determine whether the host runs the scripts held in a document's markup as it loads, as a browser does. A
     * document rendered by a static build holds the scripts injected for its Single File Components - where the host
     * has run them, they are adopted rather than injected afresh - see `fluid.adoptMarkupInjections`. A host which
     * does not, e.g. node, declares so by supplying `fluidHost.runsMarkupScripts: false` in its global object
     * @return {Boolean} `true` if scripts in markup have been run
     */
    fluid.hostRunsMarkupScripts = function () {
        return fluid.global.fluidHost?.runsMarkupScripts ?? true;
    };

    /**
     * Find the script in a document's markup, written by a static build, which was injected from a given source - see
     * `fluid-src` as written by the injection styles
     * @param {Document} dokkument - The document
     * @param {String} url - The absolute URL of the script's source
     * @return {Element|undefined} The script element, if it is present and has not been injected by this session
     */
    fluid.markupScriptFrom = function (dokkument, url) {
        const location = fluid.documentLocation(dokkument);
        return [...dokkument.querySelectorAll("script[fluid-src]")].find(node => !node.flInjected &&
            new URL(node.getAttribute("fluid-src"), location).href === new URL(url, location).href);
    };

    /**
     * Adopt the injections of a Single File Component which a document's markup already holds, e.g. as written by a
     * static build of the document, rather than injecting them afresh - so that a script is not run a second time, nor
     * a stylesheet loaded again. Styles and symbols are always adopted. Scripts are adopted only where the host has run
     * those in the markup - see `fluid.hostRunsMarkupScripts`. An adopted injection is taken to be the one its record
     * describes, since the document was rendered from the same SFC - should the SFC change, it is injected afresh.
     * @param {Document} dokkument - The document
     * @param {Object<String, InjectRecord>} injRecs - The injection records of the SFC
     * @return {Object<String, InjectRecord>} The records adopted, keyed by node id
     */
    fluid.adoptMarkupInjections = function (dokkument, injRecs) {
        const adopted = {};
        Object.values(injRecs).forEach(injRec => {
            const node = dokkument.getElementById(injRec.nodeId);
            if (node && !node.flInjected && (injRec.variety !== "script" || fluid.hostRunsMarkupScripts())) {
                node.flInjected = true;
                adopted[injRec.nodeId] = injRec;
            }
        });
        return adopted;
    };

        // The I/O is the work of a computation returning a promise, so that the cell is pending within the reactive
        // graph until it completes, and fluid.cell.settle waits for it - e.g. before a document rendered under node is
        // written. It begins once the cell is first read
        const load = async function () {
            let togo;
            try {
                const response = await fetch(url, {...options, ...fluid.cacheOptions});
                if (!response.ok) {
                    togo = fluid.unavailable({message: `HTTP error ${response.status} for URL ${url}`, variety: "error"});
                } else {

                    }

            return togo;

QUnit.test("Attributes written by other agents survive re-rendering, whilst those a template ceases to write are removed", function (assert) {
    const container = qs(".container");
    const that = fluid.tests.foreignAttrs({container});
    fluid.cell.stabilize();
    const input = qs(".field", container);
    // As a widget might mark an element of the template
    input.setAttribute("data-ready", "true");
    that.variant = "b";
    fluid.cell.stabilize();
    assert.equal(qs(".field", container), input, "Element reused on re-rendering");
    assert.equal(input.getAttribute("data-ready"), "true", "Attribute written by another agent survives re-rendering");
    assert.notOk(input.hasAttribute("title"), "Attribute the template no longer writes is removed");
    assert.equal(input.getAttribute("data-variant"), "b", "Attribute the template writes is updated");
    that.destroy();
});

● Classes now merge, and step 2 is done. The BBEA page and a smaller test page each render the same whether booted from the minimal page or from the static one `hydrate.js` writes. Nothing is committed.
  
  ## Class merging and the race
  
  The race you saw is real, and it was wider than classes:
  - **The original race:** a container element had up to three writers of its `class`: the parent template's `@id` element, the child template's root, and any `@class` binding. Each replaced the whole attribute, so a parent re-rendering alone wiped out the child's classes.
  - **Interpolated classes:** a bound `class="x @{y}"` was a fourth whole-attribute writer.
  - **Other attributes:** an ordinary template element removed every attribute it didn't write, including ones a widget had set. The dual range widget's `data-ready` turned up or not depending on timing, and the BBEA round trip caught it.
  
  Each writer now contributes its own set of classes, and the attribute holds their union. A writer removes only classes it wrote and no longer writes. Template classes come first, in a fixed order, followed by classes other code added. `classList.add` appends, so a widget adding a class leaves the order unchanged. The same "remove only what you wrote" rule now covers all other attributes.
  
  The new tests re-render one side alone in each order and compare the result with a fresh render. They cover static and bound classes on both sides, a class added by other code, and stale classes on markup from a static build.
  
  ## Things that behave differently now
  
  - **Class order:** on a free component's container, the page's own class now comes after the template's, e.g. `outer container` rather than `container outer`. I updated five existing test expectations to match.
  - **`@class` on an `@id` element** still belongs to the child's placeholder template, as the code's comment intends. A parent binds that element's class by interpolation, as `class="slot @{extra}"`.
  - **A new marker attribute:** a page author's own classes on a `fluid-layers` element can't otherwise be told apart from template classes once the page has been rendered statically. When a template first renders into such an element, the framework records those classes as `fluid-own-class`, following the `fluid-site-root` precedent. Without it, the author's classes were dropped when booting the static page but kept when booting the minimal one.
  
  ## Static rendering (step 2)
  
  **infusion-6 changes:**
  - **Placeholders:** a page names placeholder data with `<fluid-placeholder for="…" src="…">`. Under node those files are fetched in place of the real data, and `fluid.renderingPlaceholders` is set. The browser ignores the element.
  - **Waiting for data:** under node, relative URLs resolve against the page. `fluid.fetch` now runs inside the reactive graph, so `hydrate.js` waits for data instead of writing the page while a fetch is pending.
  - **Portable output:** the static page refers to its injected files relative to itself (no `file:` URLs). Each script it holds records its source in `fluid-src`.
  - **Booting the static page:**
    - The browser adopts the scripts, styles and symbols the page already holds, so nothing runs twice.
    - A component that boots before its SFC has been fetched waits for its template rather than failing.
    - An interpolated class still pending no longer renders an error in place of its element.
  
  **bagatelle changes:**
  - **Config SFC:** the page's configuration now lives in `drivers/hortis-bbea-bcba.vue`, because `hydrate.js` doesn't run inline page scripts.
  - **Placeholder data:** `scripts/makePlaceholderData.js` builds the BCBA placeholders in `data/b-team/placeholder/`: 8 observations, the 29 taxa they need, and 3 regions.
  - **Fixes for rendering under node:** `.csv` files are loaded with `fetch`, and `src/geom/geoJSON.js` no longer calls `require` outside a node module.
  - **Loading indicator:** the static page shows it until the real data arrives.
  
  ## The round-trip tests
  
  - `npm run hydrate-roundtrip-test` (infusion-6) uses a small fixture with nested SFC imports, a script shared between SFCs, a browser-only widget, a stylesheet, a symbol and placeholder data.
  - `node test/i6/bbeaHydrationRoundTrip.js` (bagatelle) does the same for the BCBA page.
  - **What they do:**
    1. Run `hydrate.js` on the page.
    2. Load the minimal page and the static one in headless Chrome.
    3. Wait until each is ready with the real data.
    4. Compare the rendered markup and the set of injected nodes, with attributes in sorted order.
  - **Also checked:**
    - The static page shows the placeholder render as soon as it is parsed, and has no `file:` URLs.
    - Shared and browser-only scripts each run exactly once.
    - Neither page reports errors.
    - On the BBEA page, MapLibre's own markup inside the map container is left out of the comparison.
  - **Timings:** the BCBA page is ready in about 590ms from the minimal page and 375ms from the static one, and the result matched on all three runs.

         /**
          * Acquires all `<fluid-module>` elements within the given DOM root and populates the fluid module registry.
          * Each `<fluid-module>` element must have an `id` and a `src` attribute. The `src` is normalized to ensure it does not end with a "/".
          *
          * @param {Document} dokkument - The document for/from which the module should be registered
          * @param {VNode|Element} root - The root DOM element to search for `<fluid-module>` elements.
          * @return {Object<String, Object>} An array of objects representing the acquired `<fluid-module>` nodes.
          */
         fluid.acquireModules = function (dokkument, root) {
             const moduleNodes = fluid.querySelectorAll(root, "fluid-module");
             const entries = moduleNodes.map(node => {
                 const id = node.attrs.id;
                 const rawSrc = node.attrs.src;
                 const origSrc = fluid.deSlash(rawSrc);
                 const abs = fluid.isAbsolutePath(origSrc);
                 const src = abs ? origSrc : fluid.deSlash(new URL(origSrc, dokkument.location.href).href);
                 fluid.module.register(id, src, origSrc, abs);
                 return [id, {node, path: src}];
             });
             return Object.fromEntries(entries);
         };

// Every URL fetched under node, as the document refers to it - i.e. before any is redirected to a module's source -
// including both the URL of any data for which a placeholder is fetched, and that of the placeholder
fluid.serverFetchedUrls = new Set();

// Map of the absolute URL of a module's directory as a document declares it with <fluid-module>, ending in "/", to the
// absolute URL of a directory from which its files are fetched under node in its place - see fluid.registerModuleSources
fluid.serverModuleSources = {};

/**
 * Redirect a URL which lies within the directory of a module, as a document declares it, to the corresponding URL
 * within the directory registered as that module's source, if any - see `fluid.registerModuleSources`
 * @param {String} url - An absolute URL
 * @return {String} The URL from which the resource is to be fetched
 */
fluid.moduleSourceUrl = function (url) {
    const declared = Object.keys(fluid.serverModuleSources).filter(prefix => url.startsWith(prefix))
        .sort((a, b) => b.length - a.length)[0];
    return declared ? fluid.serverModuleSources[declared] + url.substring(declared.length) : url;
};

/**
 * Register the directories from which the files of modules which a document declares by `<fluid-module id="..."
 * src="...">` are read under node, in place of the directories which it declares. This allows a page to be booted, and
 * so its dependencies discovered, before the files of those modules have been copied to the places it expects - see
 * copyOut.js
 * @param {Document} dokkument - The document, whose location has been set
 * @param {Object<String, String>} moduleSources - Map of module id to the absolute path of its source directory
 * @return {Object<String, String>} Map of the absolute URL of each module's declared directory to that of its source
 */
fluid.registerModuleSources = function (dokkument, moduleSources) {
    dokkument.querySelectorAll("fluid-module").forEach(node => {
        const source = moduleSources[node.getAttribute("id")];
        if (source) {
            const declared = new URL(fluid.deSlash(node.getAttribute("src")) + "/", dokkument.location).href;
            fluid.serverModuleSources[declared] = fluid.deSlash(pathToFileURL(source).href) + "/";
        }
    });
    const unknown = Object.keys(moduleSources).filter(id => !dokkument.querySelector(`fluid-module[id="${id}"]`));
    if (unknown.length > 0) {
        fluid.fail("Sources supplied for modules " + unknown.join(", ") + " which the document does not declare with <fluid-module>");
    }
    return fluid.serverModuleSources;
};

 * Wait until the reactive graph has settled with a booted document, so that all the injections and rendering it
 * triggers are complete, without writing it - see `fluid.writeDocumentsWhenSettled`
 * @param {Document} dokkument - The document which has been booted

 */
fluid.documentWhenSettled = async function (dokkument) {
    const ready = fluid.documentReady(dokkument);
    const readyWatcher = fluid.cell.effect(readiness => readiness, [ready], {isFree: true, name: "Watch document ready"});

/* eslint-env node */
"use strict";

// Test copyOut.js, which copies into a project the files of the modules its pages depend upon. The project is a copy
// of copyout/site, made in a temporary directory, whose page declares two modules - Infusion, and the round trip
// fixture's Single File Components - and holds data of its own. Once their files are copied out, the project must
// render, served from its own directory alone, identically whether booted from its minimal page or from the page as
// hydrated - see hydrate-roundtrip-test.js

const childProcess = require("child_process"),
    fs = require("fs"),
    os = require("os"),
    path = require("path");

const fluidHydrationRoundTrip = require("../../test-core/browser/js/hydration-roundtrip.js");

const repoRoot = path.resolve(__dirname, "../../.."),
    copyOutScript = path.join(repoRoot, "src/framework/server/copyOut.js"),
    rtRoot = path.join(__dirname, "roundtrip");

const failures = [];
const expect = function (condition, message) {
    if (!condition) {
        failures.push(message);
    }
};

/**
 * Run copyOut.js on the project's page
 * @param {String} projectDir - The project's directory
 * @param {String[]} extraArgs - Further arguments
 * @return {Object} The result of the child process, with members `status` and `stdout`
 */
const copyOut = function (projectDir, extraArgs) {
    const result = childProcess.spawnSync(process.execPath, [copyOutScript, "index.html",
        "--source", "infusion-6=" + repoRoot, "--source", "fluid-tests-rt=" + rtRoot, ...extraArgs], {
        cwd: projectDir, encoding: "utf8", timeout: 120000
    });
    return {status: result.status, stdout: result.stdout + result.stderr};
};

const summary = stdout => (stdout.match(/\n(\d+ new, \d+ changed, \d+ unchanged, \d+ missing.*)/) || [])[1];

const main = async function () {
    const projectDir = fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), "fluid-copyout-"));
    try {
        fs.cpSync(path.join(__dirname, "copyout/site"), projectDir, {recursive: true});
        const exists = file => fs.existsSync(path.join(projectDir, file));

        const dry = copyOut(projectDir, ["-n"]);
        expect(dry.status === 0, "Dry run succeeds - " + dry.stdout.slice(-2000));
        expect(!exists("vendor"), "Dry run copies nothing");

        const first = copyOut(projectDir, []);
        expect(first.status === 0, "Copy out succeeds - " + first.stdout.slice(-2000));
        [
            "vendor/infusion/src/framework/core/js/Fluid.js",
            "vendor/infusion/src/framework/core/js/sfc-parser.js",
            "vendor/infusion/src/lib/lezer/lezer-javascript-browser.js",
            "vendor/rt/sfc/fluid-tests-rt-app.vue",
            "vendor/rt/sfc/parts/fluid-tests-rt-list.vue",
            "vendor/rt/sfc/parts/fluid-tests-rt-item.vue",
            "vendor/rt/sfc/parts/fluid-tests-rt-panel.vue",
            "vendor/rt/sfc/parts/panel.css",
            "vendor/rt/sfc/parts/star.svg",
            "vendor/rt/lib/shared.js",
            "vendor/rt/lib/client-widget.js"
        ].forEach(file => expect(exists(file), "Demanded file copied out: " + file));
        [
            "vendor/rt/index.html",
            "vendor/rt/data/records.json",
            "vendor/infusion/src/framework/core/js/FluidDebugging.js",
            "vendor/infusion/package.json"
        ].forEach(file => expect(!exists(file), "File not demanded is not copied out: " + file));
        expect(/^0 new, 0 changed, \d+ unchanged, 0 missing/.test(summary(copyOut(projectDir, []).stdout)),
            "Second copy out finds everything unchanged");

        fs.appendFileSync(path.join(projectDir, "vendor/rt/lib/shared.js"), "\n// Local edit\n");
        const changed = copyOut(projectDir, ["-n"]).stdout;
        expect(changed.includes("changed: vendor/rt/lib/shared.js") && /^0 new, 1 changed/.test(summary(changed)),
            "Dry run reports a file differing from its checkout - found " + summary(changed));
        copyOut(projectDir, []);

        const result = await fluidHydrationRoundTrip.run({
            root: projectDir,
            page: "index.html",
            ready: `document.querySelectorAll(".rt-item").length === 3 && !!document.querySelector(".rt-app.rt-loaded")
                && !!document.querySelector(".rt-widget-live")`,
            initial: `[...document.querySelectorAll(".rt-item")].map(item => item.textContent).join()`,
            timeout: 30000
        });
        expect(result.hydrated.initial === "Placeholder", "Hydrated project page rendered from its own placeholder - found " + result.hydrated.initial);
        expect(result.hydratedText.includes("src=\"vendor/rt/lib/client-widget.js\""), "Hydrated page refers to the copied out script");
        [["dehydrated", result.dehydrated], ["hydrated", result.hydrated]].forEach(([name, loaded]) => {
            expect(loaded.errors.length === 0, `No errors in ${name} page served from the project alone - found ${JSON.stringify(loaded.errors)}`);
        });
        const difference = fluidHydrationRoundTrip.firstDifference(result.dehydrated.snapshot, result.hydrated.snapshot);
        expect(difference === null, "Dehydrated and hydrated project pages render identically - " + difference);
    } finally {
        fs.rmSync(projectDir, {recursive: true, force: true});
    }

    if (failures.length === 0) {
        console.log("copyout-test PASS");
    } else {
        console.log("copyout-test FAIL:\n  " + failures.join("\n  "));
        process.exitCode = 1;
    }
};

main().catch(error => {
    console.error("copyout-test FAIL: ", error);
    process.exitCode = 1;
});
EOF

  ⎿  #### Minimal pages and placeholder data
     
     A page need hold no more than its framework scripts, a `<fluid-import>` of the Single File Component at the root of
     its tree, and an element bearing `fluid-layers`. The SFCs it imports, and those they import in turn, supply all of its
     scripts, stylesheets, symbols and markup. Booted in the browser, such a page discovers them as its components are
     instantiated. Rendered by `hydrate.js`, the page is written with all of them in place, and the browser shows its markup
     as soon as it is parsed.
     
     Data which only a live page needs to load in full is named with a placeholder, a short file of the same shape:
     
     ```html
     <fluid-placeholder for="data/observations.csv" src="data/placeholder/observations.csv"></fluid-placeholder>
     ```
     
     When the page is rendered under node, data fetched from `for` is fetched from `src` instead, and
     `fluid.renderingPlaceholders` is `true`, so that a component can show that it is still loading. In the browser the
     element has no effect.
     
     When the browser boots a page written by `hydrate.js`, it adopts what the page already holds:
     
     * Injected scripts, styles and symbols are not injected again. A script referred to by `src` records its source as
       `fluid-src`, so that it is recognised, and is not run a second time, by any other SFC which refers to it.
     * Scripts bearing `fluid-client`, which were written but not run under node, load as the page does.
     * The rendered markup is claimed by position, and rerendered as the real data arrives. Classes and attributes which
       the templates no longer write are removed from it. Those of
          ... [+5 more lines truncated]
