  ## Your question about inlined scripts
  
  Yes. Papa Parse, pako and the i6 files are needed at runtime in the browser as well. They're the scripts without `fluid-client`, which the components need even to render under node. `hydrate.js` evaluates them there and writes their text into the static page. That's why the BCBA static page is about 300KB.
  
  Scripts with `fluid-client`, such as MapLibre and d3, are never run under node. They're written as `<script src>` links instead.
  
  The scripts run under node are inlined because each one is wrapped before it runs: a script without `data-fl-scope="global"` is put inside a function, and a completion marker is added. A plain `<script src>` can't apply that wrapping. They could be written as links if those scripts became global-scoped, or if the framework served the wrapped versions. Either would shrink the static page a lot.
  
  ## The copy-out tool
  
  `infusion-6/src/framework/server/copyOut.js` uses the `<fluid-module>` element pages already support. A subsidiary page declares each library in a folder of its own and refers to its files through that folder:
  
  ```html
  <fluid-module id="imerss-bioinfo" src="vendor/imerss-bioinfo"></fluid-module>
  <fluid-import src="%imerss-bioinfo/drivers/hortis-bbea-bcba.vue"></fluid-import>
  ```
  
  ```
  node copyOut.js index.html --source imerss-bioinfo=../bagatelle --source infusion-6=../infusion-6 [-n] [--list]
  ```
  
  - **What it copies:** it boots the page under node, reading each module's files from its source checkout, and records every file the page uses:
    - the imported SFCs, nested ones included;
    - the scripts and stylesheets they inject, browser-only ones included;
    - the Infusion scripts in the page itself;
    - images and fonts referenced from the CSS;
    - any data it fetches.
  
    It copies each into the declared folder, so the page and its SFCs need no rewriting.
  - **Repeat runs and dry runs:** run again, it reports which copied files differ from their source; `-n` copies nothing.
  - **Missing files:** the page's own data is left alone, but the tool fails if a file it needs doesn't exist.
  - **Config:** module sources can also come from a `moduleOverrides.json5` file, as howe-sound already has.
  - **Framework change:** under node, stylesheet injection now looks for the file in the module's source checkout as well.
  
  ## Tests
  
  - **`npm run copyout-test` (infusion-6):** copies a small fixture project into a temporary folder and copies out its two modules. It then checks:
    - only the files the page uses are copied, including an image referenced from a stylesheet;
    - a second run finds nothing to copy, and a local edit is reported as changed;
    - nothing fails to load before anything has been copied;
    - the page served from that folder alone renders the same from its minimal form as from its static one, with no errors.
  - **The real BCBA page:** I ran the same process on a scratch project holding its own data. That copied 67 files (4.5MB) in under a second. I added an optional `<root> <page>` argument to `bbeaHydrationRoundTrip.js` so it can test that project, and the copied-out page passed the round trip.

  ⎿   * Render a row's checkbox. Its checked and indeterminate states are written as literal attributes, which the

      * @param {String} id - The row's taxon id
      * @param {String} selected - The row's selection state

     hortis.checklist.checkboxNode = function (id, selected) {
         const attrs = {type: "checkbox", "class": "checklist-check", "data-row-id": id};
         if (selected === "selected") {
             attrs.checked = "";
         } else if (selected === "indeterminate") {
             attrs.indeterminate = "";

         return {tag: "span", attrs: {"class": "pretty p-icon"}, children: [

                 {tag: "i", attrs: {"class": "icon mdi" + (selected === "indeterminate" ? "" : " mdi-check")}, children: []},

             ]}

// Adds a method `download`, which downloads as CSV the names of the leaf taxa selected in the checklist, or of all
// those displayed if none is selected, which are of the ranks `copyChecklistRanks`
fluid.def("hortis.checklist.withDownload", {
    copyChecklistRanks: ["species"],
    downloadFile: "taxa.csv",
    allLeaves: "$compute:hortis.checklist.computeLeaves({self}.idToEntry, {self}.rowSelection, {self}.copyChecklistRanks)",
    download: "$method:hortis.checklist.download({self}.allLeaves, {self}.downloadFile)"
});

/**
 * Find the scientific names of the leaf taxa beneath a selection, of the given ranks.
 * @param {Object<String, ChecklistEntry>} idToEntry - Map of taxon id to entry
 * @param {Object<String, Boolean>} selection - The selected taxon ids
 * @param {String[]} copyChecklistRanks - The ranks of the leaves to be listed
 * @return {String[]} The sorted names of the leaves
 */
hortis.checklist.computeLeaves = function (idToEntry, selection, copyChecklistRanks) {
    const leaves = {};
    const appendLeaves = function (id) {
        const entry = idToEntry[id];
        // The NO_TAXON entry stands for no taxon, e.g. a bee recorded on no plant
        if (entry && id !== "0") {
            if (entry.children.length === 0) {
                leaves[entry.row.id] = entry.row;
            } else {
                entry.children.forEach(child => appendLeaves(child.row.id));
            }
        }
    };
    Object.keys(selection).forEach(appendLeaves);
    return Object.values(leaves).filter(leaf => copyChecklistRanks.includes(leaf.rank)).map(hortis.rowToScientific).sort();
};

hortis.checklist.download = function (allLeaves, downloadFile) {
    hortis.triggerDownload(["taxon", ...allLeaves].join("\\n"), "text/csv", downloadFile);
};
'''
open(p,"w").write(s)

<script>
"use strict";

// Filters observations by the regions in which they lie, offering a checkbox for each row of a region indirection
// table, with members `regionField`, the column of the observations holding the region, `id`, the value found there
// and `label`. Rows of the regionFields `fieldNames` are offered - e.g. ["dataset"] for a filter by dataset
fluid.def("hortis.regionFilter", {
    $layers: "hortis.obsFilter",
    filterName: "Region",
    // fieldNames: String[]
    // indirectionRows: Object[]
    summaryNouns: ["region", "regions"],
    filterRows: "$compute:hortis.regionFilter.filterRows({self}.indirectionRows, {self}.fieldNames)",
    // Hash of the index of each selected row of filterRows to true
    filterState: {},
    filterSummary: "$compute:hortis.keyCountSummary({self}.filterState, {self}.summaryNouns)",
    doFilter: "$method:hortis.regionFilter.doFilter({self}.filterRows, {0}:obsRows, {1}:filterState)",
    reset: "$method:hortis.regionFilter.reset({self})",
    regionRows: {
        $component: {
            $layers: "hortis.regionFilter.row",
            $for: {
                source: "{regionFilter}.filterRows",
                valueAs: "region",
                keyAs: "index"
            }
        }
    }
});

hortis.regionFilter.filterRows = function (indirectionRows, fieldNames) {
    return indirectionRows.filter(row => fieldNames.includes(row.regionField));
};

hortis.regionFilter.isChecked = (filterState, index) => !!filterState[index];

hortis.regionFilter.toggle = function (that, index, checked) {
    const filterState = {...that.filterState};
    if (checked) {
        filterState[index] = true;
    } else {
        delete filterState[index];
    }
    that.filterState = filterState;
};

hortis.regionFilter.rowChange = function (event, row) {
    row.toggle(event.target.checked);
};

hortis.regionFilter.reset = function (that) {
    that.filterState = {};
};

hortis.regionFilter.doFilter = function (filterRows, obsRows, filterState) {
    const selected = Object.keys(filterState).map(index => filterRows[index]);
    return selected.length === 0 ? obsRows : obsRows.filter(obsRow => selected.some(iRow => obsRow[iRow.regionField] === iRow.id));
};

        const input = dokkument.getElementById(that.controlId);

/**
 * Filter observations to those of a taxon, or of any taxon beneath it.
 * @param {Object[]} obsRows - The observations
 * @param {TaxonRow|null} filterState - The chosen taxon, or null if none is chosen
 * @param {Object<String, TaxonRow>} rowById - Map of taxon id to indexed taxon row
 * @return {Object[]} The observations surviving the filter
 */
hortis.taxonSearchFilter.doFilter = function (obsRows, filterState, rowById) {
    const includeRow = function (obsRow) {
        let taxonRow = rowById[obsRow.iNaturalistTaxonId];
        while (taxonRow && taxonRow.id !== filterState.id) {
            taxonRow = taxonRow.parent;
        }
        return !!taxonRow;
    };
    return filterState ? obsRows.filter(includeRow) : obsRows;
};

/**
 * Render the tooltip of a grid cell, listing the ten taxa with the most observations in it.
 * @param {Object} grid - The grid, whose `buckets` hold each cell's observations by taxon id
 * @param {Object<String, TaxonRow>} rowById - Map of taxon id to taxon row
 * @param {String} cellId - The id of the hovered cell
 * @return {String|null} The tooltip's markup, or null if the cell holds no observations
 */
hortis.renderVizGridTooltip = function (grid, rowById, cellId) {
    const bucket = grid.buckets[cellId];
    let togo = null;
    if (bucket) {
        const rowTemplate = "<div>%taxonName: %obsCount observation%s</div>";
        const rows = Object.entries(bucket.byTaxonId).map(([taxonId, obsIds]) => ({
            taxonName: rowById[taxonId]?.iNaturalistTaxonName || "Unknown",
            obsCount: obsIds.length,
            s: obsIds.length === 1 ? "" : "s"
        })).sort((rowa, rowb) => rowb.obsCount - rowa.obsCount);
        const shown = rows.slice(0, 10);
        togo = hortis.stringTemplate(hortis.vizGridTooltipTemplate, {
            obsCount: bucket.obsCount,
            taxonCount: rows.length,
            taxa: shown.map(row => hortis.stringTemplate(rowTemplate, row)).join("\n"),
            footer: rows.length > 10 ? "<div class=\"text\">...</div>" : ""
        });
    }
    return togo;
};

<script src="../js/i6/imerss-core.js"></script>
<script src="../js/i6/filters.js"></script>
<script>
"use strict";

// The counts of taxa by reporting status of a BioBlitz - historical records, which are confirmed or unconfirmed by its
// contributors, and new ones. The confirmed, unconfirmed and new counts are buttons which together filter the
// observations to taxa of the chosen statuses
fluid.def("hortis.blitzRecords", {
    $layers: "hortis.obsFilter",
    rowById: "{vizLoader}.taxa.rowById",
    filterState: {
        $reactiveRoot: {confirmed: false, unconfirmed: false, new: false}
    },
    statusById: "$compute:hortis.blitzRecords.statusById({self}.rowById)",
    counts: "$compute:hortis.blitzRecords.counts({self}.statusById)",
    filterSummary: "$compute:hortis.blitzRecords.summarise({self}.filterState)",
    doFilter: "$method:hortis.blitzRecords.doFilter({0}:obsRows, {1}:filterState, {self}.statusById)",
    toggle: "$method:hortis.blitzRecords.toggle({self}, {0}:status)",
    reset: "$method:hortis.blitzRecords.reset({self})"
});

/**
 * Classify the reporting status of each taxon as "confirmed", "unconfirmed" or "new".
 * @param {Object<String, TaxonRow>} rowById - Map of taxon id to taxon row, each with a `reportingStatus`
 * @return {Object<String, String>} Map of taxon id to its status, for the taxa which have one
 */
hortis.blitzRecords.statusById = function (rowById) {
    const togo = {};
    Object.values(rowById).forEach(row => {
        const reportingStatus = row.reportingStatus || "";
        if (reportingStatus === "confirmed") {
            togo[row.id] = "confirmed";
        } else if (reportingStatus === "reported" || reportingStatus === "unconfirmed") {
            togo[row.id] = "unconfirmed";
        } else if (reportingStatus.startsWith("new")) {
            togo[row.id] = "new";
        }
    });
    return togo;
};

hortis.blitzRecords.counts = function (statusById) {
    const counts = {confirmed: 0, unconfirmed: 0, new: 0};
    Object.values(statusById).forEach(status => ++counts[status]);
    return {
        historical: hortis.formatInt(counts.confirmed + counts.unconfirmed),
        confirmed: hortis.formatInt(counts.confirmed),
        unconfirmed: hortis.formatInt(counts.unconfirmed),
        new: hortis.formatInt(counts.new)
    };
};

hortis.blitzRecords.summarise = function (filterState) {
    return hortis.countSummary(filterState.confirmed + filterState.unconfirmed + filterState.new, ["record status", "record statuses"]);
};

hortis.blitzRecords.doFilter = function (obsRows, filterState, statusById) {
    const count = filterState.confirmed + filterState.unconfirmed + filterState.new;
    const all = count === 0 || count === 3;
    return all ? obsRows : obsRows.filter(obsRow => filterState[statusById[obsRow.iNaturalistTaxonId]]);
};

hortis.blitzRecords.toggle = function (that, status) {
    that.filterState = {...that.filterState, [status]: !that.filterState[status]};
};

hortis.blitzRecords.reset = function (that) {
    that.filterState = {confirmed: false, unconfirmed: false, new: false};
};
</script>

<template>
    <div class="imerss-blitz-records">
        <div class="imerss-records-historical imerss-records">
            <div class="records-label">Historical Records</div>
            <div class="records-value">@{counts.historical}</div>
        </div>
        <button class="imerss-records-confirmed imerss-records" @class="selected:@{filterState.confirmed}" type="button"
            @onclick="{self}.toggle(confirmed)">
            <div class="records-label">Confirmed Records</div>
            <div class="records-value">@{counts.confirmed}</div>
        </button>
        <button class="imerss-records-unconfirmed imerss-records" @class="selected:@{filterState.unconfirmed}" type="button"
            @onclick="{self}.toggle(unconfirmed)">
            <div class="records-label">Unconfirmed Records</div>
            <div class="records-value">@{counts.unconfirmed}</div>
        </button>
        <button class="imerss-records-new imerss-records" @class="selected:@{filterState.new}" type="button"
            @onclick="{self}.toggle(new)">
            <div class="records-label">New Records</div>
            <div class="records-value">@{counts.new}</div>
        </button>
    </div>
</template>

hortis.standardVizLoader.loaded = () => !fluid.renderingPlaceholders;

/**
 * Find the taxa of a set of observations, together with all their ancestors.
 * @param {Object[]} filteredObs - The observations, each with an `iNaturalistTaxonId`
 * @param {Object<String, TaxonRow>} rowById - Map of taxon id to indexed taxon row
 * @return {Object<String, Boolean>} Map of the id of each such taxon to true
 */
hortis.taxaFromObs = function (filteredObs, rowById) {
    const taxonIds = {};
    filteredObs.forEach(row => {
        taxonIds[row.iNaturalistTaxonId] = true;
    });
    return hortis.closeParentTaxa(taxonIds, rowById);
};

  out=$1; title=$2; driver=$3; layer=$4; dir=$5; shift 5
  { sed -n '1,/<fluid-import/p' indexBeasBCBA-6.html | sed '/<fluid-import\|The visualisation of the BCBA\|depends on -->/d' | sed "s#<title>.*</title>#<title>$title - Infusion 6</title>#"

}

/* eslint-env node */
"use strict";

// Test that the pages of the standard visualisation - indexBlitz-6.html, of the Galiano BioBlitz 2023, and
// indexDiatoms-6.html, of the diatoms of the Salish Sea - render identically whether booted in the browser from their
// minimal, dehydrated forms or from the forms written for them by Infusion 6's hydrate.js. See
// bbeaHydrationRoundTrip.js, whose assumptions this shares. Run from the bagatelle checkout with
//     node test/i6/standardHydrationRoundTrip.js
// Also checks, in the Blitz page booted from its minimal form, that its tabs, record status buttons and checklist
// filter the observations.

const path = require("path"),
    linkedom = require("../../../infusion-6/node_modules/linkedom"),
    puppeteer = require("../../../infusion-6/node_modules/puppeteer");

const fluidHydrationRoundTrip = require("../../../infusion-6/tests/test-core/browser/js/hydration-roundtrip.js"),
    fluidDemoRunner = require("../../../infusion-6/tests/test-core/browser/js/demo-runner.js");

const root = path.resolve(__dirname, "../../..");

const failures = [];
const expect = function (condition, message) {
    if (!condition) {
        failures.push(message);
    }
};

const reporterText = `(document.querySelector(".imerss-record-reporter")?.textContent || "").replace(/\\s+/g, " ").trim()`;

const pages = [{
    name: "Blitz",
    page: "bagatelle/indexBlitz-6.html",
    allRows: "555",
    checks: document => {
        expect(document.querySelectorAll(".imerss-checklist-decoration").length > 0, "Blitz checklist rows decorated by reporting status");
        expect(!!document.querySelector(".imerss-blitz-records button.imerss-records-confirmed"), "Blitz record status buttons rendered");
    }
}, {
    name: "Diatoms",
    page: "bagatelle/indexDiatoms-6.html",
    allRows: "4,803",
    checks: document => {
        expect(!document.querySelector(".imerss-blitz-records"), "Diatoms page has no record status buttons");
    }
}];

const snapshot = `(() => {
    const clone = document.querySelector("[fluid-layers]").cloneNode(true);
    clone.querySelectorAll(".imerss-map").forEach(map => map.replaceChildren());
    return {
        components: fluidCanonicalMarkup(clone),
        injections: [...document.querySelectorAll("[id^='fl-script-'], [id^='fl-style-'], [id^='fl-symbols-']")].map(node => node.id).sort(),
        mapCanvases: document.querySelectorAll(".imerss-map canvas").length
    };
})()`;

const roundTrip = async function (spec) {
    const ready = `${reporterText}.includes("${spec.allRows} of ${spec.allRows}") && !document.querySelector(".imerss-loading")
        && !!document.querySelector(".imerss-map canvas")`;
    const result = await fluidHydrationRoundTrip.run({
        root, page: spec.page, ready, snapshot,
        initial: `(() => ({reporter: ${reporterText}, loading: !!document.querySelector(".imerss-loading")}))()`,
        diagnose: `({reporter: ${reporterText}, canvases: document.querySelectorAll(".imerss-map canvas").length})`,
        ignoreErrors: [/Failed to load resource/, /net::ERR_/],
        timeout: 120000,
        settle: 1000
    });
    const {document} = linkedom.parseHTML(result.hydratedText);
    spec.checks(document);
    expect(result.hydrated.initial.reporter === "Displaying 8 of 8 records" && result.hydrated.initial.loading,
        `${spec.name} hydrated page shows its placeholder rendering as soon as it is parsed - found ${JSON.stringify(result.hydrated.initial)}`);
    expect(result.dehydrated.initial.reporter === "", `${spec.name} dehydrated page holds no markup of its own`);
    [["dehydrated", result.dehydrated], ["hydrated", result.hydrated]].forEach(([name, loaded]) => {
        expect(loaded.errors.length === 0, `No errors in ${spec.name} ${name} page - found ${JSON.stringify(loaded.errors)}`);
        expect(loaded.snapshot.mapCanvases === 1, `One map drawn in ${spec.name} ${name} page`);
    });
    const difference = fluidHydrationRoundTrip.firstDifference(result.dehydrated.snapshot, result.hydrated.snapshot);
    expect(difference === null, `${spec.name} dehydrated and hydrated pages render identically - ${difference}`);
    console.log(`${spec.name}: hydrated in ${result.hydrateTime}ms; ready in browser: dehydrated ${result.dehydrated.readyTime}ms, ` +
        `hydrated ${result.hydrated.readyTime}ms`);
};

// Drive the Blitz page booted from its minimal form
const interact = async function () {
    const server = await fluidDemoRunner.startServer(root);
    const browser = await puppeteer.launch({headless: true, args: ["--no-sandbox"]});
    try {
        const page = await browser.newPage();
        const errors = [];
        page.on("pageerror", error => errors.push(error.message));
        await page.setViewport({width: 1400, height: 1000});
        await page.goto(`http://127.0.0.1:${server.address().port}/bagatelle/indexBlitz-6.html`, {waitUntil: "domcontentloaded"});
        await page.waitForFunction(`${reporterText}.includes("555 of 555")`, {timeout: 60000});
        const reporter = () => page.evaluate(reporterText);
        const until = condition => page.waitForFunction(condition, {timeout: 5000}).then(() => true, () => false);

        await page.click(".ui-tabs-tab:nth-child(2) a");
        expect(await until(`!document.getElementById("fli-tab-checklist").hidden && document.getElementById("fli-tab-map").hidden`),
            "Clicking the Checklist tab shows its panel and hides the map's");

        await page.click(".imerss-records-confirmed");
        expect(await until(`!${reporterText}.includes("555 of 555") && !!document.querySelector(".imerss-records-confirmed.selected")`),
            "Clicking Confirmed Records filters the observations - found " + await reporter());
        await page.click(".imerss-records-confirmed");
        expect(await until(`${reporterText}.includes("555 of 555")`), "Clicking Confirmed Records again clears its filter");

        const name = await page.evaluate(`document.querySelector(".checklist-rank-species p[data-row-id]")?.textContent`);
        await page.click(".checklist-rank-species p[data-row-id]");
        expect(await until(`!${reporterText}.includes("555 of 555") && document.querySelector(".imerss-search-checklist input").value !== ""`),
            `Clicking the checklist name ${name} filters to its taxon - found ` + await reporter());
        await page.click(".imerss-filter-controls");
        expect(await until(`${reporterText}.includes("555 of 555") && document.querySelector(".imerss-search-checklist input").value === ""`),
            "Reset filters clears the taxon filter - found " + await reporter());

        await page.click(".imerss-dataset-filter .imerss-filter-row:nth-child(1) input");
        expect(await until(`!${reporterText}.includes("555 of 555")`), "Checking a dataset filters the observations - found " + await reporter());
        expect(errors.length === 0, "No errors interacting with the Blitz page - found " + JSON.stringify(errors));
    } finally {
        await browser.close();
        server.close();
    }
};

const main = async function () {
    for (const spec of pages) {
        await roundTrip(spec);
    }
    await interact();
    if (failures.length === 0) {
        console.log("standardHydrationRoundTrip PASS");
    } else {
        console.log("standardHydrationRoundTrip FAIL:\n  " + failures.join("\n  "));
        process.exitCode = 1;
    }
};

main().catch(error => {
    console.error("standardHydrationRoundTrip FAIL: ", error);
    process.exitCode = 1;
});

● Bash: cd /home/amb26/Source/gits/bagatelle/src/client; grep -n "fluid.colour.memoStops = \|fluid.colour.lookupStop = \|longitudeLength = " js/colour.js js/i6/*.js ../geom/*.js | head; cat >> js/i6/libreMap.js <<'EOF'

// Adds to a map with an observation grid a legend showing the range of observation counts of each colour of its cells,
// and the width of a cell
fluid.def("hortis.libreMap.withObsGridLegend", {
    legendStops: 5,
    legendPosition: "bottom-right",
    legendMarkup: `$compute:hortis.libreMap.obsGridLegendMarkup({self}.obsQuantiser.grid, {self}.fillStops, {self}.legendStops,
        {self}.maxObsCountOverride, {self}.inverseCountTransform, {self}.obsQuantiser.longResolution, {self}.obsQuantiser.baseLatitude)`,
    legend: {
        $bindable: {
            bind: "hortis.libreMap.addLegend({self}.readyMap, {self}.legendPosition, {global}.document)",
            unbind: "hortis.libreMap.removeLegend({self}.readyMap, {boundValue})",
            onceOnly: true
        }
    },
    renderLegend: "$effect:hortis.libreMap.renderLegend({self}.legend, {self}.legendMarkup, {self}.gridVisible)"
});

/**
 * Add an empty legend to a map as a control.
 * @param {maplibregl.Map} map - The map
 * @param {String} legendPosition - The corner of the map holding the legend, e.g. "bottom-left"
 * @param {Document} dokkument - The document holding the map
 * @return {Object} The control, whose `container` is the legend's element
 */
hortis.libreMap.addLegend = function (map, legendPosition, dokkument) {
    const container = dokkument.createElement("div");
    container.classList.add("imerss-legend");
    const control = {container, onAdd: () => container, onRemove: () => container.remove()};
    map.addControl(control, legendPosition);
    return control;
};

hortis.libreMap.removeLegend = function (map, control) {
    map.removeControl(control);
};

hortis.libreMap.renderLegend = function (control, markup, gridVisible) {
    control.container.innerHTML = markup;
    hortis.toggleClass(control.container, "fl-hidden", !gridVisible);
};

hortis.libreMap.legendRowTemplate = `
<div class="imerss-legend-row" title="%rowTitle">
    <span class="imerss-legend-icon"></span>
    <span class="imerss-legend-preview" style="%previewStyle"></span>
    <span class="imerss-legend-label">%keyLabel</span>
</div>`;

/**
 * Render the markup of the legend of an observation grid.
 * @param {Object} grid - The grid, as computed by `hortis.obsQuantiser.indexObs`
 * @param {Array[]} fillStops - The colour stops of the grid's cells
 * @param {Number} legendStops - The number of rows of the legend
 * @param {Number|null} maxObsCountOverride - A count to be taken as the maximum in place of the grid's own
 * @param {String} inverseCountTransform - Global name of the inverse of the transform applied to each cell's proportion
 * @param {Number} longResolution - The width of a cell in degrees of longitude
 * @param {Number} baseLatitude - The latitude at which the width of a cell is measured
 * @return {String} The legend's markup
 */
hortis.libreMap.obsGridLegendMarkup = function (grid, fillStops, legendStops, maxObsCountOverride, inverseCountTransform, longResolution, baseLatitude) {
    const maxObsCount = maxObsCountOverride || grid.maxObsCount;
    const inverse = fluid.getGlobalValue(inverseCountTransform);
    const memoStops = fluid.colour.memoStops(fillStops, 256);
    const props = fluid.iota(legendStops + 1).map(stop => stop / legendStops);
    const propToLevel = prop => prop >= 1 ? maxObsCount : Math.round(inverse(prop, maxObsCount) * maxObsCount);
    const rows = fluid.iota(legendStops).map(stop => {
        const label = propToLevel(props[stop]) + " - " + propToLevel(props[stop + 1]);
        return hortis.stringTemplate(hortis.libreMap.legendRowTemplate, {
            previewStyle: "background-color: " + fluid.colour.lookupStop(memoStops, (props[stop] + props[stop + 1]) / 2),
            keyLabel: label,
            rowTitle: "Grid cells holding " + label + " observations"
        });
    });
    const cellWidth = Math.round(longResolution * hortis.longitudeLength(baseLatitude));
    return "<div class=\"imerss-legend-title\" title=\"Number of observations falling within each grid cell\">Observation count</div>" +
        rows.join("\n") + `<div class="imerss-legend-cell-size" title="Width of each grid cell in metres">Cell size: ${cellWidth}m</div>`;
};

  ## Blitz and Diatoms
  
  `indexBlitz-6.html` and `indexDiatoms-6.html` are minimal pages like the BCBA one: the Infusion scripts, one `<fluid-import>` of a driver SFC, and placeholders for their three data files. Their drivers (`drivers/hortis-blitz-galiano.vue`, `drivers/hortis-diatoms-salish.vue`) set the title, data paths and grid size.
  
  Side-by-side screenshots show the same layout as the Infusion 4 pages:
  - tabs;
  - a map with the grid and its observation-count legend;
  - the recorder and dataset filters;
  - the record counter;
  - the four Blitz record-count boxes;
  - a checklist with status icons.
  
  The new SFCs in `src/client/sfc/` are:
  - **Loaders:** `hortis-standardVizLoader` (the whole page shell) and `hortis-blitzVizLoader` (adds the record buttons and the checklist icons).
  - **Filters:** `hortis-regionFilter` (the dataset checkboxes), `hortis-taxonSearchFilter`, `hortis-blitzRecords` (record counts that double as a status filter) and `hortis-standardFilterControls`.
    - The taxon search filters every observation to one taxon, and clicking a checklist name does the same.
  - **Views:** `hortis-standardChecklist` (search, CSV download, status icons), `hortis-vizLibreMap` (map with the grid tooltip and legend) and `hortis-pageTabs` (jQuery UI–style tabs without jQuery).
  
  Changes to shared code:
  - **`checklist.js`:** optional row decorations, a hook for clicks on taxon names, and a CSV download layer. BBEA behaves as before.
  - **`libreMap.js`:** the grid legend layer, which had never been ported to i6.
  - **`imerss-i6.css`:** a rule so unselected tab panels stay hidden.
  - **`makePlaceholderData.js`:** now finds the taxon-id columns of any observation table, not just BBEA's. It wrote placeholder data for both new pages.
  
  ## Tests
  
  `node test/i6/standardHydrationRoundTrip.js` runs the minimal-versus-static round trip for both pages; it passes with no errors. It then drives the minimal Blitz page and checks that:
  - the tabs switch panels;
  - Confirmed Records filters and unfilters;
  - clicking a checklist name filters to its taxon;
  - Reset clears that filter;
  - a dataset checkbox filters.
  
  The BBEA tests (155/155) and the BCBA round trip still pass.
  
  **One small difference:** the zoom buttons now sit above the polygon-draw buttons, where Infusion 4 had them the other way round.
  
  ## Decision needed: how to port the story map
  
  The story map is far bigger than Blitz: about 2,500 lines of Infusion 4 page code in howe-sound, plus about 1,300 lines across `taxonDisplay`, `dataTable` and `resizeBar`. Its page is built by `reknit.js`, which folds the knitted R HTML into a Hugo partial. There are two ways to port it:
  
  1. **Keep `reknit.js` as the page builder (my recommendation):** port the page code to SFCs and have `reknit.js` write the minimal page (imports, placeholders and the R panes). `hydrate.js` then renders it statically, and `copyOut.js` fills `static/` in place of the copy jobs in `config.json5`. The R pipelines and Hugo layouts don't change, which keeps the R-pipeline and navigation-sync rules.
  2. **Replace `reknit.js` with SFCs:** treat each knitted R pane as content an SFC imports and renders itself. This is cleaner in the long run, but it changes how the Hugo site is assembled in both projects.
  
  Shall I go ahead with option 1?


❯ Go for option 2. Reforming navigation-sync so that it ensures that the rendered panel is immediately selected from the URL fetched from the HashManager rather than rendering first and then jumping is one of the main goals of this work. The URL needs to be decoded into some "potentia-like" material on startup before any stabilisation and rendering begins.

old2='''    /**
     * Creates an effect that automatically instantiates self-booting Fluid components for elements'''
new2='''    /**
     * Parse the hash of a URL into a record. The hash takes the form `#key1:value1&key2:value2`, where a value
     * beginning with `{` or `[` is JSON. Segments without a `:` are ignored.
     * @param {String} hash - The hash, with or without its leading `#`
     * @return {Object} The record encoded by the hash
     */
    fluid.parseUrlHash = function (hash) {
        const parseSegment = function (segment) {
            const decoded = decodeURIComponent(segment);
            const colonIndex = decoded.indexOf(":");
            const value = decoded.substring(colonIndex + 1);
            return [decoded.substring(0, colonIndex), value.startsWith("{") || value.startsWith("[") ? JSON.parse(value) : value];
        };
        const sections = (hash || "").replace(/^#/, "").split("&");
        return Object.fromEntries(sections.filter(section => section.includes(":")).map(parseSegment));
    };

    /**
     * Render a record as the hash of a URL, in the form parsed by `fluid.parseUrlHash`. Members with `null` or
     * `undefined` values are omitted.
     * @param {Object} record - The record to be rendered
     * @return {String} The hash, beginning with `#`
     */
    fluid.renderUrlHash = function (record) {
        const nonEmpty = Object.entries(record).filter(([, value]) => fluid.isValue(value));
        return "#" + nonEmpty.map(([key, value]) => key + ":" + (fluid.isPrimitive(value) ? "" + value : JSON.stringify(value))).join("&");
    };

    /**
     * Compute the state with which a component booted by an element bearing `fluid-layers` begins, decoded from the
     * document's URL before the component is instantiated. An element bearing `fluid-hash="member"` begins its
     * component with the URL's hash, as parsed by `fluid.parseUrlHash`, as the initial value of a reactive root at
     * `member`. Since this is part of the component's potentia, everything computed from the hash - e.g. which of
     * several panels is shown - is first computed and rendered from it, rather than first from defaults which the
     * hash then overrides. Under node, e.g. when rendering a page statically, the document has no hash, and the
     * record is empty.
     * @param {Document} dokkument - The document holding the element
     * @param {Element} element - The element bearing `fluid-layers`
     * @return {Object} Members to be merged into the component's construction record
     */
    fluid.bootStateRecord = function (dokkument, element) {
        const hashMember = element.getAttribute("fluid-hash");
        const togo = {};
        if (hashMember) {
            togo[hashMember] = {$reactiveRoot: fluid.parseUrlHash(fluid.documentLocation(dokkument)?.hash)};
        }
        return togo;
    };

cat > boot-hash-test.js <<'EOF'
/* eslint-env node */
"use strict";

// Test that a component booted by an element bearing fluid-hash begins with the state encoded in the URL's hash -
// the pane it names is the first, and only, pane computed and rendered, rather than the default pane being rendered
// and then replaced. Selecting a pane writes it back to the hash, and navigating back restores the previous pane.

const path = require("path"),
    puppeteer = require("puppeteer");

const fluidDemoRunner = require("../../test-core/browser/js/demo-runner.js");

const repoRoot = path.resolve(__dirname, "../../..");

const failures = [];
const expect = function (condition, message) {
    if (!condition) {
        failures.push(message);
    }
};

const main = async function () {
    const server = await fluidDemoRunner.startServer(repoRoot);
    const browser = await puppeteer.launch({headless: true, args: ["--no-sandbox"]});
    try {
        const base = `http://127.0.0.1:${server.address().port}/tests/framework-tests/server/boothash/index.html`;
        const page = await browser.newPage();
        const errors = [];
        page.on("pageerror", error => errors.push(error.message));
        const shownIs = pane => page.waitForFunction(`document.querySelector(".shown-pane")?.textContent === "${pane}"`, {timeout: 10000})
            .then(() => true, () => false);
        const logs = () => page.evaluate("({computed: window.fluidTestsBoothashLog, shown: window.fluidTestsBoothashShown, hash: location.hash})");

        await page.goto(base + "#pane:second");
        expect(await shownIs("second"), "Page booted with #pane:second shows the second pane");
        let state = await logs();
        expect(JSON.stringify(state.computed) === "[\"second\"]", "Only the pane named by the URL was ever computed - found " + JSON.stringify(state.computed));
        expect(JSON.stringify(state.shown) === "[\"second\"]", "Only the pane named by the URL was ever shown - found " + JSON.stringify(state.shown));

        await page.click(".tab-first");
        expect(await shownIs("first"), "Selecting the first pane shows it");
        state = await logs();
        expect(state.hash === "#pane:first", "Selecting a pane writes it to the URL's hash - found " + state.hash);

        await page.goBack();
        expect(await shownIs("second"), "Navigating back restores the pane named by the previous URL");

        const fresh = await browser.newPage();
        await fresh.goto(base);
        expect(await fresh.waitForFunction(`document.querySelector(".shown-pane")?.textContent === "first"`, {timeout: 10000}).then(() => true, () => false),
            "Page booted without a hash shows the default pane");
        expect(errors.length === 0, "No errors - found " + JSON.stringify(errors));
    } finally {
        await browser.close();
        server.close();
    }
    if (failures.length === 0) {
        console.log("boot-hash-test PASS");
    } else {
        console.log("boot-hash-test FAIL:\n  " + failures.join("\n  "));
        process.exitCode = 1;
    }
};

main().catch(error => {
    console.error("boot-hash-test FAIL: ", error);
    process.exitCode = 1;
});
EOF

    // instantiated, by booting it from an element bearing fluid-hash="hash" - see fluid.bootStateRecord. Thereafter a

    /**
     * Determine whether two URL hashes are equivalent, ignoring percent-encoding and an empty hash's `#`.
     * @param {String} hash1 - The first hash
     * @param {String} hash2 - The second hash
     * @return {Boolean} `true` if the hashes are equivalent
     */
    fluid.hashSync.equivalent = function (hash1, hash2) {
        const normalise = hash => decodeURIComponent(hash.replace(/^#/, ""));
        return normalise(hash1) === normalise(hash2);
    };

    /**
     * Begin listening to a window's hash, writing it into `hash` whenever it changes. Unlike Infusion 4's hash
     * managers, the hash is not read here, since it was decoded before the component was instantiated.
     * @param {fluid.hashSync} that - The component
     * @param {Window} window - The window whose hash is listened to
     * @return {Object} A record of the listener, to be supplied to `fluid.hashSync.unlisten`
     */
    fluid.hashSync.listen = function (that, window) {
        const apply = fluid.cell.withAmbientSource("hash", () => {
            const parsed = fluid.parseUrlHash(window.location.hash);
            if (!fluid.hashSync.equivalent(fluid.renderUrlHash(parsed), fluid.renderUrlHash(that.hash))) {
                that.hash = parsed;
            }
        });
        window.addEventListener("hashchange", apply);
        window.addEventListener("popstate", apply);
        return {window, apply};
    };

    fluid.hashSync.unlisten = function (listener) {
        listener.window.removeEventListener("hashchange", listener.apply);
        listener.window.removeEventListener("popstate", listener.apply);
    };

    fluid.hashSync.pushState = function (hash, window) {
        const rendered = fluid.renderUrlHash(hash);
        if (!fluid.hashSync.equivalent(rendered, window.location.hash)) {
            window.history.pushState(null, null, rendered);
        }
    };

● I've built the Infusion 6 piece that lets a page start on the panel named in its URL, but I haven't started porting the story map itself yet. A page booted with `#pane:second` now computes and shows only that pane; it never renders the default first. Nothing is committed.
  
  ## How the URL becomes starting state
  
  - **`fluid-hash`:** a new attribute on the element that boots a component, e.g. `<div fluid-layers="..." fluid-hash="hash">`. Before the component is created, the framework decodes the URL's hash (`#pane:Status&taxon:…`, JSON allowed for values) into the starting value of that member. It becomes part of the component's creation record, so every value derived from it, and the first render, already reflects the URL. No project script is involved, because the decoder has to work before any SFC's scripts have loaded. Under node there is no hash, so a static rendering shows the defaults.
  - **`fluid.hashSync`:** a new layer that keeps that member and the URL in step afterwards. Navigating back writes the URL into it, and a change to it is pushed into the browser history. It doesn't read the URL again at startup, which is where the old render-then-jump came from.
  - **The test:** `npm run boot-hash-test` loads a page with `#pane:second` and logs every pane the component computes and every pane the page shows from the moment it's parsed. Both logs must read only `["second"]`. It also checks that selecting a pane updates the URL, going back restores the previous pane, and a page with no hash shows the default.
  
  ## Framework bugs fixed along the way
  
  - **Component proxies and symbols:** a component's state, read through its proxy, answered truthy for `Symbol.asyncIterator`. The signal graph then took a hash object for an async iterable and crashed. Symbol keys now read from the underlying value. This affects all components; the full Infusion suite (2,189 tests) still passes.
  - **Silent failure in URL writing:** URL rendering called `fluid.isValue`, which doesn't exist in Infusion 6, and the error inside the effect was swallowed, so nothing was written to the URL. Errors thrown inside effects being swallowed is worth fixing separately.
  
  A pitfall I documented: a component should read the decoded hash as a whole object. Reading a single key such as `.pane` gives an unavailable value when the URL lacks it, which holds up everything computed from it.
  
  The round trips, copy-out test and bagatelle's 155 tests still pass. ponder has a new section, "State held in the URL".
  
  ## One gap: the static page
  
  A page written by `hydrate.js` shows its default pane as soon as it's parsed, before the framework boots and switches to the URL's pane, so there is still a brief jump there. A one-line inline script can hide `[fluid-hash]` elements until boot whenever the URL has a hash; I'll add it when hydrating the story page.
  
  ## Plan for the story map (option 2)
  
  - **Where the code goes:** the shared story code moves to bagatelle as SFCs, so howe-sound and saanich take it through `copyOut.js`. `copyFrameworkOut.sh` keeps only the Hugo layouts and R files.
  - **Story page component:** hosted in a hand-written `layouts/story/single.html`, with `fluid-hash="hash"` and the `fluid.hashSync` layer. Its active pane is computed from the whole hash, so the section nav, pane visibility, map layers and camera, and data panes all render from the URL's pane first.
  - **Panes:** each knitted R page is fetched and parsed by a pane SFC. Its section markup and plotly widgets are rendered as-is, and its map layers are gathered into the shared map style. A project driver lists the pane keys; each pane's settings still come from its `.Rmd` front matter, so the R pipeline stays the single source.
  - **Build:** R knit, then Hugo, then `hydrate.js` over the built story page, which replaces `reknit.js`.
  - **Order:** `resizeBar`, `dataTable` and `taxonDisplay` first, then the panes and map, then the History slider and Solow controls.
  
  The knitted pages are 1.4–2.9MB each, mostly map JSON. Booting from the minimal page would fetch all of them, which is slow. The static page avoids that, so it is the form to deploy.


❯ go ahead with the story map port - although there's a lot of useful work done by reknit.js in discarding duplicate definitions so we may prefer to retain an explicit build step in the middle together with hydrate, depending what is meant by "the static page avoids that"

/* eslint-env node */
"use strict";

// Build the material of a story map from the HTML knitted from its R Markdown panes - the step between knitting and
// rendering the story page statically with Infusion 6's hydrate.js. In place of reknit.js, which wove the panes into
// a page template, this writes small files which the story page's Single File Components fetch:
//   - <out>/panes.json - one record per pane, in order of the `weight` of its front matter, holding its front matter,
//     its `paneKey`, the name of its file, and any members of its <viz_data>/<paneKey>-mapData.json
//   - <out>/<paneKey>.html - the section of each pane, without the pandoc page around it, and without the data of
//     its map widgets, which are folded into
//   - <out>/mapData.json - a single map style, holding every source and layer of every pane's map once, together
//     with the layers, camera and fill patterns of each pane
// Usage: node storyBuild.js <contentDir> <vizDataDir> <outDir>
// e.g. from a bioReportR project, node ../bagatelle/src/story/storyBuild.js content/story viz_data static/story

const fs = require("fs"),
    path = require("path"),
    yaml = require("js-yaml"),
    JSON5 = require("json5"),
    linkedom = require("linkedom");

const storyBuild = {};

/**
 * Parse the YAML front matter of an R Markdown file.
 * @param {String} text - The text of the file
 * @return {Object} The front matter, or an empty object if there is none
 */
storyBuild.frontMatter = function (text) {
    const match = text.match(/^---\r?\n([\s\S]*?)\r?\n---/);
    return match ? yaml.load(match[1]) : {};
};

/**
 * Find the panes of a story, in order of the weight of their front matter.
 * @param {String} contentDir - The directory holding each pane's .Rmd file and the .html knitted from it
 * @return {Object[]} A record for each pane, with members `paneKey`, `htmlFile` and `frontMatter`
 */
storyBuild.findPanes = function (contentDir) {
    const panes = fs.readdirSync(contentDir).filter(file => file.endsWith(".Rmd")).map(file => {
        const paneKey = path.basename(file, ".Rmd");
        const frontMatter = storyBuild.frontMatter(fs.readFileSync(path.join(contentDir, file), "utf8"));
        return {paneKey, htmlFile: path.join(contentDir, paneKey + ".html"), frontMatter};
    }).filter(pane => fs.existsSync(pane.htmlFile));
    return panes.sort((a, b) => (parseFloat(a.frontMatter.weight) || 0) - (parseFloat(b.frontMatter.weight) || 0));
};

/**
 * Create an empty accumulation of the maps of a story's panes.
 * @return {Object} The accumulation, with members `sources`, `layers` and `panes`, each keyed by id
 */
storyBuild.makeMapData = function () {
    return {sources: {}, layers: {}, fillPatterns: {}, panes: {}};
};

/**
 * Remove the map widgets from a pane, folding their sources and layers into the accumulated map data. Each source
 * and layer is held once, however many panes' maps hold it. The plotly widgets which are not maps are left in place.
 * @param {Element} container - The pane's markup
 * @param {String} paneKey - The pane's key
 * @param {Object} mapData - The accumulated map data
 */
storyBuild.extractMaps = function (container, paneKey, mapData) {
    [...container.querySelectorAll(".html-widget.plotly")].forEach(widget => {
        const dataNode = widget.id ? container.querySelector(`[data-for="${widget.id}"]`) : null;
        const mapbox = dataNode ? JSON.parse(dataNode.textContent)?.x?.layout?.mapbox : null;
        if (mapbox) {
            Object.assign(mapData.sources, mapbox.style.sources);
            const paneLayers = {};
            mapbox.style.layers.forEach(layer => {
                mapData.layers[layer.id] = layer;
                paneLayers[layer.id] = 1;
                const fillPattern = layer.paint?.["fill-pattern"];
                if (fillPattern) {
                    mapData.fillPatterns[fillPattern] = 1;
                }
            });
            mapData.panes[mapbox.style.id || paneKey] = {layers: paneLayers, center: mapbox.center, zoom: mapbox.zoom};
            widget.remove();
            dataNode.remove();
        }
    });
};

/**
 * Extract the section of a knitted pane, ready to be rendered by the story page. Its content other than its heading
 * is enclosed in a column, so that the page can lay it out beside the map, and any fixed dimensions are removed from
 * its plotly widgets, so that they can be resized.
 * @param {Document} document - The knitted pane
 * @param {String} paneKey - The pane's key
 * @param {Object} mapData - The accumulated map data, into which the pane's maps are folded
 * @return {String} The markup of the pane's section
 */
storyBuild.extractSection = function (document, paneKey, mapData) {
    const container = document.querySelector(".main-container");
    container.querySelector("#header")?.remove();
    container.querySelectorAll(".html-widget.plotly").forEach(widget => widget.removeAttribute("style"));
    storyBuild.extractMaps(container, paneKey, mapData);
    const section = container.querySelector(".section.level2");
    section.classList.add("mxcw-paneKey-" + paneKey);
    const children = [...section.childNodes].filter(node => node.tagName !== "H2");
    const inner = document.createElement("div");
    inner.setAttribute("class", "mxcw-sectionInner");
    const column = document.createElement("div");
    column.setAttribute("class", "mxcw-sectionColumn");
    children.forEach(child => column.appendChild(child));
    inner.appendChild(column);
    section.appendChild(inner);
    return section.outerHTML;
};

/**
 * Compose the accumulated map data into a single map style, with the layers highlighting a selection last.
 * @param {Object} mapData - The accumulated map data
 * @return {Object} The map data to be written, with members `style`, `panes` and `fillPatterns`
 */
storyBuild.composeMapData = function (mapData) {
    const layers = Object.values(mapData.layers);
    layers.sort((a, b) => (+a.id.endsWith("-highlight")) - (+b.id.endsWith("-highlight")));
    return {
        style: {version: 8, sources: mapData.sources, layers},
        panes: mapData.panes,
        fillPatterns: Object.keys(mapData.fillPatterns)
    };
};

/**
 * Read the members of a pane's map data file which configure its pane, and the ids of its selectable layers.
 * @param {String} vizDataDir - The directory holding each pane's <paneKey>-mapData.json
 * @param {String} paneKey - The pane's key
 * @return {Object} Members `view` and `regionField` of the file, if any, and `selectableRegions`, the ids of its
 * layers marked as selectable
 */
storyBuild.paneMapData = function (vizDataDir, paneKey) {
    const file = path.join(vizDataDir, paneKey + "-mapData.json");
    let togo = {};
    if (fs.existsSync(file)) {
        const plotData = JSON5.parse(fs.readFileSync(file, "utf8"));
        togo = {
            ...(plotData.view ? {view: plotData.view} : {}),
            ...(plotData.regionField ? {regionField: plotData.regionField} : {}),
            selectableRegions: (plotData.layers || []).filter(layer => layer.metadata?.selectable).map(layer => layer.id)
        };
    }
    return togo;
};

/**
 * Write a file, reporting its size.
 * @param {String} file - The file to be written
 * @param {String} text - Its text
 */
storyBuild.write = function (file, text) {
    fs.mkdirSync(path.dirname(file), {recursive: true});
    fs.writeFileSync(file, text, "utf8");
    console.log("Written " + Buffer.byteLength(text) + " bytes to " + file);
};

/**
 * Build the material of a story map.
 * @param {String} contentDir - The directory holding the panes' .Rmd files and the .html knitted from them
 * @param {String} vizDataDir - The directory holding the panes' map data files
 * @param {String} outDir - The directory to which the material is written
 * @return {Object[]} The records written to panes.json
 */
storyBuild.build = function (contentDir, vizDataDir, outDir) {
    const mapData = storyBuild.makeMapData();
    const panes = storyBuild.findPanes(contentDir).map(({paneKey, htmlFile, frontMatter}) => {
        const {document} = linkedom.parseHTML(fs.readFileSync(htmlFile, "utf8"));
        storyBuild.write(path.join(outDir, paneKey + ".html"), storyBuild.extractSection(document, paneKey, mapData) + "\n");
        const {knit, paneHandlerLayers, ...rest} = frontMatter;
        return {...rest, ...storyBuild.paneMapData(vizDataDir, paneKey), paneKey, file: paneKey + ".html",
            layers: paneHandlerLayers || []};
    });
    storyBuild.write(path.join(outDir, "panes.json"), JSON.stringify(panes, null, 2) + "\n");
    storyBuild.write(path.join(outDir, "mapData.json"), JSON.stringify(storyBuild.composeMapData(mapData)) + "\n");
    return panes;
};

module.exports = storyBuild;

if (require.main === module) {
    const [contentDir, vizDataDir, outDir] = process.argv.slice(2);
    if (outDir === undefined) {
        console.error("Usage: node storyBuild.js <contentDir> <vizDataDir> <outDir>");
        process.exitCode = 1;
    } else {
        storyBuild.build(contentDir, vizDataDir, outDir);
    }
}

● Bash: cat > /home/amb26/Source/gits/bagatelle/src/client/js/i6/story.js <<'EOF'
/*

You may obtain a copy of the ECL 2.0 License and BSD License at

"use strict";

// The story map of a bioReportR project, ported to Infusion 6 from reknit-client.js and imerss-viz-reknit.js of
// howe-sound-mapping-2026. Its panes are written by src/story/storyBuild.js from the HTML knitted from the project's
// R Markdown. The pane shown is held in the URL's hash, which is decoded before the story page is instantiated, so
// that everything which depends on the pane - its tab, its section, the map's layers and camera, the filters - is
// first rendered for the pane the URL names.

// noinspection ES6ConvertVarToLetConst // otherwise this is a duplicate on minifying
var reknitr = fluid.registerNamespace("reknitr");

// Namespaces of components defined in Single File Components, whose functions are defined here
fluid.registerNamespace("reknitr.storyPage");
fluid.registerNamespace("reknitr.storyPane");
fluid.registerNamespace("reknitr.storyMap");
fluid.registerNamespace("reknitr.pageFragment");

/**
 * The settings of a pane, which govern what the story page shows alongside it.
 * @typedef {Object} PaneSettings
 * @property {String} paneKey - The pane's key, the name of the R Markdown file it was knitted from
 * @property {String} title - The pane's title
 * @property {String} shortTitle - The pane's title as shown in its tab
 * @property {String} file - The file holding the pane's section, relative to the story's material
 * @property {String[]} layers - The names of the pane handler layers its front matter names, e.g. "reknitr.obsMapPaneHandler"
 * @property {Boolean} [visibleMap] - Whether the map is shown
 * @property {Boolean} [visibleGrid] - Whether the map's grid of observations is shown
 * @property {Boolean} [visibleFilters] - Whether the filters of observations are applied and shown
 * @property {Boolean} [visibleObsFilters] - Whether the panel of filters is shown
 * @property {Boolean} [visibleObsTable] - Whether the table of observations is shown
 * @property {Boolean} [visibleVizControls] - Whether the filters and checklist are shown
 * @property {Boolean} [visibleSolow] - Whether the controls of the extirpation risk analysis are shown
 * @property {String} [regionField] - The field of the region indirection table whose regions the pane's map shows
 * @property {String[]} [selectableRegions] - The ids of the layers of the pane's map which may be selected
 */

// The settings implied by each pane handler layer a pane's front matter may name, ported from the Infusion 4 grades
// of the same names
reknitr.paneLayerDefaults = {
    "reknitr.obsMapPaneHandler": {
        visibleMap: true,
        visibleGrid: true,
        visibleFilters: true,
        visibleObsFilters: true,
        visibleObsTable: true,
        visibleVizControls: true
    },
    "reknitr.solowPaneHandler": {
        visibleMap: true,
        visibleVizControls: true,
        visibleSolow: true
    }
};

reknitr.paneLayerDefaults["reknitr.statusPaneHandler"] = reknitr.paneLayerDefaults["reknitr.obsMapPaneHandler"];

/**
 * Compute the settings of each pane of a story, from the defaults of the layers named by its front matter, the front
 * matter itself, and any overrides supplied for it by the project.
 * @param {Object[]} paneRecords - The records of panes.json, as written by storyBuild.js
 * @param {Object<String, Object>} paneOverrides - Map of pane key to settings overriding those of the pane's record,
 * which may also name further layers
 * @return {PaneSettings[]} The settings of each pane, in order
 */
reknitr.storyPage.paneSettings = function (paneRecords, paneOverrides) {
    return paneRecords.map(record => {
        const override = paneOverrides[record.paneKey] || {};
        const layers = [...record.layers, ...(override.layers || [])];
        const defaults = Object.assign({}, ...layers.map(layer => reknitr.paneLayerDefaults[layer] || {}));
        return {...defaults, ...record, ...override, layers};
    });
};

/**
 * Determine the pane to be shown - the one named by the URL's hash, or else the first.
 * @param {Object} hash - The URL's hash, decoded
 * @param {PaneSettings[]} panes - The settings of each pane
 * @return {String} The key of the pane to be shown
 */
reknitr.storyPage.activePaneKey = function (hash, panes) {
    return panes.some(pane => pane.paneKey === hash.pane) ? hash.pane : panes[0].paneKey;
};

reknitr.storyPage.activePane = (panes, activePaneKey) => panes.find(pane => pane.paneKey === activePaneKey);

/**
 * Show a pane, writing it into the URL's hash. Any taxon selected for the previous pane is cleared, since it will not
 * suit another.
 * @param {reknitr.storyPage} that - The story page
 * @param {String} paneKey - The key of the pane to be shown
 */
reknitr.storyPage.selectPane = function (that, paneKey) {
    that.hash = {...that.hash, pane: paneKey, taxon: null};
};

reknitr.storyPage.isActive = (activePaneKey, paneKey) => activePaneKey === paneKey;

/**
 * Read the markup of a `<template>` element of the document holding a component, e.g. site navigation rendered into
 * the page by Hugo, which is to be rendered within the component's own template.
 * @param {Element} container - An element of the document
 * @param {String} templateId - The id of the `<template>` element
 * @return {String} The markup of its content, or the empty string if there is no such element
 */
reknitr.pageFragment.markup = function (container, templateId) {
    const template = container.ownerDocument.getElementById(templateId);
    return template ? template.innerHTML : "";
};

/**
 * Fetch the text of a file.
 * @param {String} url - The URL of the file
 * @return {Promise<String>} A promise for the file's text
 */
reknitr.fetchText = function (url) {
    return fetch(url).then(response => response.ok ? response.text() : Promise.reject(response.status + " " + response.statusText + " fetching " + url));
};

/**
 * Render any HTML widgets, e.g. plotly charts, within a pane which has been rendered, using the htmlwidgets library
 * which R's knitted output relies on. Each widget is rendered once.
 * @param {Element} container - The pane's rendered container
 * @param {Object} [HTMLWidgets] - The htmlwidgets library
 * @return {Element[]|Unavailable} The widgets rendered, or an unavailable value if the library is not loaded
 */
reknitr.storyPane.renderWidgets = function (container, HTMLWidgets) {
    let togo;
    if (HTMLWidgets) {
        HTMLWidgets.staticRender();
        togo = [...container.querySelectorAll(".html-widget")];
    } else {
        togo = fluid.unavailable({message: "The htmlwidgets library is not loaded", variety: "config"});
    }
    return togo;
};

/**
 * Show the layers of a story's map which belong to its active pane, by setting their opacity, and move the map's camera
 * to the pane's - jumping on the first occasion, and flying thereafter, slowly for a large change of zoom.
 * @param {reknitr.storyMap} that - The map
 * @param {maplibregl.Map} map - The map, once its style has applied
 * @param {Object} mapData - The story's map data, as written by storyBuild.js
 * @param {String} activePaneKey - The key of the active pane
 */
reknitr.storyMap.showPane = function (that, map, mapData, activePaneKey) {
    const paneMap = mapData.panes[activePaneKey];
    const visible = paneMap?.layers || {};
    mapData.style.layers.forEach(layer => {
        const opacityProp = reknitr.storyMap.opacityProperty(layer);
        if (opacityProp && map.getLayer(layer.id)) {
            map.setPaintProperty(layer.id, opacityProp, visible[layer.id] ? layer.paint?.[opacityProp] ?? 1 : 0);
        }
    });
    if (paneMap?.center) {
        if (that.hasCamera) {
            const zoomRatio = Math.abs(Math.log(map.getZoom() / paneMap.zoom));
            map.flyTo({center: paneMap.center, zoom: paneMap.zoom, essential: true,
                duration: zoomRatio > 0.3 ? that.slowZoomDuration : that.zoomDuration});
        } else {
            map.jumpTo({center: paneMap.center, zoom: paneMap.zoom});
            that.hasCamera = true;
        }
    }
};

reknitr.storyMap.opacityProperty = function (layer) {
    return {line: "line-opacity", fill: "fill-opacity", raster: "raster-opacity"}[layer.type] || null;
};

/**
 * Download the observations surviving the filters as CSV.
 * @param {Object[]} rows - The observations
 */
reknitr.storyPage.downloadObs = function (rows) {
    hortis.triggerDownload(Papa.unparse(rows), "text/csv;charset=utf-8;", "observations.csv");
};

// The map of the story page, whose style holds the layers of every pane's map, as gathered by storyBuild.js. The

// Filters observations to the taxa of a single reporting status - confirmed, historical (unconfirmed) or new. The
// status is held by the story page, since it is also chosen from the legend of a pane whose map is coloured by status
fluid.def("reknitr.statusFilter", {
    $layers: "hortis.obsFilter",
    filterName: "Status",
    filterState: "{storyPage}.selectedStatus",
    statusById: "$compute:hortis.blitzRecords.statusById({vizLoader}.taxa.rowById)",
    checked: "$compute:reknitr.statusFilter.checked({self}.filterState)",
    filterSummary: "$compute:hortis.collectorFilter.summarise({self}.filterState, {self}.filterName)",
    doFilter: "$method:reknitr.statusFilter.doFilter({0}:obsRows, {1}:filterState, {self}.statusById)",
    toggle: "$method:reknitr.statusFilter.toggle({storyPage}, {0}:status)",
    reset: "$method:reknitr.statusFilter.toggle({storyPage}, null)"
});

fluid.registerNamespace("reknitr.statusFilter");

reknitr.statusFilter.checked = function (filterState) {
    return {confirmed: filterState === "confirmed", unconfirmed: filterState === "unconfirmed", new: filterState === "new"};
};

reknitr.statusFilter.toggle = function (storyPage, status) {
    storyPage.selectedStatus = status === storyPage.selectedStatus ? null : status;
};

reknitr.statusFilter.doFilter = function (obsRows, filterState, statusById) {
    return filterState ? obsRows.filter(row => statusById[row.iNaturalistTaxonId] === filterState) : obsRows;
};

reknitr.statusFilter.click = function (event, that) {
    const input = event.target.closest("input[data-status]");
    if (input) {
        that.toggle(input.dataset.status);
    }
};
</script>

 * @param {Object[]} obsRows - The observations
 * @param {String|null} selectedRegion - The label of the selected region, or null if none is selected
 * @param {Object[]} indirectionRows - The rows of the region indirection table
 * @param {String[]} fieldNames - The columns of the table whose regions may be selected
 * @return {Object[]} The observations surviving the filter
 */
reknitr.regionSelectionFilter = function (obsRows, selectedRegion, indirectionRows, fieldNames) {
    const rows = selectedRegion ? indirectionRows.filter(row => row.label === selectedRegion && fieldNames.includes(row.regionField)) : [];
    return selectedRegion ? obsRows.filter(obsRow => rows.some(row => obsRow[row.regionField] === row.id)) : obsRows;
};

/**
 * Find the selectable region under a map event, if any.
 * @param {maplibregl.Map} map - The map
 * @param {Object} event - A MapLibre mouse event
 * @param {String[]} selectableRegions - The ids of the layers of the active pane which may be selected
 * @return {String|null} The id of the region's layer, or null if there is none
 */
reknitr.storyMap.eventToRegion = function (map, event, selectableRegions) {
    const features = map.queryRenderedFeatures(event.point);
    const match = features.find(feature => feature.layer.paint?.["fill-opacity"] > 0 && selectableRegions.includes(feature.layer.id));
    return match?.layer.id || null;
};

reknitr.storyMap.handleRegionClick = function (storyPage, map, event, selectableRegions) {
    const region = reknitr.storyMap.eventToRegion(map, event, selectableRegions);
    if (region) {
        storyPage.selectRegion(region);
    }
    return !!region;
};

/**
 * Outline the selected region on the map.
 * @param {maplibregl.Map} map - The map, once its style has applied
 * @param {String|null} selectedRegion - The id of the selected region's layer, whose source is of the same name
 */
reknitr.storyMap.highlightRegion = function (map, selectedRegion) {
    if (map.getLayer("region-highlight")) {
        map.removeLayer("region-highlight");
    }
    if (selectedRegion && map.getSource(selectedRegion)) {
        map.addLayer({id: "region-highlight", type: "line", source: selectedRegion, paint: {"line-color": "yellow", "line-width": 3}});
    }
};

/** Legend of regions or statuses **/

/**
 * Compute the rows of the legend of the active pane's map - one per status, for a pane whose map is coloured by
 * reporting status, or else one per region of the pane's region field.
 * @param {PaneSettings} pane - The active pane
 * @param {Object[]} indirectionRows - The rows of the region indirection table
 * @param {Object[]} styleLayers - The layers of the map's style
 * @return {Object[]} The rows, each with members `key`, `label`, `colour` and `selects`, the selection it makes -
 * "status" or "region"
 */
reknitr.storyMap.legendRows = function (pane, indirectionRows, styleLayers) {
    let togo = [];
    if (pane.regionField === "!statusAsRegion") {
        togo = Object.entries(pane.statusColors || {}).map(([label, colour]) => ({
            key: label === "historical" ? "unconfirmed" : label, label, colour, selects: "status"
        }));
    } else if (pane.regionField) {
        const layerById = Object.fromEntries(styleLayers.map(layer => [layer.id, layer]));
        togo = indirectionRows.filter(row => row.regionField === pane.regionField).map(row => ({
            key: row.label, label: row.label, colour: layerById[row.label]?.paint?.["fill-color"] || "transparent", selects: "region"
        }));
    }
    return togo;
};

/**
 * Render the markup of a legend.
 * @param {Object[]} rows - The legend's rows, as computed by `reknitr.storyMap.legendRows`
 * @param {String|null} selectedStatus - The selected reporting status, if any
 * @param {String|null} selectedRegion - The selected region, if any
 * @return {String} The legend's markup
 */
reknitr.storyMap.legendMarkup = function (rows, selectedStatus, selectedRegion) {
    return rows.map(row => {
        const selected = row.key === (row.selects === "status" ? selectedStatus : selectedRegion);
        return `<div class="imerss-legend-row${selected ? " imerss-selected" : ""}" data-key="${row.key}" data-selects="${row.selects}">` +
            "<span class=\"imerss-legend-icon\"></span>" +
            `<span class="imerss-legend-preview" style="background-color: ${row.colour}"></span>` +
            `<span class="imerss-legend-label">${row.label}</span></div>`;
    }).join("\n");
};

/**
 * Add an empty legend to a map as a control, whose rows select a status or region when clicked.
 * @param {maplibregl.Map} map - The map
 * @param {reknitr.storyPage} storyPage - The story page, whose selection the rows make
 * @param {Document} dokkument - The document holding the map
 * @return {Object} The control, whose `container` is the legend's element
 */
reknitr.storyMap.addRegionLegend = function (map, storyPage, dokkument) {
    const container = dokkument.createElement("div");
    container.classList.add("mxcw-legend", "mxcw-region-legend", "maplibregl-ctrl");
    container.addEventListener("click", event => {
        const row = event.target.closest("[data-key]");
        if (row && row.dataset.selects === "status") {
            storyPage.selectedStatus = row.dataset.key === storyPage.selectedStatus ? null : row.dataset.key;
        } else if (row) {
            storyPage.selectRegion(row.dataset.key);
        }
    });
    const control = {container, onAdd: () => container, onRemove: () => container.remove()};
    map.addControl(control, "bottom-right");
    return control;
};

reknitr.storyMap.renderRegionLegend = function (control, markup) {
    control.container.innerHTML = markup;
    hortis.toggleClass(control.container, "mxcw-hidden", !markup);
};

/** Carto keys **/

/**
 * Substitute the Carto API key into the tile URLs of any source of a style whose key includes "carto-" - the key for
 * localhost when the page is served from there, and otherwise the project's.
 * @param {Object} style - The map's style
 * @param {Object<String, String>} cartoKeys - Map of "localhost" and "imerss" to Carto API keys
 * @param {Location} location - The location of the page
 * @return {Object} The style, with the keys substituted
 */
reknitr.storyMap.styleWithCartoKeys = function (style, cartoKeys, location) {
    const key = cartoKeys[String(location?.href).includes("//localhost") ? "localhost" : "imerss"];
    const sources = fluid.transform(style.sources, (source, sourceKey) => sourceKey.includes("carto-") && source.tiles ?
        {...source, tiles: source.tiles.map(tile => hortis.stringTemplate(tile, {CARTO_API_KEY: key}))} : source);
    return {...style, sources};
};

● Bash: cd /home/amb26/Source/gits/bagatelle/src/client; cat > js/i6/dataTable.js <<'EOF'
/*
Copyright 2025-2026 Antranig Basman
Licensed under the Educational Community License (ECL), Version 2.0 or the New
BSD license. You may not use this file except in compliance with one these
Licenses.
You may obtain a copy of the ECL 2.0 License and BSD License at
https://github.com/fluid-project/infusion/raw/master/Infusion-LICENSE.txt
