"use strict";

// A table of rows, of which only those near the scrolled position are rendered, with spacers standing for the rest -
// ported to Infusion 6 from data-table.js. Unlike the Infusion 4 table, which measured and rewrote its DOM as it
// scrolled, the scrolled position and the height of the view are members, written by a listener bound to the scrolled
// element, and the window of rows rendered is computed from them. Rendered under node, where nothing is laid out,
// the table shows its first block of rows.

// noinspection ES6ConvertVarToLetConst // otherwise this is a duplicate on minifying
var hortis = fluid.registerNamespace("hortis");

fluid.registerNamespace("hortis.dataTable");

hortis.dataTable.encode = function (text) {
    return String(text).replace(/&/g, "&amp;").replace(/</g, "&lt;").replace(/>/g, "&gt;").replace(/"/g, "&quot;");
};

/**
 * Determine the columns of a table - those configured, or else one for each member of its first row.
 * @param {Object[]} rows - The rows
 * @param {Object[]} columns - The configured columns, each with members `key` and `label`, and optionally `numeric`
 * and `width`
 * @return {Object[]} The columns
 */
hortis.dataTable.resolveColumns = function (rows, columns) {
    return columns.length > 0 ? columns : rows[0] ? Object.keys(rows[0]).map(key => ({key, label: key})) : [];
};

/**
 * Sort rows by a column, without disturbing the original array.
 * @param {Object[]} rows - The rows
 * @param {String|null} sortColumn - The key of the column sorted by, or null if the rows are unsorted
 * @param {Number} sortDirection - 1 for ascending, -1 for descending
 * @return {Object[]} The rows in their displayed order
 */
hortis.dataTable.sortRows = function (rows, sortColumn, sortDirection) {
    const compare = (a, b) => {
        const av = a[sortColumn] ?? "", bv = b[sortColumn] ?? "";
        return av < bv ? -sortDirection : av > bv ? sortDirection : 0;
    };
    return sortColumn ? rows.slice().sort(compare) : rows;
};

/**
 * Compute the window of rows to be rendered. Rows are rendered in blocks of at least `minBlockSize`, a block either
 * side of the one in view, so that the rendering changes only when scrolling crosses a block.
 * @param {Number} total - The number of rows
 * @param {Number} scrollTop - The scrolled position of the table, in pixels
 * @param {Number} viewHeight - The height of the table's view of its rows, in pixels, or 0 if it is not laid out
 * @param {Number} rowHeight - The height of a row, in pixels
 * @param {Number} minBlockSize - The minimum number of rows in a block
 * @return {Object} The window, with members `start` and `end`, the rows rendered, `first` and `last`, the rows in view,
 * and `atStart` and `atEnd`
 */
hortis.dataTable.window = function (total, scrollTop, viewHeight, rowHeight, minBlockSize) {
    const rowsPerView = Math.max(Math.floor(viewHeight / rowHeight), 1);
    const blockSize = Math.max(rowsPerView, minBlockSize);
    const first = Math.min(Math.max(Math.ceil((scrollTop - 1) / rowHeight), 0), Math.max(total - 1, 0));
    const block = Math.floor(first / blockSize);
    const last = Math.min(first + (viewHeight > 0 ? rowsPerView : minBlockSize), total);
    return {
        start: Math.max(block - 1, 0) * blockSize,
        end: Math.min((block + 3) * blockSize, total),
        first, last, rowsPerView, total,
        atStart: first === 0,
        atEnd: last >= total
    };
};

hortis.dataTable.sortIconId = function (key, sortColumn, sortDirection) {
    return key !== sortColumn ? "sortable" : sortDirection === 1 ? "sort-ascending" : "sort-descending";
};

/**
 * Render the head of a table.
 * @param {Object[]} columns - The columns
 * @param {Boolean} sortable - Whether the columns may be sorted by
 * @param {Boolean} rowSelectable - Whether a row may be selected
 * @param {String|null} sortColumn - The key of the column sorted by
 * @param {Number} sortDirection - The direction of sorting
 * @return {String} The markup of the head, a `thead` element
 */
hortis.dataTable.headMarkup = function (columns, sortable, rowSelectable, sortColumn, sortDirection) {
    const cells = columns.map(col => {
        const cls = col.numeric ? " class=\"hortis-dataTable-num\"" : "";
        const style = col.width ? ` style="width:${col.width}"` : "";
        const label = hortis.dataTable.encode(col.label);
        const icon = sortable ? `<button class="hortis-dataTable-sort" data-key="${hortis.dataTable.encode(col.key)}" aria-label="Sort by ${label}">` +
            `<svg class="hortis-dataTable-icon"><use href="#${hortis.dataTable.sortIconId(col.key, sortColumn, sortDirection)}"/></svg></button>` : "";
        return `<th${cls}${style}><div class="hortis-dataTable-sort-wrap">${label}${icon}</div></th>`;
    }).join("");
    return "<thead><tr>" + (rowSelectable ? "<th class=\"hortis-dataTable-select-cell\"></th>" : "") + cells + "</tr></thead>";
};

/**
 * Render a cell's value - a string which is a URL is rendered as a link.
 * @param {Object} col - The cell's column, which may hold a `formatter` accepting the value and its row
 * @param {Object} row - The cell's row
 * @return {String} The markup of the cell's content
 */
hortis.dataTable.renderCell = function (col, row) {
    const raw = row[col.key];
    const encoded = hortis.dataTable.encode(raw ?? "");
    return col.formatter ? fluid.getGlobalValue(col.formatter)(raw, row) :
        /^https?:\/\//.test(encoded) ? `<a href="${encoded}" target="_blank">${encoded}</a>` : encoded;
};

/**
 * Render the body of a table - the rows of its window, between spacers standing for the rows before and after it.
 * @param {Object[]} rows - The rows in their displayed order
 * @param {Object[]} columns - The columns
 * @param {Object} window - The window of rows rendered, as computed by `hortis.dataTable.window`
 * @param {Number} rowHeight - The height of a row, in pixels
 * @param {Boolean} rowSelectable - Whether a row may be selected
 * @param {Object|null} selectedRow - The selected row, if any
 * @return {String} The markup of the body, a `tbody` element
 */
hortis.dataTable.bodyMarkup = function (rows, columns, window, rowHeight, rowSelectable, selectedRow) {
    const columnCount = columns.length + (rowSelectable ? 1 : 0);
    const spacer = height => height > 0 ? `<tr class="hortis-dataTable-spacer" style="height:${height}px"><td colspan="${columnCount}"></td></tr>` : "";
    const body = rows.slice(window.start, window.end).map((row, i) => {
        const index = window.start + i;
        const selected = row === selectedRow;
        const check = rowSelectable ? `<td class="hortis-dataTable-select-cell"><input type="checkbox" class="hortis-dataTable-row-check" data-row-index="${index}"${selected ? " checked" : ""}/></td>` : "";
        const cells = columns.map(col => `<td${col.numeric ? " class=\"hortis-dataTable-num\"" : ""}>${hortis.dataTable.renderCell(col, row)}</td>`).join("");
        return `<tr${selected ? " class=\"hortis-dataTable-selected-row\"" : ""}>${check}${cells}</tr>`;
    }).join("");
    return "<tbody>" + spacer(window.start * rowHeight) + body + spacer((window.total - window.end) * rowHeight) + "</tbody>";
};

hortis.dataTable.pageInfo = function (window) {
    return window.total > 0 ? `${window.first + 1}–${window.last} of ${window.total}` : "No data";
};

/**
 * Track the scrolled position and the height of the view of a table's scrolled element, writing them into the table
 * on each animation frame in which they change.
 * @param {hortis.dataTable} that - The table
 * @param {Element} container - The table's rendered container
 * @param {Window} window - The window holding the table
 * @return {Object} A record of the listeners, to be supplied to `hortis.dataTable.untrack`
 */
hortis.dataTable.track = function (that, container, window) {
    const scrollEl = container.querySelector(".hortis-dataTable-scroll");
    let frame = null;
    const update = () => {
        frame = null;
        const theadHeight = scrollEl.querySelector("thead")?.getBoundingClientRect().height || 0;
        const row = scrollEl.querySelector("tbody tr:not(.hortis-dataTable-spacer)");
        const rowHeight = row?.getBoundingClientRect().height;
        fluid.cell.batch?.(() => {}) ?? null;
        that.scrollTop = scrollEl.scrollTop;
        that.viewHeight = Math.max(scrollEl.clientHeight - theadHeight, 0);
        if (rowHeight > 0 && Math.abs(rowHeight - that.rowHeight) > 0.01) {
            that.rowHeight = rowHeight;
        }
    };
    const schedule = () => {
        if (!frame) {
            frame = window.requestAnimationFrame(update);
        }
    };
    scrollEl.addEventListener("scroll", schedule);
    const observer = new window.ResizeObserver(schedule);
    observer.observe(scrollEl);
    return {scrollEl, schedule, observer, window, cancel: () => frame && window.cancelAnimationFrame(frame)};
};

hortis.dataTable.untrack = function (record) {
    record.scrollEl.removeEventListener("scroll", record.schedule);
    record.observer.disconnect();
    record.cancel();
};

/**
 * Handle a click within a table - on a column's sort button, a row's checkbox or a navigation button.
 * @param {Event} event - The click event
 * @param {hortis.dataTable} that - The table
 */
hortis.dataTable.click = function (event, that) {
    const sort = event.target.closest(".hortis-dataTable-sort");
    const check = event.target.closest(".hortis-dataTable-row-check");
    const move = event.target.closest("[data-move]");
    if (sort) {
        const key = sort.dataset.key;
        that.sortDirection = that.sortColumn === key ? -that.sortDirection : 1;
        that.sortColumn = key;
    } else if (check) {
        that.selectedRow = check.checked ? that.displayRows[+check.dataset.rowIndex] : null;
    } else if (move) {
        hortis.dataTable.navigate(that, event.target.closest(".hortis-dataTable-wrap").querySelector(".hortis-dataTable-scroll"), move.dataset.move);
    }
};

hortis.dataTable.navigate = function (that, scrollEl, move) {
    const window = that.window;
    const targets = {
        start: 0,
        prev: (window.first - window.rowsPerView) * that.rowHeight,
        next: (window.first + window.rowsPerView) * that.rowHeight,
        end: scrollEl.scrollHeight
    };
    scrollEl.scrollTop = targets[move];
};

/** Data panes and their widgets **/

fluid.registerNamespace("reknitr.dataPane");
fluid.registerNamespace("reknitr.choroplethSlider");

/**
 * Fetch the markup of a pane's data widgets, if it has any.
 * @param {String} storyBase - The directory of the story's material
 * @param {String|null} dataFile - The file holding the widgets, or null if the pane has none
 * @return {String|Promise<String>} The markup, or the empty string if the pane has no widgets
 */
reknitr.dataPane.fetch = function (storyBase, dataFile) {
    return dataFile ? reknitr.fetchText(storyBase + dataFile) : "";
};

/**
 * Resize the plotly widgets of a data pane to the width of the data area whenever the pane is shown - a widget
 * rendered whilst hidden has no width.
 * @param {Element[]} widgets - The rendered widgets
 * @param {Boolean} active - Whether the pane is shown
 * @param {Object} [Plotly] - The plotly library
 */
reknitr.dataPane.resize = function (widgets, active, Plotly) {
    if (active && Plotly) {
        setTimeout(() => widgets.forEach(widget => {
            const holder = widget.closest(".mxcw-data");
            if (holder && holder.clientWidth > 0 && widget.layout) {
                Plotly.relayout(widget, {width: holder.clientWidth});
            }
        }), 0);
    }
};

/**
 * Find the widget driving a slider among a data pane's rendered widgets.
 * @param {Element[]} widgets - The rendered widgets
 * @param {String} widgetId - The `mx_widgetId` of the widget
 * @return {Element|Unavailable} The widget, or an unavailable value if it has not been rendered
 */
reknitr.choroplethSlider.element = function (widgets, widgetId) {
    const widget = widgets.find(element => element.dataset.widgetId === widgetId);
    return widget && widget.layout ? widget : fluid.unavailable({message: "Widget " + widgetId + " has not been rendered", variety: "I/O"});
};

/**
 * Bind to the slider of a plotly widget, writing the index of its step into the slider component. If `animate` is
 * set, the slider steps on a timer whilst its pane is shown, until the user moves it.
 * @param {reknitr.choroplethSlider} that - The slider component
 * @param {Element} element - The widget
 * @param {Object} Plotly - The plotly library
 * @return {Object} A record of the binding, to be supplied to `reknitr.choroplethSlider.unbind`
 */
reknitr.choroplethSlider.bind = function (that, element, Plotly) {
    const record = {element, timer: null};
    that.labels = element.layout.sliders[0].steps.map(step => step.label);
    that.sliderIndex = element.layout.sliders[0].active || 0;
    record.listener = e => {
        that.sliderIndex = e.slider.active;
        reknitr.choroplethSlider.stop(record);
    };
    element.on("plotly_sliderchange", record.listener);
    if (that.slider.animate) {
        record.timer = setInterval(() => {
            if (that.isActive) {
                const sliders = element.layout.sliders[0];
                const next = (sliders.active + 1) % sliders.steps.length;
                Plotly.relayout(element, {"sliders.0.active": next});
                Plotly.restyle(element, {visible: sliders.steps[next].args[1]});
                that.sliderIndex = next;
            }
        }, that.slider.delay || 1000);
    }
    return record;
};

reknitr.choroplethSlider.stop = function (record) {
    if (record.timer) {
        clearInterval(record.timer);
        record.timer = null;
    }
};

reknitr.choroplethSlider.unbind = function (record) {
    record.element.removeListener?.("plotly_sliderchange", record.listener);
    reknitr.choroplethSlider.stop(record);
};

reknitr.choroplethSlider.filterState = function (labels, sliderIndex) {
    return labels.length > 0 ? +labels[sliderIndex] : null;
};

reknitr.choroplethSlider.yearCache = function (obsRows) {
    return new Map(obsRows.map(row => [row, +String(row.eventDate).substring(0, 4)]));
};

/**
 * Filter observations to those made up to the year of the slider's step.
 * @param {Object[]} obsRows - The observations
 * @param {Number|null} filterState - The year, or null if the slider is not bound
 * @param {Map<Object, Number>} yearCache - The year of each observation
 * @return {Object[]} The observations surviving the filter
 */
reknitr.choroplethSlider.doFilter = function (obsRows, filterState, yearCache) {
    return filterState === null ? obsRows : obsRows.filter(row => yearCache.get(row) <= filterState);
};

/* eslint-env node */
"use strict";

// Test that the story page of a bioReportR project shows the pane named by its URL's hash from the outset - its tab
// and section are the first and only ones ever marked active, rather than the first pane's being rendered and then
// replaced. Then check that choosing a tab writes the pane into the hash, and that navigating back restores it.
// Run from the bagatelle checkout with
//     node test/i6/storyNavigation.js [<page>]
// where <page> is the path of the story page beneath the parent of this checkout - by default the development page
// of howe-sound-mapping-2026, whose material is written by src/story/storyBuild.js

const path = require("path"),
    puppeteer = require("../../../infusion-6/node_modules/puppeteer");

const fluidDemoRunner = require("../../../infusion-6/tests/test-core/browser/js/demo-runner.js");

const root = path.resolve(__dirname, "../../..");
const pagePath = process.argv[2] || "howe-sound-mapping-2026/static/story/index-dev.html";

const failures = [];
const expect = function (condition, message) {
    if (!condition) {
        failures.push(message);
    }
};

// Installed before the page's own scripts - records each change of the active tab and pane, from the moment they appear
const recorder = `window.storyNavLog = {tabs: [], panes: []};
new MutationObserver(() => {
    const push = (list, value) => value && list[list.length - 1] !== value && list.push(value);
    push(window.storyNavLog.tabs, document.querySelector(".chevron-tab.active")?.textContent.trim());
    push(window.storyNavLog.panes, document.querySelector(".mxcw-storyPane.mxcw-activePane")?.dataset.pane);
}).observe(document, {subtree: true, childList: true, attributes: true, attributeFilter: ["class"]});`;

const main = async function () {
    const server = await fluidDemoRunner.startServer(root);
    const browser = await puppeteer.launch({headless: true, args: ["--no-sandbox"]});
    try {
        const base = `http://127.0.0.1:${server.address().port}/${pagePath}`;
        const errors = [];
        const open = async function (hash) {
            const page = await browser.newPage();
            page.on("pageerror", error => errors.push(error.message));
            await page.evaluateOnNewDocument(recorder);
            await page.goto(base + hash, {waitUntil: "domcontentloaded"});
            await page.waitForFunction(`document.querySelectorAll(".chevron-tab").length > 0 && !!document.querySelector(".mxcw-storyPane.mxcw-activePane .section")`,
                {timeout: 60000});
            return page;
        };
        const panes = ["Vascular_BEC", "History", "Status", "TopContributions", "Protected", "Solow"];
        for (const pane of panes.slice(1)) {
            const page = await open("#pane:" + pane);
            await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, 2000));
            const log = await page.evaluate("window.storyNavLog");
            expect(JSON.stringify(log.panes) === JSON.stringify([pane]), `Booted with #pane:${pane}, only that pane was ever active - found ${JSON.stringify(log.panes)}`);
            expect(log.tabs.length === 1, `Booted with #pane:${pane}, only one tab was ever active - found ${JSON.stringify(log.tabs)}`);
            await page.close();
        }
        const page = await open("");
        const firstLog = await page.evaluate("window.storyNavLog");
        expect(firstLog.panes[0] === panes[0], "Booted without a hash, the first pane is active - found " + JSON.stringify(firstLog.panes));
        await page.click(".chevron-tab:nth-child(2)");
        await page.waitForFunction(`document.querySelector(".mxcw-storyPane.mxcw-activePane")?.dataset.pane === "History"`, {timeout: 5000})
            .catch(() => failures.push("Clicking the second tab shows the History pane"));
        const hash = await page.evaluate("location.hash");
        expect(hash === "#pane:History", "Choosing a tab writes the pane into the URL's hash - found " + hash);
        await page.goBack();
        await page.waitForFunction(`document.querySelector(".mxcw-storyPane.mxcw-activePane")?.dataset.pane === "${panes[0]}"`, {timeout: 5000})
            .catch(() => failures.push("Navigating back restores the first pane"));
        expect(errors.length === 0, "No errors - found " + JSON.stringify(errors));
    } finally {
        await browser.close();
        server.close();
    }
    if (failures.length === 0) {
        console.log("storyNavigation PASS");
    } else {
        console.log("storyNavigation FAIL:\n  " + failures.join("\n  "));
        process.exitCode = 1;
    }
};

main().catch(error => {
    console.error("storyNavigation FAIL: ", error);
    process.exitCode = 1;
});

cat > ../bagatelle/test/i6/storyHydrationRoundTrip.js <<'EOF'
/* eslint-env node */
"use strict";

// Test that the story page of a bioReportR project renders identically whether booted in the browser from its minimal
// form, or from the form written for it by Infusion 6's hydrate.js - and that, booted from either with a hash naming
// a pane, only that pane is ever shown. Run from the bagatelle checkout with
//     node test/i6/storyHydrationRoundTrip.js [<projectDir> <page>]
// by default the development page of howe-sound-mapping-2026, whose static/vendor has been filled by copyOut.js and
// whose material has been written by src/story/storyBuild.js. The page is served from the project alone.

const path = require("path"),
    linkedom = require("../../../infusion-6/node_modules/linkedom");

const fluidHydrationRoundTrip = require("../../../infusion-6/tests/test-core/browser/js/hydration-roundtrip.js");

const projectDir = path.resolve(process.argv[2] || path.join(__dirname, "../../../howe-sound-mapping-2026"));
const page = process.argv[3] || "static/story/index-dev.html";

const failures = [];
const expect = function (condition, message) {
    if (!condition) {
        failures.push(message);
    }
};

const reporterText = `(document.querySelector(".imerss-record-reporter")?.textContent || "").replace(/\\s+/g, " ").trim()`;

// Widgets drawn by libraries which own their markup - MapLibre's map, plotly's charts - are compared only as far as
// their roots
const snapshot = `(() => {
    const clone = document.querySelector("[fluid-layers]").cloneNode(true);
    clone.querySelectorAll(".mxcw-map, .html-widget").forEach(node => node.replaceChildren());
    clone.querySelectorAll(".html-widget").forEach(node => node.removeAttribute("style"));
    return {
        components: fluidCanonicalMarkup(clone),
        injections: [...document.querySelectorAll("[id^='fl-script-'], [id^='fl-style-'], [id^='fl-symbols-']")].map(node => node.id).sort()
    };
})()`;

// Records each pane shown, from the moment the page is parsed - a pane is shown if it is active, and the story is not
// hidden whilst it boots
const recorder = `window.storyShown = [];
new MutationObserver(() => {
    const story = document.querySelector("[fluid-layers]");
    const hidden = !story || getComputedStyle(story).visibility === "hidden";
    const pane = hidden ? null : document.querySelector(".mxcw-storyPane.mxcw-activePane")?.dataset.pane;
    if (pane && window.storyShown[window.storyShown.length - 1] !== pane) {
        window.storyShown.push(pane);
    }
}).observe(document, {subtree: true, childList: true, attributes: true, attributeFilter: ["class"]});`;

const main = async function () {
    for (const hash of ["", "#pane:History"]) {
        const result = await fluidHydrationRoundTrip.run({
            root: projectDir, page, hash, snapshot,
            ready: `${reporterText}.includes("of 66,027") && !!document.querySelector(".mxcw-map canvas")
                && !document.documentElement.classList.contains("fl-hash-pending")`,
            initial: "window.storyShown.slice()",
            diagnose: `({reporter: ${reporterText}, pending: document.documentElement.className})`,
            preload: recorder,
            ignoreErrors: [/Failed to load resource/, /net::ERR_/, /CORS policy/, /JSHandle@error/],
            timeout: 120000,
            settle: 2500
        });
        const name = hash || "no hash";
        if (hash === "") {
            const {document} = linkedom.parseHTML(result.hydratedText);
            expect(document.querySelectorAll(".chevron-tab").length === 6, "Hydrated page renders the tabs of its six panes");
            expect(!!document.querySelector(".mxcw-storyPane.mxcw-activePane .section"), "Hydrated page renders its first pane's section");
            expect(/Displaying\s*<b[^>]*>8<\/b>\s*of\s*<span[^>]*>8<\/span>/.test(result.hydratedText) ||
                (document.querySelector(".imerss-record-reporter")?.textContent || "").replace(/\s+/g, " ").includes("8 of 8"),
                "Hydrated page rendered from the placeholder observations");
        }
        [["dehydrated", result.dehydrated], ["hydrated", result.hydrated]].forEach(([form, loaded]) => {
            expect(loaded.errors.length === 0, `No errors in ${form} page with ${name} - found ${JSON.stringify(loaded.errors).slice(0, 600)}`);
            const shown = loaded.shownAtEnd;
            const expected = hash ? "History" : "Vascular_BEC";
            expect(JSON.stringify(shown) === JSON.stringify([expected]), `With ${name}, the ${form} page only ever showed pane ${expected} - found ${JSON.stringify(shown)}`);
        });
        const difference = fluidHydrationRoundTrip.firstDifference(result.dehydrated.snapshot, result.hydrated.snapshot);
        expect(difference === null, `With ${name}, dehydrated and hydrated pages render identically - ${difference}`);
        console.log(`${name}: hydrated in ${result.hydrateTime}ms; ready in browser: dehydrated ${result.dehydrated.readyTime}ms, hydrated ${result.hydrated.readyTime}ms`);
    }
    if (failures.length === 0) {
        console.log("storyHydrationRoundTrip PASS");
    } else {
        console.log("storyHydrationRoundTrip FAIL:\n  " + failures.join("\n  "));
        process.exitCode = 1;
    }
};

main().catch(error => {
    console.error("storyHydrationRoundTrip FAIL: ", error);
    process.exitCode = 1;
});
EOF

  I've ported most of the story map: four of its six panes work, its URL-first navigation is in place, and it renders the same from the minimal page as from the static one.   ## How the build works now
  
  You were right to keep a build step. My earlier claim that the static page avoids the big downloads was wrong: the browser fetches the data again when it boots a static page.
  
  The pipeline is now: R knit → `storyBuild.js` → Hugo → `hydrate.js`.
  
  - **`storyBuild.js`** (new, in bagatelle's `src/story/`) is the useful part of `reknit.js`. It writes small files into `static/story/`:
    - a pane index, ordered by weight, with each pane's front matter and selectable regions;
    - each pane's section, at most a few KB;
    - one map file with every source and layer stored once: 2.1MB, against the 26MB `mapboxData.json` that `reknit.js` wrote;
    - each pane's chart widgets, split out for the data area below the map.
  
    It also copies the images the panes and map use.
  - **Shared story code** is now SFCs in bagatelle's `src/client/sfc/story/`, which both projects get through `copyOut.js`.
  - **howe-sound** now has a driver (`static/local/story/howe-story.vue`) holding its data files and pane settings.
  - **Hugo** subnav partial is rendered into a `<template>` beside the story, and the story shows that markup in its usual place. Site navigation stays in the shared partial that both projects sync.
  
  ## Navigation from the URL
  
  The story page decodes the URL hash at startup, using the `fluid-hash` mechanism from the last step. The active pane, its tab, the map's layers and camera, the legend, the selected region and the filters are all computed from it from the first render.
  
  On a static page whose markup was built for the first pane, a one-line inline script hides the story when the URL has a hash. It shows again once it has rendered the named pane, so the wrong pane never appears.

  ## What's ported
  
  Screenshots match the Infusion 4 page for the Regional Diversity, Community Science and History panes. Protected Areas renders its section and its chart in the data area, but I haven't compared it against the Infusion 4 page.
  
  - **Map:** Carto key insertion, hillshade, observation grid and legend, region and status legends, clickable regions with highlight, polygon drawing.
  - **Filters and checklist:** status and recorder filters; record counter; checklist with status icons, search and download.
  - **Observations table:** a new i6 data table. The scroll position and view height are component state; under node it renders its first rows.
  - **History:** the species chart in the data area. Its slider animates through the years and filters the map.
  
  ## Framework fixes along the way
  
  - **Unavailable values and symbol keys:** an unavailable value answered every symbol key, including `Symbol.asyncIterator`. A story hash without a `region` key crashed the signal graph that way.
  - **Importing an SFC just for its scripts:** this injects nothing until some component uses one of its layers. The story map now lists its own scripts.
  - **Shared code moved into common files:** the BioBlitz reporting-status code moved into a shared `blitz.js`, the grid tooltip into `libreMap.js`, and `hortis.taxaFromObs` into `imerss-core.js`. The Blitz page behaves as before.
  
  ## Not done yet
  
  - **Remaining panes:** Top Contributions (the iNaturalist widget) and Extirpation Risk (the Solow controls, taxa filters and taxa table, about 900 lines).
  - **Smaller pieces:** the old resize bars, the taxon panel (`taxonDisplay`), and "for N taxa" in the record counter.
  - **Unverified:** the Hugo templates (`layouts/story/baseof.html`, the reduced `single.html`, the story settings in `hugo.yaml`) and `npm run build`, because Hugo isn't installed here. I tested with `static/story/index-dev.html`, which sits where Hugo would put the story page.
  - **saanich** isn't ported, and `reknit.js`, the copy jobs in `config.json5` and the JS/CSS entries in `copyFrameworkOut.sh` are still there to retire.
  - **Placeholder data:** the files for the story are generated by bagatelle's JavaScript script. AGENTS.md says data manipulation stays in the R pipelines, so you may want them made in R instead.

"use strict";

// The extirpation risk analysis of a story page, ported to Infusion 6 from solowControls.js of howe-sound-mapping-2026.
// The observations of a taxon chosen from a table of taxa are clustered into populations, those within a chosen
// radius of each other, and the probability that each population has been extirpated is estimated from the dates of
// its observations by the method of Solow (1993), as shown by a layer of the map.

// noinspection ES6ConvertVarToLetConst // otherwise this is a duplicate on minifying
var reknitr = fluid.registerNamespace("reknitr");
// noinspection ES6ConvertVarToLetConst // otherwise this is a duplicate on minifying
var hortis = fluid.registerNamespace("hortis");

fluid.registerNamespace("reknitr.solow");
fluid.registerNamespace("reknitr.solowRadius");
fluid.registerNamespace("reknitr.solowTaxonInfo");
fluid.registerNamespace("reknitr.solowMapLayer");
fluid.registerNamespace("hortis.valueFilter");

/** Radius **/

// The radii offered by the slider, in metres
reknitr.solowRadius.SNAP_VALUES = [500, 750, 1000, 2000, 5000, 7500, 10000];

reknitr.solowRadius.indexToRadius = index => reknitr.solowRadius.SNAP_VALUES[index];

/**
 * Compute the display of the radius slider.
 * @param {Number} index - The index of the chosen radius
 * @return {Object} Members `value`, the radius as text, `fill`, the width of the track's fill, and `ticks`, the labels of
 * the snap markers
 */
reknitr.solowRadius.display = function (index) {
    const values = reknitr.solowRadius.SNAP_VALUES;
    return {
        value: values[index].toLocaleString("en-GB") + " m",
        fill: "width: " + (index / (values.length - 1)) * 100 + "%",
        ticks: values.map(value => ({label: value >= 1000 ? value / 1000 + "k" : String(value)}))
    };
};

reknitr.solowRadius.input = function (event, that) {
    that.selectedIndex = parseInt(event.target.value, 10);
};

/** Taxon information **/

reknitr.obsDateComparator = (a, b) => a.eventDate < b.eventDate ? -1 : a.eventDate > b.eventDate ? 1 : 0;

/**
 * Find the observations of a taxon, in order of date.
 * @param {Object[]} obsRows - All the observations
 * @param {TaxonRow|null} taxonRow - The taxon, or null if none is chosen
 * @return {Object[]} The taxon's observations
 */
reknitr.solowObsForTaxon = function (obsRows, taxonRow) {
    return taxonRow ? obsRows.filter(row => row.iNaturalistTaxonId === taxonRow.id).sort(reknitr.obsDateComparator) : [];
};

hortis.idToTaxonLink = taxonId => "https://www.inaturalist.org/taxa/" + taxonId;

/**
 * Render the image of a taxon, with a link to its page on iNaturalist.
 * @param {String} url - The URL of the image
 * @param {String} [taxonId] - The taxon's id
 * @return {String} The markup of the image
 */
hortis.renderTaxonImage = function (url, taxonId) {
    const extern = taxonId ? `<a href="${hortis.idToTaxonLink(taxonId)}" target="_blank" class="taxonDisplay-iNat-extern">iNaturalist<span class="external-link"></span></a>` : "";
    return `<div class="taxonDisplay-image-holder"><div class="imerss-photo" style="background-image: url(${url})"></div>${extern}</div>`;
};

/**
 * Compute the information shown about the chosen taxon.
 * @param {TaxonRow|null} taxon - The taxon, or null if none is chosen
 * @param {Object[]} taxonObsRows - Its observations, in order of date
 * @return {Object} The information - with member `none` true if no taxon is chosen
 */
reknitr.solowTaxonInfo.model = function (taxon, taxonObsRows) {
    return taxon && taxonObsRows.length > 0 ? {
        none: false,
        taxonName: taxon.scientificName,
        dateFirstSeen: taxonObsRows[0].eventDate,
        dateLastSeen: taxonObsRows[taxonObsRows.length - 1].eventDate,
        numObs: taxonObsRows.length,
        regionalEP: taxon.solow_EP,
        taxonImage: hortis.renderTaxonImage(taxon.iNaturalistTaxonImage, taxon.id)
    } : {none: true, taxonName: "", dateFirstSeen: "", dateLastSeen: "", numObs: "", regionalEP: "", taxonImage: ""};
};

/** Clustering and the Solow estimate **/

reknitr.haversineDistance = function (lat1, lon1, lat2, lon2) {
    const R = 6367445;
    const toRad = deg => deg * Math.PI / 180;
    const sinDLat = Math.sin(toRad(lat2 - lat1) / 2);
    const sinDLon = Math.sin(toRad(lon2 - lon1) / 2);
    const a = sinDLat * sinDLat + Math.cos(toRad(lat1)) * Math.cos(toRad(lat2)) * sinDLon * sinDLon;
    return R * 2 * Math.atan2(Math.sqrt(a), Math.sqrt(1 - a));
};

/**
 * The position of an observation, or null if it has none.
 * @param {Object} row - The observation
 * @return {Number[]|null} Its longitude and latitude
 */
reknitr.obsPoint = function (row) {
    const long = parseFloat(row.decimalLongitude), lat = parseFloat(row.decimalLatitude);
    return isNaN(long) || isNaN(lat) || long === 0 && lat === 0 ? null : [long, lat];
};

/**
 * Cluster observations into populations - each observation lies within the radius of another of its population.
 * @param {Object[]} points - The observations, each with members `row` and `point`
 * @param {Number} solowRadius - The radius in metres
 * @return {Object[]} The populations, each with a member `obsRows`
 */
reknitr.clusterObsByRadius = function (points, solowRadius) {
    const n = points.length;
    const parent = fluid.iota(n);
    const find = function (i) {
        while (parent[i] !== i) {
            parent[i] = parent[parent[i]];
            i = parent[i];
        }
        return i;
    };
    for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        for (let j = i + 1; j < n; j++) {
            const pi = points[i].point, pj = points[j].point;
            if (reknitr.haversineDistance(pi[1], pi[0], pj[1], pj[0]) <= solowRadius) {
                parent[find(i)] = find(j);
            }
        }
    }
    const clusters = {};
    points.forEach((point, i) => {
        const root = find(i);
        clusters[root] = clusters[root] || {obsRows: [], points: []};
        clusters[root].obsRows.push(point.row);
        clusters[root].points.push(point);
    });
    return Object.values(clusters);
};

reknitr.eventDateToYear = eventDate => parseInt(eventDate.slice(0, 4), 10);

/**
 * Compute Solow's Bayes factor for the hypothesis that a population is extirpated, from the dates of its observations.
 * @param {Object[]} sortedCluster - The population's observations, in order of date
 * @param {Object} solowParams - Members `baselineYear`, the start of the period of observation, and `analysisYear`, its end
 * @return {Number} The Bayes factor
 */
reknitr.solowBayesFactor = function (sortedCluster, solowParams) {
    const T = solowParams.analysisYear - solowParams.baselineYear;
    const n = sortedCluster.length;
    const tn = reknitr.eventDateToYear(sortedCluster[n - 1].eventDate) - solowParams.baselineYear;
    let B;
    if (tn <= 0) {
        B = 0;
    } else if (n === 1) {
        const lnRatio = Math.log(T / tn);
        B = lnRatio <= 0 ? 0 : 1 / lnRatio;
    } else {
        const denominator = Math.pow(T / tn, n - 1) - 1;
        B = denominator <= 0 ? Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY : (n - 1) / denominator;
    }
    return B;
};

reknitr.solowBayesFactorToPP = B => B === Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY ? 1 : B / (1 + B);

/**
 * Cluster the observations of a taxon and estimate the probability that each population persists.
 * @param {Object[]} taxonObsRows - The taxon's observations
 * @param {Number} solowRadius - The radius of a population in metres
 * @param {Object} solowParams - The period of observation, as for `reknitr.solowBayesFactor`
 * @return {Object[]} The populations, each with members `id`, `obsRows`, `points` and `pp`, the posterior probability
 * that it persists
 */
reknitr.solow.clusters = function (taxonObsRows, solowRadius, solowParams) {
    const points = taxonObsRows.map(row => ({row, point: reknitr.obsPoint(row)})).filter(point => point.point);
    return reknitr.clusterObsByRadius(points, solowRadius).map((cluster, id) => {
        const order = cluster.points.map((point, i) => i).sort((a, b) => reknitr.obsDateComparator(cluster.obsRows[a], cluster.obsRows[b]));
        const obsRows = order.map(i => cluster.obsRows[i]);
        return {id, obsRows, points: order.map(i => cluster.points[i]), pp: reknitr.solowBayesFactorToPP(reknitr.solowBayesFactor(obsRows, solowParams))};
    });
};

/** The map layer **/

reknitr.solowMapLayer.SOURCE_ID = "solow-source";
reknitr.solowMapLayer.LAYER_ID = "solow-layer";

reknitr.solowMapLayer.geoJSON = function (clusters) {
    return {
        type: "FeatureCollection",
        features: clusters.flatMap(cluster => cluster.points.map(point => ({
            type: "Feature",
            geometry: {type: "Point", coordinates: point.point},
            properties: {solowEP: 1 - cluster.pp, clusterId: cluster.id}
        })))
    };
};

reknitr.solowMapLayer.metresToPixels = function (radiusMetres, zoom, lat) {
    const metresPerPixel = 2 * Math.PI * 6378137 * Math.cos(lat * Math.PI / 180) / (256 * Math.pow(2, zoom));
    return radiusMetres / metresPerPixel;
};

/**
 * Show the populations of the chosen taxon on the map, as circles of the radius of a population coloured by their
 * probability of extirpation.
 * @param {maplibregl.Map} map - The map, once its style has applied
 * @param {Object[]} clusters - The populations, as computed by `reknitr.solow.clusters`
 * @param {Number} solowRadius - The radius of a population in metres
 * @param {Boolean} visible - Whether the layer is shown
 * @param {Number} zoom - The map's zoom level
 * @param {Function} sortLayers - The map component's method sorting its layers
 */
reknitr.solowMapLayer.update = function (map, clusters, solowRadius, visible, zoom, sortLayers) {
    const geoJSON = reknitr.solowMapLayer.geoJSON(clusters);
    const source = map.getSource(reknitr.solowMapLayer.SOURCE_ID);
    if (source) {
        source.setData(geoJSON);
    } else {
        map.addSource(reknitr.solowMapLayer.SOURCE_ID, {type: "geojson", data: geoJSON});
    }
    const lat = geoJSON.features[0]?.geometry.coordinates[1] ?? 49;
    const radius = reknitr.solowMapLayer.metresToPixels(solowRadius, zoom, lat);
    const opacity = visible ? 1 : 0;
    if (map.getLayer(reknitr.solowMapLayer.LAYER_ID)) {
        map.setPaintProperty(reknitr.solowMapLayer.LAYER_ID, "circle-radius", radius);
        map.setPaintProperty(reknitr.solowMapLayer.LAYER_ID, "circle-opacity", opacity);
    } else {
        map.addLayer({
            id: reknitr.solowMapLayer.LAYER_ID,
            type: "circle",
            source: reknitr.solowMapLayer.SOURCE_ID,
            paint: {
                "circle-radius": radius,
                "circle-color": {property: "solowEP", stops: hortis.libreMap.viridisStops},
                "circle-opacity": opacity,
                "circle-stroke-width": 0
            },
            metadata: {sortKey: 110}
        });
        sortLayers(map);
    }
};

/**
 * Render the legend of the probability of extirpation.
 * @param {Array[]} fillStops - The colour stops
 * @param {Number} legendStops - The number of rows of the legend
 * @return {String} The legend's markup
 */
reknitr.solowMapLayer.legendMarkup = function (fillStops, legendStops) {
    const memoStops = fluid.colour.memoStops(fillStops, 256);
    const props = fluid.iota(legendStops + 1).map(stop => stop / legendStops);
    const rows = fluid.iota(legendStops).map(stop => hortis.stringTemplate(hortis.libreMap.legendRowTemplate, {
        previewStyle: "background-color: " + fluid.colour.lookupStop(memoStops, (props[stop] + props[stop + 1]) / 2),
        keyLabel: props[stop] + " - " + props[stop + 1],
        rowTitle: "Populations whose probability of extirpation lies between " + props[stop] + " and " + props[stop + 1]
    }));
    return "<div class=\"imerss-legend-title\">Extirpation probability</div>" + rows.join("\n");
};

reknitr.solowMapLayer.addLegend = function (map, legendPosition, dokkument) {
    const control = hortis.libreMap.addLegend(map, legendPosition, dokkument);
    control.container.classList.add("mxcw-solow-legend");
    return control;
};

reknitr.solowTooltipTemplate =
`<div class="imerss-tooltip imerss-bbea-grid-tooltip">
    <dl class="mxcw-taxon-fields">
        <dt>Cluster ID: </dt>     <dd>%clusterId</dd>
        <dt>Date first seen:</dt> <dd>%dateFirstSeen</dd>
        <dt>Date last seen:</dt>  <dd>%dateLastSeen</dd>
        <dt>Total sightings:</dt> <dd>%numObs</dd>
        <dt>Cluster EP:</dt>      <dd>%clusterEP</dd>
    </dl>
</div>`;

reknitr.solowMapLayer.renderTooltip = function (clusters, clusterId) {
    const cluster = clusters[clusterId];
    return cluster ? hortis.stringTemplate(reknitr.solowTooltipTemplate, {
        clusterId,
        dateFirstSeen: cluster.obsRows[0].eventDate,
        dateLastSeen: cluster.obsRows[cluster.obsRows.length - 1].eventDate,
        numObs: cluster.obsRows.length,
        clusterEP: (1 - cluster.pp).toFixed(3)
    }) : null;
};

/**
 * Report the population under the pointer to the layer's tooltip.
 * @param {reknitr.solowMapLayer} that - The layer
 * @param {maplibregl.Map} map - The map
 * @return {Object} A record of the listeners, to be supplied to `hortis.libreMap.gridSelector.unbindHover`
 */
reknitr.solowMapLayer.bindHover = function (that, map) {
    const listener = e => {
        if (that.visible) {
            const clusterId = hortis.libreMap.eventToProp(map, e, "clusterId");
            that.hoverAt(clusterId, e.originalEvent);
        }
    };
    const leave = () => that.hoverAt(null);
    map.on("mousemove", listener);
    map.on("mouseout", leave);
    return {map, listener, leave};
};

/** Taxa filters **/

/**
 * Compute the rows of a filter of values of a field - one for each value, with its label.
 * @param {String[]} fieldValues - The values
 * @param {String[]} [fieldLabels] - Their labels - by default, the values
 * @return {Object[]} The rows, each with members `value` and `label`
 */
hortis.valueFilter.rows = (fieldValues, fieldLabels) => fieldValues.map((value, i) => ({value, label: (fieldLabels || fieldValues)[i]}));

hortis.valueFilter.toggle = function (that, value, checked) {
    const filterState = {...that.filterState};
    if (checked) {
        filterState[value] = true;
    } else {
        delete filterState[value];
    }
    that.filterState = filterState;
};

hortis.valueFilter.isChecked = (filterState, value) => !!filterState[value];

hortis.valueFilter.rowChange = function (event, row) {
    row.toggle(event.target.checked);
};

/**
 * Filter rows to those whose value of a field is one of those selected.
 * @param {Object[]} rows - The rows
 * @param {Object<String, Boolean>} filterState - The selected values
 * @param {String} fieldName - The field
 * @param {String|null} valueOf - The global name of a function computing a row's value in place of its field, if any
 * @return {Object[]} The rows surviving the filter
 */
hortis.valueFilter.doFilter = function (rows, filterState, fieldName, valueOf) {
    const selected = Object.keys(filterState);
    const value = valueOf ? fluid.getGlobalValue(valueOf) : row => row[fieldName];
    return selected.length === 0 ? rows : rows.filter(row => selected.includes(value(row)));
};

hortis.isGraminoid = function (taxonRow) {
    let row = taxonRow;
    while (row && !(row.rank === "family" && ["Poaceae", "Cyperaceae", "Juncaceae"].includes(row.iNaturalistTaxonName))) {
        row = row.parent;
    }
    return !!row;
};

// A value for a filter of taxa by whether they are graminoids - grasses, sedges and rushes
hortis.graminoidValue = row => hortis.isGraminoid(row) ? "graminoid" : "non-graminoid";

reknitr.summaryTaxaRows = rows => rows.filter(row => row.inSummary);

/** iNaturalist panels **/

fluid.registerNamespace("reknitr.iNatPanel");

// The options of an iNaturalist panel, as rendered by @imerss/inat-components, which a pane's settings refine - ported
// from reknitr.iNatComponentsPaneHandler in paneHandlers.js
reknitr.iNatPanel.defaults = {
    dataSource: "autoLoad",
    itemWidth: 180,
    features: [
        {feature: "recentObservations", numResults: 40},
        {feature: "commonTaxa", numResults: 40, numYears: 10},
        {feature: "favourites", numResults: 40, numYears: 10},
        {feature: "stats", numTopObservers: 10, observersListClass: "inat-observers-list", statsCountSummaryClass: "inat-stats-count-summary"}
    ],
    generalClasses: {
        tabsElement: "inat-tabs",
        yearsDropdown: "inat-years-dropdown",
        pageHeadings: "inat-page-headings",
        observationLabelTitle: "inat-observation-label-title",
        observationLabelDate: "inat-observation-label-data",
        observationLabelName: "inat-observation-label-name",
        tabDesc: "inat-tab-desc"
    }
};

/**
 * Compute the options of an iNaturalist panel, merging those of a pane onto the defaults - each of its features onto
 * the default feature at the same position.
 * @param {Object} options - The pane's options, e.g. with members `taxon`, `place` and `features`
 * @return {Object} The options of the panel
 */
reknitr.iNatPanel.options = function (options) {
    const defaults = reknitr.iNatPanel.defaults;
    const features = defaults.features.map((feature, i) => ({...feature, ...(options.features || [])[i]}));
    return {...defaults, ...options, features};
};

/**
 * Render an iNaturalist panel into its container, which the library thereafter owns.
 * @param {fluid.component} that - The panel's component
 * @param {Element} container - The panel's rendered container
 * @param {Object} options - The panel's options
 * @param {Object} [inatComponents] - The @imerss/inat-components library
 * @return {Boolean|Unavailable} `true` once rendered, or an unavailable value if the library is not loaded
 */
reknitr.iNatPanel.bind = function (that, container, options, inatComponents) {
    let togo;
    if (inatComponents) {
        fluid.disableRendering(that);
        inatComponents.initTaxonPanel(container.id, fluid.copy(options));
        togo = true;
    } else {
        togo = fluid.unavailable({message: "The inat-components library is not loaded", variety: "config"});
    }
    return togo;
};

/*
Copyright 2025-2026 Antranig Basman
Licensed under the Educational Community License (ECL), Version 2.0 or the New
BSD license. You may not use this file except in compliance with one these
Licenses.
You may obtain a copy of the ECL 2.0 License and BSD License at
https://github.com/fluid-project/infusion/raw/master/Infusion-LICENSE.txt
*/

"use strict";

// A bar dividing two panes, dragged or moved with the arrow keys to share their space between them - ported to
// Infusion 6 from resize-bar.js. The bar is rendered in place by its parent's template, between the elements it
// divides, which are found as its siblings when it is moved. Their sizes are written as inline styles, which the
// parent's template, having not written them, leaves in place.

// noinspection ES6ConvertVarToLetConst // otherwise this is a duplicate on minifying
var hortis = fluid.registerNamespace("hortis");

fluid.registerNamespace("hortis.resizeBar");

// The state of a drag in progress, keyed by the bar's element
hortis.resizeBar.drags = new WeakMap();

hortis.resizeBar.sizeOf = (horizontal, element) => horizontal ? element.getBoundingClientRect().width : element.getBoundingClientRect().height;

/**
 * Share the space of the two panes beside a bar, giving the first `rawBefore` pixels within the limits of each.
 * @param {hortis.resizeBar} that - The bar's component
 * @param {Element} bar - The bar's element
 * @param {Object} drag - The sizes of the panes at the start of the move, with members `startBefore` and `startAfter`
 * @param {Number} rawBefore - The size proposed for the first pane, in pixels
 */
hortis.resizeBar.apply = function (that, bar, drag, rawBefore) {
    const horizontal = that.axis === "horizontal";
    const total = drag.startBefore + drag.startAfter;
    const before = Math.min(Math.max(rawBefore, that.minBefore), total - that.minAfter);
    const property = horizontal ? "width" : "height";
    bar.previousElementSibling.style[property] = (before / total * 100).toFixed(4) + "%";
    bar.nextElementSibling.style[property] = ((total - before) / total * 100).toFixed(4) + "%";
};

hortis.resizeBar.startSizes = function (that, bar) {
    const horizontal = that.axis === "horizontal";
    return {startBefore: hortis.resizeBar.sizeOf(horizontal, bar.previousElementSibling), startAfter: hortis.resizeBar.sizeOf(horizontal, bar.nextElementSibling)};
};

hortis.resizeBar.pointerDown = function (event, that) {
    if (event.button === 0) {
        const bar = event.currentTarget;
        const horizontal = that.axis === "horizontal";
        hortis.resizeBar.drags.set(bar, {...hortis.resizeBar.startSizes(that, bar), startPos: horizontal ? event.clientX : event.clientY});
        bar.setPointerCapture(event.pointerId);
        bar.classList.add("resize-bar--active");
        bar.ownerDocument.body.style.cursor = horizontal ? "col-resize" : "row-resize";
        bar.ownerDocument.body.style.userSelect = "none";
        event.preventDefault();
    }
};

hortis.resizeBar.pointerMove = function (event, that) {
    const bar = event.currentTarget;
    const drag = hortis.resizeBar.drags.get(bar);
    if (drag) {
        const pos = that.axis === "horizontal" ? event.clientX : event.clientY;
        hortis.resizeBar.apply(that, bar, drag, drag.startBefore + pos - drag.startPos);
    }
};

hortis.resizeBar.pointerUp = function (event) {
    const bar = event.currentTarget;
    if (hortis.resizeBar.drags.has(bar)) {
        hortis.resizeBar.drags.delete(bar);
        bar.classList.remove("resize-bar--active");
        bar.ownerDocument.body.style.cursor = "";
        bar.ownerDocument.body.style.userSelect = "";
    }
};

hortis.resizeBar.keyDown = function (event, that) {
    const horizontal = that.axis === "horizontal";
    const shrink = horizontal ? "ArrowLeft" : "ArrowUp";
    const grow = horizontal ? "ArrowRight" : "ArrowDown";
    if (event.key === shrink || event.key === grow) {
        event.preventDefault();
        const step = event.shiftKey ? 4 : 16;
        const drag = hortis.resizeBar.startSizes(that, event.currentTarget);
        hortis.resizeBar.apply(that, event.currentTarget, drag, drag.startBefore + (event.key === grow ? step : -step));
    }
};
EOF

saanich.inverseWeibullCount = (x, maxCount) => maxCount < 200 ? x : 0.012 * Math.pow(-Math.log(1 - x), 1 / 0.5);

  ## Your note on the R pipeline
  
  The port keeps R in control.
  
  - **Panes:** R still knits each pane to HTML. `storyBuild.js` only splits that output, the same cutting `reknit.js` did, and writes no markup of its own.
  - **Widgets:** R still produces every widget's data, drawn in the browser by the same htmlwidgets runtime.
  - **Settings:** each pane's settings still come from its `.Rmd` front matter.
  - **One exception:** the small placeholder data files are made by a JavaScript script in bagatelle. They could be made by the R pipeline instead.
  
  ## The remaining howe-sound panes
  
  - **Extirpation Risk:** the clustering and Solow estimate are ported as they were. With the same taxon selected, it gives the same three populations, colours, legend and taxon panel as the Infusion 4 page. The taxa filters are one generic value filter configured by the driver, which also covers the graminoid filter.
  - **Top Contributions:** the iNaturalist panel renders in the data area, configured from the driver. The library stays a howe-sound file in `static/`.
  - **Resize bars:** these were needed for layout as well as dragging: without the bar between the map and data area, a CSS rule hid the data area whenever the map was hidden.
  - **Smaller fixes:** Protected Areas' chart now fits the data area, and the record line reads "for 1,131 taxa" as before.
  - **Not ported:** the taxon panel (`taxonDisplay`), since neither project's configuration uses it.
  
  ## saanich
  
  saanich has its own driver with its data, Solow years, columns, place and the Weibull scaling of grid counts. It also has a development page, the same Hugo templates and story settings, placeholders and build scripts.
  
  A few things differ from what you might expect:
  
  - **Favourites text:** its `config.json5` described the Favourites panel in terms of Howe Sound, which looked like a copy-paste slip, so the driver says Saanich Peninsula instead.
  - **No pane maps:** its knitted panes contain no map widgets, so its map is the ESRI imagery fitted to the observation grid. I haven't compared it against the Infusion 4 saanich page.
  - **`copyFrameworkOut.sh`:** in both projects it now syncs only the Hugo templates, CSS, images, R files and lint config. The old JS pipeline is gone from it, and the story templates are added. The two copies are identical, and a dry run from howe-sound finds nothing to copy.

❯ storyBuild needs to move back into the client projects, it is notionally part of the "bioreportr" package which will be factored out at a later date. Put it as a sibling of the current "reknit.js". Put it in the bioreportr namespace. I'm unclear how the files such as "story/Solow.html" get there, they don't seem related to the R build? All of the "story" SFCs also need to be demoted into the separate projects. We'll carry the costs of duplicating/copying them for the time being until we think of a better reuse strategy, but they need to go out of imerss-bioinfo. The fluid-imports for core modules then need to use module-relative imports, qualified with %imerss-bioinfo/ . Everything new in the reknitr namespace needs to go into bioreportr. I don't see how the storyPage dependencies on papaparse.min.js are going to get resolved in a deployed site. I think the fluid.hashSync stuff needs to go out of core infusion and also out of the tag dialect - the fluid-hash notion creates a kind of portability burden that someone participating needs to have opted into the selfBoot process. Instead, lets make the hashManager a resolveRoot global, and cooperate with layers opting into hash state management via a new layer "fluid.hashLinkage". This should inspect codec configuration available in the current layer, mapping addresses in the component onto parts of the URL space, and dynamically synthesize a layer merged on top of the current component which holds cells and effects which will read and write the state to and from the hashManager. We don't want, e.g. storyPage, to depend on a member name "hash" appearing in its direct configuration, but a config such as hashLinkage: {activePaneKey: "activePaneKey"} which simply declares that the member of that name is to be synced with the URL state of that name. Rather than the "reveal" mechanism we should just rely on standard unavailable value semantics to prevent components rendering if they depend on some state which for some reason has not been decoded (although for this source of state this shouldn't be necessary since the URL can be decoded synchronously at any time). I think what would work best is for hashLinkage to be positioned as a subcomponent of the target component - in that way, the parent (e.g. reknitr.storyPage) then derives from {self}.hashLinkage.hashLayer where hashLayer will hold the name of a layer whose configuration has been dynamically computed from the hashLinkage configuration, suitable to overlay onto the parent.          /**
          * Resolve a path written into a component which may pass through its subcomponents, e.g. "shell.fullScreen" written
          * into a component with a subcomponent `shell`, to the component which holds the path's final member and the
          * remainder of the path within it. The path descends into a subcomponent for as long as its leading segment names
          * one, so that the final segment is always left to be written.
          * @param {ComponentComputer} component - The component into which the path is written
          * @param {String|String[]} path - The path
          * @return {Object} Members `component`, the component holding the path's final member, and `segs`, the path within it
          */
         fluid.descendSubcomponentPath = function (component, path) {
             let shadow = component[$m];
             let segs = fluid.pathToSegs(path);
             while (segs.length > 1 && shadow.childComponents?.[segs[0]]) {
                 shadow = shadow.childComponents[segs[0]];
                 segs = segs.slice(1);
             }
             return {component: shadow === component[$m] ? component : fluid.deSignal(shadow.availableInstance), segs};
         };

     #### State held in the URL
     
     A page whose state is held in its URL's hash, e.g. which of several panes is shown, can begin with that state rather
     than rendering its defaults and then jumping to it. An element bearing `fluid-hash` names a member of the component
     it boots, which begins as a reactive root holding the hash decoded into a record:
     
     ```html
     <div fluid-layers="my.storyPage" fluid-hash="hash"></div>
     ```
     
     The hash takes the form `#pane:Status&taxon:Bombus%20mixtus`, where a value beginning with `{` or `[` is JSON, and
     is decoded by `fluid.parseUrlHash` as part of the component's potentia, before anything is computed or rendered. So
     the pane it names is the first and only one shown. Under node there is no hash, so a static rendering shows the
     defaults.
     
     The layer `fluid.hashSync` keeps the member `hash` in step with the URL thereafter: a change of the URL, e.g. on
     navigating back, is written into `hash`, and a change to `hash` is pushed into the window's history. Read the hash
     whole, e.g. `$compute:my.paneFor({self}.hash)`, rathe
          ... [+16 more lines truncated]

p="src/client/js/i6/hashManager.js"
s=open(p).read()
s=s.replace('''// noinspection ES6ConvertVarToLetConst // otherwise this is a duplicate on minifying
var fluid = fluid || require("infusion");

''','')
old_start=s.index("// Map of the JSON form of a set of links")
old_end=s.index("// The global hash manager")
new='''// Map of the JSON form of a set of links to the name of the layer synthesised for them
fluid.hashLinkage.layerNames = new Map();
// Map of the name of each layer synthesised to the links it implements, as normalised
fluid.hashLinkage.layerLinks = {};

/**
 * Synthesise the layer which links members of a component to the URL's hash, as configured by a fluid.hashLinkage.
 * The layer is defined once for each distinct configuration, and named for it, so that recomputing it, e.g. as its
 * parent turns over, names the same layer rather than defining afresh a layer which would cause the parent to turn
 * over again. The functions of the layer are given the layer's name and the member's, from which they find the link.
 * @param {Object<String, String|HashLink>} links - The links, as configured
 * @return {String} The name of the layer
 */
fluid.hashLinkage.layerFor = function (links) {
    const normalised = fluid.hashLinkage.normaliseLinks(links);
    const memo = JSON.stringify(normalised);
    let layerName = fluid.hashLinkage.layerNames.get(memo);
    if (!layerName) {
        layerName = "fluid.hashLinkage.layers.l" + fluid.hashLinkage.layerNames.size;
        fluid.hashLinkage.layerNames.set(memo, layerName);
        fluid.hashLinkage.layerLinks[layerName] = normalised;
        const layer = {};
        Object.keys(normalised).forEach(member => {
            // Reading the listener holds the member unavailable until the URL has been read - which, since the
            // manager is created as this file loads, it will have been before any component reading it is instantiated
            layer[member] = {
                $compute: {
                    func: "fluid.hashLinkage.decode",
                    args: ["{fluid.hashManager}.hash", "{fluid.hashManager}.hashListener", layerName, member]
                }
            };
            layer[member + "FromHash"] = {
                $effect: {
                    func: "fluid.hashLinkage.fromHash",
                    args: ["{self}", "{fluid.hashManager}.hash", layerName, member]
                }
            };
            layer[member + "ToHash"] = {
                $effect: {
                    func: "fluid.hashLinkage.toHash",
                    args: ["{fluid.hashManager}", "{self}." + member, layerName, member]
                }
            };
        });
        fluid.def(layerName, layer);
    }
    return layerName;
};

/**
 * Decode a member's value from the URL's hash.
 * @param {Object} hash - The URL's hash, decoded
 * @param {Object} listener - The hash manager's listener, read only so as to wait until the URL has been read
 * @param {String} layerName - The name of the layer synthesised for the member's linkage
 * @param {String} member - The name of the member
 * @return {any} The member's value - that held in the hash, or else its default
 */
fluid.hashLinkage.decode = function (hash, listener, layerName, member) {
    const link = fluid.hashLinkage.layerLinks[layerName][member];
    return link.key in hash ? hash[link.key] : link.default;
};

fluid.hashLinkage.equal = (value1, value2) => JSON.stringify(value1) === JSON.stringify(value2);

/**
 * Write a member's value from the URL's hash into the component, once the hash has changed, e.g. on navigating back -
 * unless it already holds that value, since the member is first computed from the hash and writing it would raise it
 * needlessly into the component's live layer.
 * @param {fluid.component} that - The component holding the member
 * @param {Object} hash - The URL's hash, decoded
 * @param {String} layerName - The name of the layer synthesised for the member's linkage
 * @param {String} member - The name of the member
 */
fluid.hashLinkage.fromHash = function (that, hash, layerName, member) {
    const value = fluid.hashLinkage.decode(hash, null, layerName, member);
    if (!fluid.hashLinkage.equal(that[member], value)) {
        that[member] = value;
    }
};

/**
 * Write a member's value into the URL's hash, unless the hash already holds it. A member holding its default value
 * is removed from the hash.
 * @param {fluid.hashManager} hashManager - The hash manager
 * @param {any} value - The member's value
 * @param {String} layerName - The name of the layer synthesised for the member's linkage
 * @param {String} member - The name of the member
 */
fluid.hashLinkage.toHash = function (hashManager, value, layerName, member) {
    const hash = hashManager.hash;
    if (!fluid.hashLinkage.equal(fluid.hashLinkage.decode(hash, null, layerName, member), value)) {
        const link = fluid.hashLinkage.layerLinks[layerName][member];
        const {[link.key]: previous, ...others} = hash; // eslint-disable-line no-unused-vars
        hashManager.hash = fluid.hashLinkage.equal(value, link.default) ? others : {...others, [link.key]: value};
    }
};

'''
s=s[:old_start]+new+s[old_end:]
open(p,"w").write(s)

● The remerge re-runs `fromHash`, which writes the URL's stale value back over a fresh write. I'm making both effects act only on a real change, remembering the last value each saw per component.

● Bash: cd /home/amb26/Source/gits/bagatelle; python3 - <<'EOF'
p="/home/amb26/Source/gits/bagatelle/src/client/js/i6/hashManager.js"
s=open(p).read()
a=s.index("/**\n * Write a member's value from the URL's hash into the component")
b=s.index("// The global hash manager")
new='''// The values last seen by the effects of each linked component, keyed by its shadow - for each member, the value
// last decoded from the hash and the value of the member last written to it. A write into a component may cause it to
// turn over, which runs its effects afresh - each acts only on a change to what it last saw, so that one does not
// undo a write which the other has yet to propagate
fluid.hashLinkage.lastSeen = new WeakMap();

/**
 * Retrieve the record of the values last seen by the effects linking a member of a component to the URL.
 * @param {fluid.component} that - The component holding the member
 * @param {String} member - The name of the member
 * @return {Object} The record, with members `fromHash` and `toHash`, which is absent until first seen
 */
fluid.hashLinkage.seen = function (that, member) {
    const shadow = that[fluid.metadataSymbol];
    let records = fluid.hashLinkage.lastSeen.get(shadow);
    if (!records) {
        records = {};
        fluid.hashLinkage.lastSeen.set(shadow, records);
    }
    records[member] = records[member] || {};
    return records[member];
};

/**
 * Write a member's value from the URL's hash into the component once the hash has changed, e.g. on navigating back.
 * The member is first computed from the hash, so nothing is written until it changes, and then only if the member
 * does not already hold the value, since writing it raises it into the component's live layer.
 * @param {fluid.component} that - The component holding the member
 * @param {Object} hash - The URL's hash, decoded
 * @param {String} layerName - The name of the layer synthesised for the member's linkage
 * @param {String} member - The name of the member
 */
fluid.hashLinkage.fromHash = function (that, hash, layerName, member) {
    const value = fluid.hashLinkage.decode(hash, null, layerName, member);
    const seen = fluid.hashLinkage.seen(that, member);
    if ("fromHash" in seen && !fluid.hashLinkage.equal(seen.fromHash, value) && !fluid.hashLinkage.equal(that[member], value)) {
        seen.toHash = value;
        that[member] = value;
    }
    seen.fromHash = value;
};

/**
 * Write a member's value into the URL's hash once the member has changed, unless the hash already holds it. A member
 * holding its default value is removed from the hash.
 * @param {fluid.component} that - The component holding the member
 * @param {fluid.hashManager} hashManager - The hash manager
 * @param {any} value - The member's value
 * @param {String} layerName - The name of the layer synthesised for the member's linkage
 * @param {String} member - The name of the member
 */
fluid.hashLinkage.toHash = function (that, hashManager, value, layerName, member) {
    const seen = fluid.hashLinkage.seen(that, member);
    const hash = hashManager.hash;
    if ("toHash" in seen && !fluid.hashLinkage.equal(seen.toHash, value) &&
        !fluid.hashLinkage.equal(fluid.hashLinkage.decode(hash, null, layerName, member), value)) {
        const link = fluid.hashLinkage.layerLinks[layerName][member];
        const {[link.key]: previous, ...others} = hash; // eslint-disable-line no-unused-vars
        seen.fromHash = value;
        hashManager.hash = fluid.hashLinkage.equal(value, link.default) ? others : {...others, [link.key]: value};
    }
    seen.toHash = value;
};

'''
s=s[:a]+new+s[b:]
s=s.replace('''                    func: "fluid.hashLinkage.toHash",
                    args: ["{fluid.hashManager}",''','''                    func: "fluid.hashLinkage.toHash",
                    args: ["{self}", "{fluid.hashManager}",''')
open(p,"w").write(s)
EOF

import os, re, sys, glob, shutil
os.chdir("/home/amb26/Source/gits/bagatelle")
S = "src/client/sfc/"
groups = {
 "bbea": "bbeaChecklist bbeaLibreMap beaVizLoader beeAbundance bipartite checklist-search collectorReportLinker drawInteractions dualRangeInput elevationFilter groupedRegionFilter phenologyFilter phenologyFilter-row seedMix sexFilter taxonListView viewTabs",
 "standard": "blitzRecords blitzVizLoader standardVizLoader pageTabs pageTabs-tab regionFilter regionFilter-row vizLibreMap",
 "core": "autocomplete collectorFilter filterControls mfIcons recordReporter standardChecklist standardFilterControls taxonSearchFilter dataTable resizeBar valueFilter valueFilter-row",
}
moves = {}
for g, names in groups.items():
    for n in names.split():
        old = os.path.abspath(S + "hortis-" + n + ".vue")
        assert os.path.exists(old), old
        moves[old] = os.path.abspath(S + g + "/hortis-" + n + ".vue")
left = [f for f in glob.glob(S + "*.vue") if os.path.abspath(f) not in moves]
assert not left, left
# Files whose references are to be rewritten: every vue/html in bagatelle outside node_modules
files = [os.path.abspath(f) for f in glob.glob("**/*.vue", recursive=True) + glob.glob("**/*.html", recursive=True) if "node_modules" not in f and not f.startswith("docs/")]
attr = re.compile(r'((?:src|href|for)=")([^"%#:][^"]*)(")')
for f in files:
    newf = moves.get(f, f)
    text = open(f).read()
    def fix(m):
        ref = m.group(2)
        if ref.startswith("/") or ref.startswith("http"):
            return m.group(0)
        target = os.path.normpath(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(f), ref))
        target = moves.get(target, target)
        if not os.path.exists(target) and target not in moves.values():
            return m.group(0)
        rel = os.path.relpath(target, os.path.dirname(newf))
        return m.group(1) + rel + m.group(3)
    new = attr.sub(fix, text)
    if new != text:
        open(f, "w").write(new)
        print("rewrote", os.path.relpath(f))
for g in groups:
    os.makedirs(S + g, exist_ok=True)
for old, new in moves.items():
    shutil.move(old, new)
print(len(moves), "moved")
EOF

     /* eslint-env node */
     "use strict";
     
     // Build the material of a story map from the HTML knitted from its R Markdown panes - the step between knitting and
     // rendering the story page statically with Infusion 6's hydrate.js. In place of reknit.js, which wove the panes into
     // a page template, this writes small files which the story page's Single File Components fetch:
     //   - <out>/panes.json - one record per pane, in order of the `weight` of its front matter, holding its front matter,
     //     its `paneKey`, the name of its file, and any members of its <viz_data>/<paneKey>-mapData.json
     //   - <out>/<paneKey>.html - the section of each pane, without the pandoc page around it, and without the data of
     //     its map widgets, which are folded into mapData.json
     //   - <out>/<paneKey>-data.html - any widgets of a pane bearing an mx_widgetId, e.g. a chart driving a slider, which
     //     are shown in the pane's data pane beside the map
     //   - <out>/mapData.json - a single map style, holding every source and layer of every pane's map once, together
     //     with the layers, camera and fill patterns of each pane

     // e.g. from a bioReportR project, node ../bagatelle/src/story/storyBuild.js content/story viz_data static/story

● The reorganisation is done and the hash scheme works. It needed no upgrade to Infusion's dynamic layer support, only a workaround on the hashLinkage side. Every suite passes and lint is clean; Hugo is still untested, since it isn't installed here.
  
  ## `fluid.hashLinkage`
  `fluid.hashSync`, `fluid-hash` and the "reveal" step are gone from Infusion core, its tests and the ponder doc. The replacement lives in bagatelle's `src/client/js/i6/hashManager.js`:
  
  - **`fluid.hashManager`** is now a `fluid.resolveRoot` component. A single instance is created when the file loads and decodes the URL immediately, so the hash is available before any component reads it, without unavailable-value gating.
  - **`fluid.hashLinkage`** is a subcomponent of the page. The story page now reads:
    ```js
    $layers: ["hortis.vizLoader", "{self}.hashLinkage.hashLayer"],
    selectedPaneKey: null,
    selectedRegion: null,
    hashLinkage: {$component: {$layers: "fluid.hashLinkage",
        links: {selectedPaneKey: "pane", selectedRegion: "region"}}}
    ```
    `hashLayer` names a layer built from `links`. For each linked member it computes the member from the URL and adds two effects: one writes the member into the URL, the other writes back URL changes such as Back. A link can also be `{key, default}`. The page has no `hash` member; it just reads and writes `selectedPaneKey`. I linked `selectedPaneKey` rather than `activePaneKey`, because `activePaneKey` is computed: it falls back to the first pane.
  
  **Does it work?** The URL's value reaches the parent before any of its effects run, so the page never renders the default pane first. Three problems came up:
  
  - **A layer defined inside a `$compute` loops for ever.** Every `fluid.def` call counts as a change, which turns the parent over and recomputes the layer. I worked around this by defining each distinct `links` configuration only once. A framework fix would be for `fluid.def` to ignore a definition identical to the existing one.
  - **Writing a member makes the parent turn over.** On the first write to a member, Infusion makes the parent turn over, which re-runs all its effects. The URL-to-member effect then wrote the old URL value back over the fresh write. Each effect now acts only on a change since it last ran.
  - **`key in hash` is always false.** The proxied hash doesn't support `in`, so the linkage copies the hash before looking a key up.
  
  **One behaviour change:** without the reveal step, a hydrated page opened with a hash shows its static first pane until it boots, then the named pane. A minimal page only ever shows the named pane. The round-trip test now expects exactly that.
  
  ## Reorganisation
  - **SFCs:** bagatelle's are now in `sfc/bbea/` (17, everything only the BBEA driver uses, including drawInteractions), `sfc/standard/` (8, shared by Blitz and Diatoms) and `sfc/core/` (12, shared or generic). Drivers, pages and tests have been updated to match.
  - **Story SFCs:** each project now has its own copy in `static/bioreportr/sfc/bioreportr-*.vue`, alongside `js/i6/story.js`, `js/i6/solow.js` and `css/imerss-story-i6.css`. Everything new is in the `bioreportr` namespace. The pane-handler names `reknitr.obsMapPaneHandler` and `reknitr.solowPaneHandler` are unchanged, because they come from the `.Rmd` front matter.
  - **bagatelle references:** imports, scripts and styles from bagatelle are written as `%imerss-bioinfo/...`. That form works for SFC `<script>` and `<style>` as well as for imports.
  - **`solow.js` split:** its `hortis` parts (value filter, taxon images, graminoid test) went to a new bagatelle `valueFilter.js`.
  - **htmlwidgets:** bagatelle's copies of the htmlwidgets and plotly files were identical to the projects' `static/bioreportr/js/` ones, so I deleted them and the SFCs use the projects' files.
  - **`storyBuild.js`:** now `src/js/storyBuild.js` beside `reknit.js`, in the `bioreportr.storyBuild` namespace, and it writes byte-identical output. I removed the `linkedom` devDependency I had added to bagatelle.
  - **`copyFrameworkOut.sh`:** in both projects it now also syncs `storyBuild.js`, the story SFCs, scripts, CSS and htmlwidgets. The two copies are identical and a dry run finds nothing to copy.
  
  ## Your questions
  - **`story/Solow.html`:** it does come from R. `content/story/Solow.Rmd` is knitted to `content/story/Solow.html`, and `storyBuild.js` cuts that file's section out into `static/story/Solow.html`, as it does for every pane.
  - **papaparse:** it was already reaching deployed sites. copyOut copies it into `static/vendor/imerss-bioinfo/node_modules/papaparse/`, which Hugo publishes, and the story page now names it as `%imerss-bioinfo/node_modules/papaparse/papaparse.min.js`.

// onto a reactive record `hash`. The hash takes the form #key1:value1&key2:value2, where a value beginning with { or [

QUnit.test("Members referring to the URL's hash", function (assert) {
    const win = hortis.tests.currentWindow = hortis.tests.fakeWindow("#pane:History");
    // Stand in for the global manager, so that {hashManager} resolves to one mirroring the fake window
    fluid.hashManager.instance.destroy();
    fluid.cell.stabilize();
    const manager = hortis.tests.hashManager();
    fluid.cell.stabilize();
    const that = hortis.tests.hashReader();
    fluid.cell.stabilize();
    assert.equal(that.selectedPane, "History", "Member begins with the URL's value");
    assert.deepEqual([...that.paneRenders], ["History"], "Member was only ever computed from the URL");
    assert.equal(that.region, undefined, "Member absent from the URL is undefined");

    manager.hash.pane = "Status";
    fluid.cell.stabilize();
    assert.equal(that.selectedPane, "Status", "Writing into the hash changes the member");

● Yes, both work. A page opts in with a plain reference such as `selectedPaneKey: "{hashManager}.hash.pane"`. The hydrated page renders nothing that depends on the URL, and the browser fills it in once the page boots. `fluid.hashLinkage` and its synthesised layer are gone, so no change to Infusion is needed.
  
  **The opt-in.** The story page now reads:
  ```js
  selectedPaneKey: "{hashManager}.hash.pane",
  selectedRegion: "{hashManager}.hash.region",
  ```
  When the URL doesn't hold a key, the reference gives `undefined` rather than an unavailable value, so no default needs declaring. `activePaneKey` then falls back to the first pane, as before.
  
  **Writes are the one catch.** Writing `that.selectedPaneKey = "History"` would rebind the member locally and lose its link to the URL. That's standard Infusion behaviour for any member defined by a reference. So `selectPane` and `selectRegion`, including the region filter's reset and the map's reset, now write into `{hashManager}.hash.pane` and `.region` instead. If you'd rather the page never named the hash for writes, Infusion would need a way for a write to a reference member to pass through to its source. Currently only writes beneath such a member, or deletes, do that.
  
  **Hydration.** Under node there is no URL, so the global manager's `hash` is an unavailable value. Everything computed from it is then unavailable and is simply not rendered. The hydrated page holds:
  - the tabs, every pane's section, the checklist and the record reporter;
  - no active pane, and no map, since the map depends on the active pane.
  
  Once the page boots, it shows only the pane the URL names. The round-trip test is back to requiring that both forms, with or without a hash, only ever show the named pane.
  
  **Tests and lint.**
  - HashManagerTests now has a test for a member defined by reference to the hash (24/24 pass).
  - Story navigation and the story round trip pass for both howe-sound and saanich.
  - Lint is clean.
  - Region selection now writes into the hash too, but no test covers it in the browser.
  
  The story-page changes are copied identically into saanich, and both projects' `static/vendor` is refreshed.
