● Partly. What we supplied for the todo samples sends writes made *beneath* a referenced value back to their source. It doesn't cover a write that replaces a member which is itself a reference. I checked both under node:
  
  - **Writing the whole member doesn't write through.** With `pane: "{src}.hash.pane"` or `pane: {$reactiveRoot: "{src}.hash.pane"}`, `that.pane = "C"` changed the member but left the source hash untouched. The member was rebound locally, which is what `setHandler`'s comment says should happen. The todo items work because they write `todo.completed`, beneath the referenced todo, never replacing `todo` itself.
  - **Writing beneath a reference does write through.** With `urlState: "{src}.hash"`, both `that.urlState.pane = "C"` and a key the hash didn't yet hold, `that.urlState.region = "G"`, went upstream into the hash. Members defined as `"{self}.urlState.pane"` followed the changes, as did the URL-driven ones.
  
  So the story page could opt in like this and never name the hash manager in its methods:
  ```js
  urlState: "{hashManager}.hash",
  selectedPaneKey: "{self}.urlState.pane",
  selectedRegion: "{self}.urlState.region",
  // selectPane: that.urlState.pane = paneKey
  ```
  The cost is one extra member, and `that.selectedPaneKey = ...` would still rebind locally. Getting the single-line form, `selectedPaneKey: "{hashManager}.hash.pane"`, with direct writes would need a change to Infusion. A write to a member defined only by a reference would have to follow it upstream, using `fluid.upstreamSite` as deletes already do. That changes the documented rebinding rule, so it's your call.
  
  Shall I switch the story page to the `urlState` form, or try the framework change?

         /**
          * "Follow fish upstream" - trace a signal held at a component member through its chain of `$sitedRef`s to the
          * terminal site which holds its data, e.g. from an iteration variable `{self}.todo` to the element
          * `{todoList}.todos.0` of the list it was drawn from. If that site lies in mat-forming material, a proxy is returned
          * onto it so that writes through it are applied to the original data source rather than to the referring component.
          * @param {Signal<any>} next - The signal held at the member
          * @param {any} upcoming - The designalised value of the signal
          * @return {Proxy|any} A proxy onto the terminal site if it is mat-forming, otherwise the supplied value
          */
         fluid.proxyUpstream = function (next, upcoming) {
             const sited = fluid.deSignalToSite(next);
             if (fluid.isSignal(sited) && sited.$variety === "$sitedRef" && fluid.isMatForming(sited.site.shadow, sited.site.segs)) {
                 return fluid.proxyMat(sited, sited.site.shadow, sited.site.segs);
             } else {
                 return upcoming;
             }
         };

     **Writing through iteration variables.** When the source is sited, each `valueAs` variable keeps track of where its
     data came from, so the subcomponent can change its own element without involving the component that owns the
     list:
     
     * A write beneath the variable, e.g. `self.todo.completed = true`, is applied to the original element of the source.
     * `delete self.todo` removes the element from the source, as does [`destroy()`](#componentdestroy) on the subcomponent.
     * Writing to the variable itself, e.g. `self.todo = {...}`, rebinds it locally in the subcomponent's live layer and
       doesn't touch the source.
     
     This holds across intermediate projections. Elements selected by a non-mutating array method such as `filter()`
     remain linked to their original source:
     
     ```js
     fluid.def("my.todoItem", {
         $layers: "fluid.component",
         toggle: {
             $method: {
                 func: self => self.todo.completed = !self.todo.completed,   // Writes into {todoList}.todos
                 args: "{self}"

  ⎿  The returned **component proxy** (from regular client JavaScript code) has these semantics:
     
     * **Reads** resolve signals transparently: `that.count` returns the current concrete value, `that.child` returns a
       proxy to a subcomponent, `that.method(...)` invokes a `$method`.
     * **Writes** (`that.count = 6`, or mutating array methods such as `that.items.push(x)`) are recorded in the
       component's **live layer**, the highest-precedence layer, and propagate reactively. A write beneath a
       [`$reactiveRoot`](#reactiveroot) is applied immutably to the root's value.
     * **Reads within a computation**, i.e. within the function of a [`$compute`](#compute) or [`$effect`](#effect), make
       the computation depend on the member read, so that it reruns when that member changes, as well as when its arguments
       do. A member which is only to be consulted, without the computation depending on it, is read within
       [`fluid.cell.untracked`](/docs/fluid-signals#fluidcelluntrackedfn), e.g. `fluid.cell.untracked(() => self.open)`.
     * Access after destruction throws, other than within a computation, where a destroyed component and each of its members
       read as [unavailable](#unavailable-components).
     
     ### Component.destroy()
     
     Every component (via the base layer `fluid.component`) has a `destroy` method. Destruction disposes all of the
     component's effects, bindables and subcomponents. Equivalent to `fluid.destroyComponent(that)`.

● It does work in the deployed site. A relative path in an SFC is resolved against the SFC's own URL, not the page's, so it holds wherever the module is copied, provided the file it names moves with the module. Your instinct is right about one case though, covered under "Where it breaks" below.
  
  **How it resolves.** In the howe-sound story page the chain is:
  
  1. The page declares `<fluid-module id="imerss-bioinfo" src="../vendor/imerss-bioinfo">`. The story page imports `%imerss-bioinfo/src/client/sfc/core/hortis-valueFilter.vue`, which therefore loads from `/vendor/imerss-bioinfo/src/client/sfc/core/hortis-valueFilter.vue`.
  2. `fluid.resolveSFCPath` resolves the SFC's `<style src="../../../../node_modules/pretty-checkbox/dist/pretty-checkbox.min.css">` against that URL. That gives `/vendor/imerss-bioinfo/node_modules/pretty-checkbox/dist/pretty-checkbox.min.css`.
  3. On injection, the link is rewritten relative to the page. The hydrated page holds:
     ```html
     <link id="fl-style-hortis.valueFilter-0" href="../vendor/imerss-bioinfo/node_modules/pretty-checkbox/dist/pretty-checkbox.min.css" rel="stylesheet">
     ```
  4. copyOut put that file there. The path falls inside the `imerss-bioinfo` module's directory, so copyOut copied it from bagatelle's own `node_modules`. `static/vendor/imerss-bioinfo/node_modules/pretty-checkbox/dist/pretty-checkbox.min.css` exists, and Hugo publishes it.
  
  So `../../../../node_modules/...` and `%imerss-bioinfo/node_modules/...` mean the same thing: the dependency is treated as part of the imerss-bioinfo module's tree. The relative form only needs the extra step of resolving against the SFC first.
  
  **Where it breaks.** Both forms assume pretty-checkbox sits inside bagatelle's own `node_modules`. That holds for a bagatelle checkout, which is how copyOut is run today. It fails if a project installs imerss-bioinfo from npm, because npm hoists the dependency to the project's top-level `node_modules/pretty-checkbox`. Nothing would exist at `node_modules/imerss-bioinfo/node_modules/pretty-checkbox`, and the reference would point at nothing. The path encodes bagatelle's install layout, not a fact about bagatelle.
  
  **The robust form** is a module reference to the dependency itself:
  ```html
  <style src="%pretty-checkbox/dist/pretty-checkbox.min.css"></style>
  ```
  The page, or copyOut's `--source` list, would then say where `pretty-checkbox` lives, as it already does for `infusion-6` and `imerss-bioinfo`. To make that workable:
  
  - **Unregistered modules.** Something has to resolve a `%name` that no `<fluid-module>` declares. The natural fallback is npm-style lookup from the referring module's directory up through `node_modules`, under node at copy-out time.
  - **copyOut.** It would copy each such dependency into a directory of its own, e.g. `vendor/pretty-checkbox/`, and record that in the page's module declarations, or in a declaration file the page loads, so the browser can resolve it too.
  
  The same applies to every third-party file the SFCs name: maplibre, mapbox-gl-draw, popper, papaparse, pako, accessible-autocomplete and dual-range-input.
  
  Shall I implement that? The steps would be: npm-style resolution for unregistered `%name` modules in Infusion, copyOut support for placing and declaring them, then converting the bagatelle SFCs' `node_modules` references to `%package/...` form.

anchor="/**\n * Similar to fluid.module.resolvePath"
add='''// A module reference, `%name/rest`, where the name may be that of a scoped npm package, e.g. `%@mapbox/mapbox-gl-draw/`
fluid.module.dependencyRefRegex = /^%((?:@[^/]+\\/)?[^/]+)\\/(.*)$/;

/**
 * Find the registered module within whose directory a URL lies - the innermost, if their directories are nested.
 * @param {String} url - An absolute URL
 * @return {String|null} The name of the module, or `null` if the URL lies within none
 */
fluid.module.containingModule = function (url) {
    const containing = Object.keys(fluid.module.modules).filter(name => {
        const moduleUrl = fluid.module.modules[name].url;
        return typeof(moduleUrl) === "string" && url.startsWith(moduleUrl + "/");
    }).sort((a, b) => fluid.module.modules[b].url.length - fluid.module.modules[a].url.length);
    return containing[0] || null;
};

/**
 * Resolve a reference to a package written in a file of a module, e.g. `%pretty-checkbox/dist/pretty-checkbox.min.css`
 * in one of its Single File Components. A package which is not itself registered as a module is a dependency of the
 * module holding the file, and is found as npm installs it beneath the module - in its `node_modules` directory - e.g.
 * `<module>/node_modules/pretty-checkbox/dist/pretty-checkbox.min.css`. This holds wherever the module is copied, since
 * copyOut.js copies each dependency it demands into that place, wherever npm placed it in the module's checkout. A
 * reference to a registered module, or by a file lying within no module, is returned unchanged.
 * @param {String} referrerUrl - The absolute URL of the file holding the reference
 * @param {String} path - The path, which may begin with a reference `%package/`
 * @return {String} The absolute URL of the package's file, or the path unchanged
 */
fluid.module.resolveDependencyPath = function (referrerUrl, path) {
    const match = fluid.module.dependencyRefRegex.exec(path);
    let togo = path;
    if (match && !fluid.module.modules[match[1]] && !fluid.module.modules[match[1].split("/")[0]]) {
        const container = fluid.module.containingModule(referrerUrl);
        if (container) {
            togo = fluid.module.modules[container].url + "/node_modules/" + match[1] + "/" + match[2];
        } else {
            fluid.log(fluid.logLevel.WARN, "Cannot resolve package reference " + path + " in " + referrerUrl +
                " which lies within no registered module");
        }
    }
    return togo;
};

    const declared = Object.keys(fluid.serverModuleSources).filter(prefix => url.startsWith(prefix))
        .sort((a, b) => b.length - a.length)[0];
    return declared ? fluid.moduleDependencySourceUrl(fluid.serverModuleSources[declared], url.substring(declared.length)) : url;

// A path within a module beneath its node_modules directory, naming a package, which may be scoped, and a path within it
fluid.moduleDependencyRegex = /^node_modules\\/((?:@[^/]+\\/)?[^/]+)\\/(.*)$/;

/**
 * Find the source of a file within a module's directory, as read from the module's source directory. A file beneath
 * the module's `node_modules` directory belongs to a package on which the module depends, which npm may have installed
 * there, or in the `node_modules` directory of any directory enclosing the module's, e.g. by hoisting it into that of
 * a project depending on the module. The package is sought as node finds it, beginning with the module's directory, so
 * that it is copied by copyOut.js into its place beneath the module, where the browser expects it, wherever npm put it -
 * see `fluid.module.resolveDependencyPath`
 * @param {String} sourceUrl - The absolute file: URL of the module's source directory, ending in "/"
 * @param {String} rest - The path of the file within the module's directory
 * @return {String} The absolute URL of the file's source
 */
fluid.moduleDependencySourceUrl = function (sourceUrl, rest) {
    const nested = sourceUrl + rest;
    const match = fluid.moduleDependencyRegex.exec(rest.replace(/[?#].*$/, ""));
    let togo = nested;
    if (match && sourceUrl.startsWith("file:")) {
        let dir = fileURLToPath(sourceUrl);
        let found = null;
        while (!found) {
            const candidate = path.join(dir, "node_modules", match[1]);
            const parent = path.dirname(dir);
            if (fs.existsSync(candidate)) {
                found = candidate;
            } else if (parent === dir) {
                found = false;
            } else {
                dir = parent;
            }
        }
        if (found) {
            togo = fluid.deSlash(pathToFileURL(found).href) + "/" + match[2];
        }
    }
    return togo;
};'''

An SFC refers to a file of an npm package its module depends on by naming the package, rather than by a path into
`node_modules`:

```html
<style src="%pretty-checkbox/dist/pretty-checkbox.min.css"></style>
<script src="%@mapbox/mapbox-gl-draw/dist/mapbox-gl-draw-unminified.js" fluid-client data-fl-scope="global"></script>
```

A `%name/` naming no registered module is resolved as a dependency of the module holding the SFC, beneath that
module's `node_modules` directory - e.g. `vendor/imerss-bioinfo/node_modules/pretty-checkbox/...`. The SFC must
lie within a module the page declares, so a page served from the module's own checkout declares the checkout
itself, e.g. `<fluid-module id="imerss-bioinfo" src="./">`.

In a checkout, npm may not have installed the package beneath the module: it may be hoisted into the `node_modules`
of an enclosing directory. When copyOut.js or hydrate.js read a module from its checkout, a file beneath the
module's `node_modules` is sought as node finds packages, from the module's directory upwards, and copyOut.js copies
it to its place beneath the module, where the browser looks for it. So the copied-out site has the same layout
however the checkout was installed. A file outside any module can refer to the same place as
`%imerss-bioinfo/node_modules/pretty-checkbox/...`, which is resolved in the same way.

`tests/framework-tests/server/copyout-test.js` copies out a page and checks that it then renders correctly when
served from its own directory alone - including packages installed beneath its module and hoisted above it.

  **Resolution in the browser.** A `%name/` that names no registered module is treated as a package the SFC's module depends on. It resolves into that module's own `node_modules`, e.g. `vendor/imerss-bioinfo/node_modules/pretty-checkbox/...`, and scoped names like `%@mapbox/mapbox-gl-draw/...` work too. This is in `fluid.module.resolveDependencyPath` in `FluidModules.js`, called from `fluid.resolveSFCPath`. References to registered modules behave as before. A `%name/` in a file that lies in no module is left unchanged, with a warning.
  
  **Resolution under node.** When copyOut or `hydrate.js` read a module from its checkout, a path beneath the module's `node_modules/package/` is looked up the way node finds packages. The lookup starts in the module's directory and works upwards, so a hoisted package is still found. copyOut then copies it into the place under the module where the browser looks. The deployed layout is the same however the checkout was installed. This is in `fluid.moduleDependencySourceUrl` in `server-support.js`.
  
  **bagatelle:**
  - **Converted references:** all 29 `../../../../node_modules/...` references in its SFCs now use `%package/...`.
  - **Self-declaration:** for `%package/` to resolve, an SFC has to sit inside a module the page declares. So bagatelle's own pages (`indexBeasBCBA-6.html`, `indexBlitz-6.html`, `indexDiatoms-6.html`) and the three BBEA test pages now declare the checkout itself, e.g. `<fluid-module id="imerss-bioinfo" src="./">`. The projects' pages already declared it.
  - **Story SFCs stay as they are.** They live in the projects, outside any module, so they keep `%imerss-bioinfo/node_modules/maplibre-gl/...`. That path is still safe, because the node-side lookup applies to any path under a module's `node_modules`.
  
  **Checked:**
  - **Hydrated howe-sound story page:** every third-party file resolves under `../vendor/imerss-bioinfo/node_modules/`, including pretty-checkbox, maplibre, mapbox-gl-draw, popper, papaparse, pako and accessible-autocomplete.
  - **copyout-test:** extended to build a temporary checkout of its fixture module. One SFC there refers to a scoped package installed beneath the module and to a package hoisted above it. Both must be copied under `vendor/rt/node_modules/`, and the page must render the same whether booted from the minimal or the hydrated form. The packages are created at run time, so no `node_modules` fixtures go into git.

  The rule is documented in ponder's `fluid-view.md` under "Packages a module depends on", and in copyOut.js's header comment. Both projects' `static/vendor` copies are refreshed.
  
  **Limitation:** a page that lives in no module can't use `%package/` directly. Only a module's own SFCs can.

❯ What's meant by "document.write of core Infusion files"?

● I meant a small generated script, sitting inside the project, that writes Infusion's own `<script>` tags into the page while the page is still being parsed. The page itself then never names where Infusion lives.
  
  For example, the page would carry only:
  
  ```html
  <script src="../../fluid-modules.js"></script>
  ```
  
  and the generated `fluid-modules.js` would hold something like:
  
  ```js
  var fluid_modules = {
      "infusion-6": "../vendor/infusion",
      "imerss-bioinfo": "../vendor/imerss-bioinfo",
      "maplibre-gl": "../vendor/imerss-bioinfo/node_modules/maplibre-gl"
  };
  ["src/lib/lezer/lezer-javascript-browser.js", "src/framework/core/js/FluidCore.js", "src/framework/core/js/FluidSignals.js",
   "src/framework/core/js/Fluid.js" /* ... the rest of the core */].forEach(file =>
      document.write(`<script src="${fluid_modules["infusion-6"]}/${file}"></script>`));
  ```
  
  **Why `document.write`.** A script tag written that way, while the parser is still running, behaves exactly like one in the page's own markup. The browser fetches it and runs it in order, before the rest of the page is parsed. So Infusion's core would be loaded and ready when the page's `<fluid-import>` and `fluid-layers` elements are reached, as happens now. Appending script elements from JavaScript instead would load them asynchronously, and the core files would no longer be guaranteed to run in order before boot.
  
  **Drawbacks:**
  - **Deprecated, though still supported.** `document.write` is discouraged. Chrome may refuse to run scripts written this way if they're cross-origin and the connection is slow, though same-origin vendored files like these are unaffected.
  - **Hydration.** `hydrate.js` would have to treat the written tags as the page's core scripts, which it currently recognises by `fluid-hydrated="%infusion-6"`.
  
  **The alternative** is to have no loader at all. The page keeps its core `<script>` tags, but they point inside its own project, e.g. `vendor/infusion/...`. Only bagatelle's own dev pages would then need a copy of Infusion inside the bagatelle checkout instead of `../infusion-6`.


❯ Infusion itself will always need to be loaded via some external reference to bootstrap the whole process, but this should be the only exception. After that, every reference can be module-relative. However, the hydrater/copier should be able to choose given the reference to where the Infusion module is housed, to expand the import reference to broken-out or built versions of the framework.

● So the one external reference is a single bootstrap script tag for Infusion, which the hydrater or copier can expand into either the separate core files or a built bundle. Everything else is a module reference, resolved through mappings set up outside the pages.   ⎿       */
         fluid.fetch = function (url, options, strategy) {
             // The I/O is the work of a computation returning a promise, so that the cell is pending within the reactive
             // graph until it completes, and fluid.cell.settle waits for it - e.g. before a document rendered under node is
             // written. It begins once the cell is first read
             const load = async function () {
                 let togo;
                 try {
                     const response = await fetch(url, {...options, ...fluid.cacheOptions});
                     if (!response.ok) {
                         togo = fluid.unavailable({message: `HTTP error ${response.status} for URL ${url}`, variety: "error"});
                     } else {
                         togo = await strategy(response);
                         if (options?.delay) {
                             await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, options.delay));
                         }
                     }
                 } catch (err) {
                     togo = fluid.unavailable({message: `I/O failure for URL ${url} - ${err}`, variety: "error"});
                 }
                 return togo;
             };
             return fluid.cell(fluid.unavailable({message: `Pending I/O for URL ${url}`, variety: "pending"}),
                 {name: `fluid.fetch for URL ${url}`}).computed(load, []);
         };

/**
 * A function which is consulted for a module which is referred to but has not been registered, and which may register
 * it - e.g. as installed by copyOut.js, which finds the module's source where node would find the package of that
 * name. Otherwise `null`, and a module is known only once registered, e.g. by `<fluid-module>` or a module map
 * @type {Function|null}
 */
fluid.module.unregisteredResolver = null;

/**
 * Look up the record of a registered module, consulting `fluid.module.unregisteredResolver` if it is not registered
 * @param {String} name - The name of the module
 * @return {Object|undefined} The module's record, with members `url`, `origUrl` and `abs`, if it is registered
 */
fluid.module.lookup = function (name) {
    if (!fluid.module.modules[name] && fluid.module.unregisteredResolver) {
        fluid.module.unregisteredResolver(name);
    }
    return fluid.module.modules[name];

/**
 * Register the modules listed in a module map - an object mapping the name of each module to its directory, relative
 * to the map's own URL. A module already registered, e.g. by `<fluid-module>`, keeps its registration.

 * @param {Object<String, String>} map - The map

fluid.module.registerMap = function (mapUrl, map) {

        if (!fluid.module.modules[name]) {

            const url = abs ? dir.replace(/\\/$/, "") : new URL(dir.replace(/\\/$/, "") + "/", mapUrl).href.replace(/\\/$/, "");

fluid.module.resolvePath = function (path) {
    const match = fluid.module.refRegex.exec(path);
    const moduleRecord = match && fluid.module.lookup(match[1]);
    return moduleRecord ? moduleRecord.url + "/" + match[2] : path;

// The record of Infusion's files which FluidBoot.js loads in the browser
fluid.bootRecord = require("../core/js/FluidBoot.js");

/**
 * Determine whether a script element is the bootstrap of Infusion, FluidBoot.js - see that file
 * @param {Element} node - The script element
 * @return {Boolean} `true` if the element loads FluidBoot.js
 */
fluid.isBootScript = function (node) {
    const src = node.getAttribute("src");
    return !!src && src.replace(/[?#].*$/, "").endsWith(fluid.bootRecord.bootPath);
};

/**
 * Do under node what the bootstrap of Infusion, FluidBoot.js, does in the browser - declare Infusion's module, by a
 * `<fluid-module>` element placed before the bootstrap's script, at the directory holding it. Infusion itself is
 * already loaded under node.
 * @param {Document} dokkument - The document, before it is booted
 * @return {String|null} The `src` of Infusion's module as the document refers to it, or `null` if it has no bootstrap
 */
fluid.expandBootScript = function (dokkument) {
    const script = [...dokkument.querySelectorAll("script[src]")].find(fluid.isBootScript);
    let togo = null;
    if (script) {
        const src = script.getAttribute("src").replace(/[?#].*$/, "");
        togo = src.substring(0, src.length - fluid.bootRecord.bootPath.length);
        if (!dokkument.querySelector(`fluid-module[id="${fluid.bootRecord.moduleName}"]`)) {
            const moduleNode = dokkument.createElement("fluid-module");
            moduleNode.setAttribute("id", fluid.bootRecord.moduleName);
            moduleNode.setAttribute("src", togo);
            script.parentNode.insertBefore(moduleNode, script);
        }
    }
    return togo;
};

/**
 * The paths of Infusion's files, relative to its root, which a page refers to when its bootstrap is written in one of
 * the forms of `fluid.writeBootScript`
 * @param {String} form - "boot", "source" or "built"
 * @return {String[]} The paths
 */
fluid.bootFiles = function (form) {
    const record = fluid.bootRecord;
    return form === "built" ? [record.builtFile] : form === "source" ? record.files : [record.bootPath, ...record.files];
};

/**
 * Write the bootstrap of Infusion into a document about to be written out, in one of three forms - "boot", leaving
 * the document's FluidBoot.js to load Infusion's files, "source", replacing it with a script for each of the files, as
 * FluidBoot.js writes them, or "built", replacing it with the bundle of them built into Infusion's dist
 * @param {Document} dokkument - The document
 * @param {String} [form] - The form of the bootstrap, "boot" by default
 */
fluid.writeBootScript = function (dokkument, form = "boot") {
    const script = [...dokkument.querySelectorAll("script[src]")].find(fluid.isBootScript);
    if (script && form !== "boot") {
        const src = script.getAttribute("src").replace(/[?#].*$/, "");
        const root = src.substring(0, src.length - fluid.bootRecord.bootPath.length);
        fluid.bootFiles(form).forEach(file => {
            const node = dokkument.createElement("script");
            node.setAttribute("src", root + file);
            node.setAttribute("fluid-hydrated", "%" + fluid.bootRecord.moduleName);
            script.parentNode.insertBefore(node, script);
        });
        script.remove();
    }
};''')

// Map of module id to the absolute path of the directory from which its files are read under node, in place of the one
// at which the document locates it - see fluid.registerModuleSources
fluid.serverModuleSourcesById = {};

/**
 * Record the source of a module which has been registered at a URL, if it has one - see `fluid.registerModuleSources`
 * @param {String} name - The module's name
 * @param {String} url - The absolute URL of its directory, as the document locates it
 */
fluid.registerServerModuleSource = function (name, url) {
    const source = fluid.serverModuleSourcesById[name];
    if (source) {
        fluid.serverModuleSources[fluid.deSlash(url) + "/"] = fluid.deSlash(pathToFileURL(source).href) + "/";
    }

/**
 * Find the directory of an npm package as node would find it from a directory - in the `node_modules` directory of
 * that directory or of any enclosing it.
 * @param {String} name - The name of the package, which may be scoped
 * @param {String} fromDir - The absolute path of the directory
 * @return {String|null} The absolute path of the package's directory, or `null` if none is found
 */
fluid.findPackageDir = function (name, fromDir) {
    let dir = fromDir;
    let found;
    while (found === undefined) {
        const candidate = path.join(dir, "node_modules", name);
        const parent = path.dirname(dir);
        if (fs.existsSync(path.join(candidate, "package.json"))) {
            found = candidate;
        } else if (parent === dir) {
            found = null;
        } else {
            dir = parent;
        }
    }
    return found;
};

// Copy into a project the files of the modules which one of its pages depends upon, from checkouts of those modules,
// and write the module map through which the page locates them. A page refers to Infusion through its one bootstrap,
// <script src=".../FluidBoot.js">, and declares the module holding it, naming its module map, e.g.
//     <fluid-module id="my-project" src="../" modules="fluid-modules.json">
// Every other reference, within the page or the Single File Components it imports, is relative to the file making it,
// or is a module reference such as %imerss-bioinfo/src/client/sfc/bbea/hortis-beaVizLoader.vue or
// %maplibre-gl/dist/maplibre-gl-dev.js. The page is booted under node, as by hydrate.js, with the files of each module
// read from its checkout - the checkout given by --source, or else the directory where node finds the npm package of
// that name, from the project or any of the checkouts given. So all the Single File Components, scripts, stylesheets
// and data which it demands are discovered, together with whatever those stylesheets refer to. Each module is placed at
// the directory the map already gives it, or else at <vendor>/<module>, its demanded files are copied there, and the
// map is written to locate it. Infusion's own files are copied in the form in which the bootstrap is to be written.

// Usage: node copyOut.js <page.html>... --source <module>=<checkout> [--source ...] [--vendor <dir>] [--in-place]
//            [--framework boot|source|built] [-n] [--list] [--hydrate]

//                file, by --sources <file>, as an array of {moduleName, baseDir} as for moduleOverrides.json5, with
//                baseDir relative to the file
//   --vendor     The directory into which modules not yet located by the map are copied, by default "vendor" beside the

//   --hydrate    Also write each page's hydrated form beside it, as hydrate.js does

s=s[:a]+'''/**
 * Find the element of a page declaring the module which holds it, and naming its module map
 * @param {Document} dokkument - The page
 * @return {Object} Members `name`, the module's name, `dir`, the absolute path of its directory, and `mapFile`, that of
 * its map
 */
fluid.copyOut.ownModule = function (dokkument) {
    const node = dokkument.querySelector("fluid-module[modules]");
    if (!node) {
        fluid.fail("Page " + fileURLToPath(dokkument.location) + " declares no module holding it, with a map - e.g. " +
            "<fluid-module id=\\"my-project\\" src=\\"../\\" modules=\\"fluid-modules.json\\">");
    }
    const dirUrl = new URL(fluid.deSlash(node.getAttribute("src")) + "/", dokkument.location);
    return {
        name: node.getAttribute("id"),
        dir: fileURLToPath(dirUrl),
        mapFile: fileURLToPath(new URL(node.getAttribute("modules"), dirUrl))
    };
};

/**
 * Read a module map, if there is one
 * @param {String} mapFile - The absolute path of the map
 * @return {Object<String, String>} The map, empty if there is none
 */
fluid.copyOut.readMap = function (mapFile) {
    return fs.existsSync(mapFile) ? JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(mapFile, "utf8")) : {};
};

/**
 * Find the source of a module - the checkout given for it, or else the directory where node finds the npm package of
 * its name from any of a list of directories
 * @param {String} name - The module's name
 * @param {Object<String, String>} moduleSources - Map of module name to the absolute path of its checkout
 * @param {String[]} fromDirs - The directories from which packages are sought
 * @return {String|null} The absolute path of the module's source, or `null` if none is found
 */
fluid.copyOut.findSource = function (name, moduleSources, fromDirs) {
    return moduleSources[name] || fromDirs.map(dir => fluid.findPackageDir(name, dir)).find(dir => dir) || null;
};

/**
 * Boot a page under node, reading the files of its modules from their sources, and collect the files it demands
 * @param {String} pageFile - The absolute path of the page
 * @param {Object<String, String>} moduleSources - Map of module name to the absolute path of its checkout
 * @param {Object} options - Options as parsed from the command line, with members `vendor`, `inPlace` and `framework`
 * @param {Object<String, String>} map - The module map being written for the page's module, which is updated with
 * each module the page locates through it
 * @return {Promise<Object>} A promise for members `demands`, the absolute file: URLs of the files the page demands,
 * and `own`, the module holding the page, as returned by `fluid.copyOut.ownModule`
 */
fluid.copyOut.pageDemands = async function (pageFile, moduleSources, options, map) {
    const dokkument = fluid.serverDocumentParser(fs.readFileSync(pageFile, "utf8"));
    dokkument.location = pathToFileURL(pageFile);
    const own = fluid.copyOut.ownModule(dokkument);
    const fromDirs = [own.dir, ...Object.values(moduleSources)];
    const vendorDir = options.vendor ? path.resolve(options.vendor) : path.join(path.dirname(own.mapFile), "vendor");
    // The source of every module the map already locates, so that its files are read from there
    const sources = {...moduleSources};
    Object.keys(fluid.copyOut.readMap(own.mapFile)).forEach(name => {
        sources[name] = sources[name] || fluid.copyOut.findSource(name, moduleSources, fromDirs);
    });
    // A module referred to which the map does not yet locate is placed in the vendor directory, or where its source is
    fluid.module.unregisteredResolver = function (name) {
        const source = fluid.copyOut.findSource(name, moduleSources, fromDirs);
        if (source) {
            const dir = options.inPlace ? source : path.join(vendorDir, name);
            fluid.serverModuleSourcesById[name] = source;
            fluid.module.register(name, fluid.deSlash(pathToFileURL(dir).href), dir, false);
        }
    };
    const dokkumentFile = pageFile;
    const booted = fluid.loadAndBootDocument(dokkumentFile, {moduleSources: sources});
    const readiness = await fluid.documentWhenSettled(booted);
    if (fluid.isUnavailable(readiness)) {
        throw new Error("Reactive graph settled but document " + pageFile + " is not ready: " + JSON.stringify(readiness));
    }
    // Every module the page reached, other than its own and Infusion, which it reaches through its bootstrap, is
    // located by the map
    const mapDir = path.dirname(own.mapFile);
    Object.entries(fluid.module.modules).forEach(([name, record]) => {
        if (name !== own.name && name !== fluid.bootRecord.moduleName && record.url.startsWith("file:")) {
            map[name] = path.relative(mapDir, fileURLToPath(record.url)).split(path.sep).join("/");
        }
    });
    const infusion = fluid.module.modules[fluid.bootRecord.moduleName];
    const frameworkUrls = infusion ? fluid.bootFiles(options.framework).map(file => infusion.url + "/" + file) : [];
    if (options.hydratedFile) {
        fluid.writeBootScript(booted, options.framework);
        fluid.writeDocument(options.hydratedFile, booted);
    }
    return {
        own,
        demands: [pathToFileURL(pageFile).href, ...fluid.serverFetchedUrls, ...fluid.copyOut.documentRefs(booted), ...frameworkUrls]
    };
};

/**
 * Write a module map, unless it already holds exactly those entries
 * @param {String} mapFile - The absolute path of the map
 * @param {Object<String, String>} map - The map
 * @param {Boolean} dryRun - If `true`, nothing is written
 * @return {String} "new", "changed" or "unchanged"
 */
fluid.copyOut.writeMap = function (mapFile, map, dryRun) {
    const sorted = Object.fromEntries(Object.keys(map).sort().map(name => [name, map[name]]));
    const text = JSON.stringify(sorted, null, 4) + "\\n";
    const existing = fs.existsSync(mapFile) ? fs.readFileSync(mapFile, "utf8") : null;
    const status = existing === null ? "new" : existing === text ? "unchanged" : "changed";
    if (status !== "unchanged" && !dryRun) {
        fluid.writeFile(mapFile, text);
    }
    return status;
};

fluid.copyOut.main = async function (args) {
    const parsedArgs = minimist(args, {boolean: ["n", "list", "hydrate", "in-place"], string: ["source", "sources", "vendor", "framework"]});
    const pages = parsedArgs._.map(page => path.resolve(page));
    if (pages.length === 0) {
        console.error("Usage: node copyOut.js <page.html>... --source <module>=<checkout> [--sources <file>] [--vendor <dir>] " +
            "[--in-place] [--framework boot|source|built] [-n] [--list] [--hydrate]");
        process.exitCode = 1;
    } else {
        const moduleSources = fluid.copyOut.parseSources(parsedArgs);
        const demands = [];
        const maps = {};
        // Each page is booted in turn - the registries a booted page populates are global, so that those demanded by
        // a later page include those of earlier ones, which are all to be copied in any case
        for (const page of pages) {
            const options = {
                vendor: parsedArgs.vendor,
                inPlace: parsedArgs["in-place"],
                framework: parsedArgs.framework || "boot",
                hydratedFile: parsedArgs.hydrate ? page.replace(/\\.html$/, "-hydrated.html") : undefined
            };
            const dokkument = fluid.serverDocumentParser(fs.readFileSync(page, "utf8"));
            dokkument.location = pathToFileURL(page);
            const mapFile = fluid.copyOut.ownModule(dokkument).mapFile;
            maps[mapFile] = maps[mapFile] || {};
            const result = await fluid.copyOut.pageDemands(page, moduleSources, options, maps[mapFile]);
            demands.push(...result.demands);
        }
        const plan = parsedArgs["in-place"] ? [] : fluid.copyOut.plan(fluid.copyOut.closeDemands(demands));
        const counts = {new: 0, changed: 0, unchanged: 0, missing: 0};
        const projectDir = process.cwd();
        plan.forEach(entry => {
            ++counts[entry.status];
            if (parsedArgs.list || entry.status !== "unchanged") {
                console.log(entry.status + ": " + path.relative(projectDir, entry.target) +
                    (entry.source ? " <- " + path.relative(projectDir, entry.source) : ""));
            }
        });
        Object.entries(maps).forEach(([mapFile, map]) => {
            const status = fluid.copyOut.writeMap(mapFile, map, parsedArgs.n);
            console.log("module map " + status + ": " + path.relative(projectDir, mapFile));
        });
        if (!parsedArgs.n) {
            fluid.copyOut.execute(plan);
        }
        console.log(`\\n${counts.new} new, ${counts.changed} changed, ${counts.unchanged} unchanged, ${counts.missing} missing` +
            (parsedArgs.n ? " (dry run - nothing copied)" : ""));
        if (counts.missing > 0) {
            process.exitCode = 1;
        }
    }
};

import re
def convert(p, bootSrc, own, comment):
    s=open(p).read()
    s=re.sub(r'\s*<fluid-module id="infusion-6"[^>]*></fluid-module>','',s)
    lines=s.split("\n")
    out=[];done=False
    for l in lines:
        if 'fluid-hydrated="%infusion-6"' in l:
            if not done:
                ind=l[:len(l)-len(l.lstrip())]
                out.append(ind+'<!-- The one reference to the location of Infusion - every other is relative, or through a module -->')
                out.append(ind+'<script src="'+bootSrc+'"></script>')
                out.append(ind+comment)
                out.append(ind+own)
                done=True
            continue
        out.append(l)
    open(p,"w").write("\n".join(out))

CORE=re.compile(r'infusion-6/src/(lib/lezer/lezer-javascript-browser|framework/core/js/(FluidCore|FluidSignals|Fluid|FluidModules|FluidIL|FluidView|FluidPTF|FluidView-browser|template-parser|sfc-parser))\.js"')
def convert(p, up, ownSrc):
    s=open(p).read()
    lines=s.split("\n"); out=[]; done=False
    for l in lines:
        if '<fluid-module id="infusion-6"' in l or '<fluid-module id="imerss-bioinfo"' in l or "as the module within which its SFCs find the packages" in l:
            continue
        if "<script" in l and CORE.search(l):
            if not done:
                ind=l[:len(l)-len(l.lstrip())]
                out += [ind+'<!-- The one reference to the location of Infusion - every other is relative, or through a module -->',
                        ind+'<script src="'+up+'infusion-6/src/framework/core/js/FluidBoot.js"></script>',
                        ind+'<!-- This checkout, as the module holding the page, and its map of the modules it depends upon - see',
                        ind+'     Infusion 6\'s copyOut.js --in-place -->',
                        ind+'<fluid-module id="imerss-bioinfo" src="'+ownSrc+'" modules="fluid-modules.json"></fluid-module>']
                done=True
            continue
        out.append(l)
    assert done, p
    open(p,"w").write("\n".join(out))

     /**
      * Determine whether a script URL from an HTML driver refers to a local file which should be loaded. Remote libraries
      * and server-relative URLs which are served by a test server (e.g. /testem.js) are skipped.
      * @param {String} src - The `src` attribute of a script element
      * @return {Boolean} `true` if the script should be loaded
      */
     fQUnit.isLoadableScript = function (src) {
         return !/^([a-z]+:)?\/\//i.test(src) && !src.startsWith("/");
     };
     
     /**
      * Load the scripts of an HTML driver file into its context in document order
      * @param {Object} context - The context constructed by `fQUnit.makeBrowserContext`
      * @param {String} htmlPath - The absolute path of the HTML file
      */
     fQUnit.loadDocumentScripts = function (context, htmlPath) {
         const scripts = [...context.document.querySelectorAll("script")];
         scripts.forEach(script => {
             const src = script.getAttribute("src");
             if (src) {
                 if (fQUnit.isLoadableScript(src)) {
                     const scriptPath = fileURLToPath(new URL(src, context.location));
                     vm.runInContext(fs.readFileSync(scriptPath, "utf8"), context, {filename: scriptPath});
                 } else {
                     fQUnit.log("Skipping script " + src + " in " + path.basename(htmlPath));
                 }
             } else {
                 vm.runInContext(script.textContent, context, {filename: htmlPath});
             }
         });
     };

  ⎿  #### Copying out the files a page depends on
     
     A page in one project can use the SFCs of another by declaring that project as a module, in a directory of its own,
     and referring to its files through it:
     
     ```html
     <fluid-module id="infusion-6" src="vendor/infusion"></fluid-module>
     <fluid-module id="imerss-bioinfo" src="vendor/imerss-bioinfo"></fluid-module>
     <script src="vendor/infusion/src/framework/core/js/Fluid.js" fluid-hydrated="%infusion-6"></script>
     ...
     <fluid-import src="%imerss-bioinfo/src/client/sfc/bbea/hortis-beaVizLoader.vue"></fluid-import>
     ```
     
     `src/framework/server/copyOut.js` fills those directories from checkouts of the modules:
     
     ```
     node copyOut.js index.html --source infusion-6=../infusion-6 --source imerss-bioinfo=../bagatelle [-n] [--list]
     ```
     
     It boots the page under node, as `hydrate.js` does, with each module's files read from its checkout. It then copies
     into the module's declared directory every file the page demanded from it. These are:
     
     * the SFCs it imported, and those they import in turn;
     * the scripts and stylesheets they inject, including those bearing `fluid-client`, which are not run under node;
     * the framework scripts in the page's own markup;
     * the images and fonts its stylesheets refer to;
     * any data it fetched.
     
     Nothing else in the checkout is copied, and the page and its SFCs need no rewriting, since the files sit where they
     refer to them. Run again, it reports which files have changed in their checkouts, and with `-n` copies nothing. A
     file the page demands from outside any module, such as its own data, is not copied, but must exist. Sour
          ... [+35 more lines truncated]
● Bash: cd /home/amb26/Source/gits/ponder; sed -n 45,75p content/docs/fluid-view.md
  ⎿  </style>
     ```
     
     * `@{count}` in text or an attribute value binds live to the component's `count` member.
     * `@onclick="{self}.increment()"` invokes the component's `increment` method when the button is clicked.
     * `self.count++` writes through the component proxy into its live layer. The text node updates, and nothing else
       in the DOM is touched.
     
     To use it, declare the module and import the SFC in a host page, and mark an element with the layers to instantiate
     on it:
     
     ```html
     <head>
         <fluid-module id="infusion-6" src="../../"></fluid-module>
         <!-- Infusion core script tags here -->
         <fluid-module id="myApp" src="./"></fluid-module>
         <fluid-import src="%myApp/sfc/my-counter.vue"></fluid-import>
     </head>
     <body>
         <div fluid-layers="my.counter"></div>
     </body>
     ```
     
     * `<fluid-module id src>` registers a module root, referred to in paths as `%id`.
     * `<fluid-import src [layer]>` loads an SFC on demand. The layer name defaults to the file name with `-` replaced by
       `.`, so `my-counter.vue` must define `my.counter`.
     * `fluid-layers="layerA layerB"` on any element instantiates a component with those layers, rendering into that
       element. The element is watched live: elements added to the document later are booted too.
     
     A component can equally be created from JavaScript with `my.counter({container: element})`, which renders into
     `element`.

* Infusion's files, in the form `--framework` chooses - see below;

else in the checkouts is copied, and the page and its SFCs need no rewriting. Run again, it reports which files have

such as its own data, is not copied, but must exist. Sources may also be given by `--sources moduleOverrides.json5`,
an array of `{moduleName, baseDir}`.

served from a checkout - e.g. bagatelle's own pages, whose map points into its `node_modules`.

* `boot` (the default) - left as it is, to load Infusion's files in the browser;

● Pages now make exactly one reference outside their own module: the Infusion bootstrap. Everything else is relative within its module or written as `%module/...`, and where each module lives comes from an external module map. All suites pass and lint is clean.
  
  **Bootstrap.** A page carries one tag, e.g. `<script src="../vendor/infusion/src/framework/core/js/FluidBoot.js">`. In the browser, that script declares the `infusion-6` module at its own location and loads Infusion's files in order.
  - `hydrate.js --framework` and `copyOut.js --framework` choose how that tag is written out:
    - `boot` leaves it as it is.
    - `source` replaces it with Infusion's separate script files.
    - `built` replaces it with a bundle, `dist/fluid.boot.min.js`, which `build.js` now makes. copyOut copies whichever set of files is chosen.
  - The file list lives once, in `FluidBoot.js`, which node can also `require`. The server, the build and the QUnit runner all read it from there.
  
  **Every page declares its own module and map.** For example, `<fluid-module id="imerss-bioinfo" src="./" modules="fluid-modules.json">`.
  - **The map** is a JSON object locating each module, e.g. `"maplibre-gl": "vendor/maplibre-gl"`. Boot fetches it before acquiring the page's imports. If it can't be fetched, it's treated as empty, with a warning.
  - **References to packages** are now qualified by the package itself, e.g. `%maplibre-gl/...`, `%@mapbox/mapbox-gl-draw/...`, `%@imerss/inat-components/dist/standalone.min.js`. My earlier rule that resolved packages under the containing module's `node_modules` is gone.
  - **Scoped names** like `%@scope/name/` now resolve everywhere.
  
  **copyOut writes the maps:**
  - **Finding sources:** each module comes from its `--source` checkout, or else from wherever node finds an npm package of that name. The lookup starts from the page's module or any checkout given, so hoisted packages are found.
  - **Placing modules:** a module goes where the map already locates it, or else to `<vendor>/<module>`, by default `vendor` beside the map. copyOut then writes the map.
  - **`--in-place`:** copies nothing and writes a map pointing at each module where it already is. bagatelle's `fluid-modules.json` was made this way, and points into its `node_modules`.
  - **Results:** the howe-sound and saanich maps put every package under `static/vendor/<package>`, with nothing missing.

  - **Hugo layout:** `baseof.html` takes the module id from a new `siteModule` parameter in `hugo.yaml`, so the two projects' copies stay identical and `copyFrameworkOut.sh` still finds nothing to sync.

❯ Explain where the html files in story come from - e.g. Solow.html

● They're built in two steps: R writes the full page, then `storyBuild.js` cuts out the part the story page needs. Both directories are called `story`, which makes it look like one step.
  
  1. **R knits the pane.** `content/story/Solow.Rmd` names its own knit function in its front matter (`knit: ... source(here::here("R/knit_render.R")) ...`). Knitting it, through blogdown or RStudio's Knit, runs the R analysis and writes `content/story/Solow.html` beside it. That's a complete pandoc page: the pane's text, its htmlwidgets (plotly charts, maps) with their data embedded, and pandoc's page wrapper. This is the R pipeline's output; nothing in JavaScript writes it.
  
  2. **`storyBuild.js` cuts it up.** `npm run story` runs `node src/js/storyBuild.js content/story viz_data static/story`. For each `.Rmd` that has a knitted `.html`, taken in order of the front matter's `weight`, it writes:
     - **`static/story/Solow.html`:** just the pane's section, without the pandoc page around it and without the data of its map widgets. This is what you're seeing in `story/`.
     - **`static/story/<pane>-data.html`:** widgets carrying an `mx_widgetId`, which are shown in the data area beside the map, e.g. `History-data.html`.
     - **`static/story/panes.json`:** one record per pane, holding its front matter, its key and file names, and its map settings from `viz_data/<pane>-mapData.json`.
     - **`static/story/mapData.json`:** one map style holding every source and layer from all the panes' maps once, deduplicated, plus each pane's layers and camera.
     - **`static/story/img/`:** any images the sections refer to, e.g. `Hillshade_80m.jpg`.
  
     This is the same cutting and deduplicating that `reknit.js` did. The difference is that `reknit.js` wove the pieces into one page template, while `storyBuild.js` writes them as separate small files.
  
  3. **The story page fetches them.** In the browser, or in `hydrate.js`, `bioreportr-storyPage` reads `panes.json` and `mapData.json` from `storyBase`. Each `bioreportr-storyPane` fetches its own section, e.g. `Solow.html`, and renders its widgets with the htmlwidgets runtime. Hugo copies `static/story/` into the site unchanged.
  
  So `content/story/*.html` is the R pipeline's output and is the source to edit through R. `static/story/*.html` is generated from it, and `npm run story` regenerates it whenever the panes are re-knitted.

# Generated story material - do not edit

Apart from `index-dev.html`, every file in this directory is generated by `npm run story`, which runs
`src/js/storyBuild.js` over the story's knitted R Markdown:

    node src/js/storyBuild.js content/story viz_data static/story

Edits made here are overwritten the next time it runs. To change a pane, edit its R Markdown in `content/story/` and
knit it again - its front matter names `R/knit_render.R` as its knit function - then run `npm run story`.

## Where each file comes from

- `<pane>.html`, e.g. `Solow.html`, is the section of `content/story/<pane>.html`, the page R knits from
  `content/story/<pane>.Rmd`. The pandoc page around it is removed, and so is the data of its map widgets, which goes

- `<pane>-data.html`, e.g. `History-data.html`, holds the pane's widgets which bear an `mx_widgetId`. These are shown

  matter and file names, and any members of `viz_data/<pane>-mapData.json`.
- `mapData.json` is a single map style holding every source and layer of every pane's map once, together with each
  pane's layers, camera and fill patterns.
- `img/` holds copies of the images the panes' sections refer to, taken from `content/story/`.

The story page, `static/bioreportr/sfc/bioreportr-storyPage.vue`, fetches these files. Hugo publishes them unchanged.

## Not generated

`index-dev.html` is written by hand. It is a development page for the story, standing in for the page Hugo renders
from `layouts/story/baseof.html`.

● Writing the core part in `FluidView.js`: `fluid.renderingStatically` replaces `fluid.renderingPlaceholders`, alongside the `fluid.withPlaceholder` mixin and `fluid.jsonReader`.

● Bash: cd /home/amb26/Source/gits/infusion-6; python3 - <<'EOF'
p="src/framework/core/js/FluidView.js"
s=open(p).read()
old='''    // `true` whilst a document is being rendered with placeholders standing in for some of its data - e.g. by a static
    // build of the document, which fetches short files of the same shape in place of the data a live page will fetch
    // - see fluid.acquirePlaceholders in server-support.js. A component may then render as it should until its real data
    // arrives, e.g. by showing a loading indicator
    fluid.renderingPlaceholders = false;
'''
new='''    // `true` whilst a document is being rendered statically, e.g. by hydrate.js, rather than live in the browser - set
    // by fluid.loadAndBootDocument in server-support.js before the document is booted. A component bearing
    // fluid.withPlaceholder then fetches its placeholder in place of its genuine data
    fluid.renderingStatically = false;

    // A mixin for a component which fetches data from its `url`, as it does through its member `fetchUrl` - e.g.
    // fluid.jsonReader - supplying as `placeholderUrl` a short file of the same shape, which is fetched in its place when
    // the document is rendered statically. So the static rendering, e.g. a page written by hydrate.js, is rendered from
    // the placeholder, and is replaced once the page boots in the browser and fetches the genuine data. The component's
    // `isPlaceholder` is then `true`, so that it, or what holds it, can render as it should until its genuine data
    // arrives, e.g. by showing a loading indicator. Each such component is listed in fluid.withPlaceholder.instances, so
    // that the hydrater can find, without knowing the design, every file a page fetches and what stands in for it
    fluid.def("fluid.withPlaceholder", {
        // url: String - the genuine URL, relative to the document
        placeholderUrl: null,
        isPlaceholder: "$compute:fluid.withPlaceholder.isPlaceholder({self}.placeholderUrl)",
        fetchUrl: "$compute:fluid.withPlaceholder.fetchUrl({self}.url, {self}.placeholderUrl)",
        registration: {
            $bindable: {
                bind: "fluid.withPlaceholder.register({self})",
                unbind: "fluid.withPlaceholder.deregister({boundValue})"
            }
        }
    });

    /**
     * Determine whether a component bearing `fluid.withPlaceholder` fetches its placeholder in place of its genuine data
     * @param {String|null} placeholderUrl - The URL of its placeholder, if it has one
     * @return {Boolean} `true` if the document is rendered statically, and the component has a placeholder
     */
    fluid.withPlaceholder.isPlaceholder = placeholderUrl => fluid.renderingStatically && !!placeholderUrl;

    /**
     * Determine the URL fetched by a component bearing `fluid.withPlaceholder`
     * @param {String} url - Its genuine URL
     * @param {String|null} placeholderUrl - The URL of its placeholder, if it has one
     * @return {String} The URL of its placeholder if it is fetched in place of its genuine data, else its genuine URL
     */
    fluid.withPlaceholder.fetchUrl = (url, placeholderUrl) => fluid.withPlaceholder.isPlaceholder(placeholderUrl) ? placeholderUrl : url;

    // Each component bearing fluid.withPlaceholder which is live
    fluid.withPlaceholder.instances = new Set();

    fluid.withPlaceholder.register = function (that) {
        fluid.withPlaceholder.instances.add(that);
        return that;
    };

    fluid.withPlaceholder.deregister = function (that) {
        fluid.withPlaceholder.instances.delete(that);
    };

    /**
     * Determine whether any of a set of components bearing `fluid.withPlaceholder` fetches its placeholder - e.g. to
     * decide whether what holds them is rendering placeholder data
     * @param {...Boolean} isPlaceholders - The `isPlaceholder` member of each component
     * @return {Boolean} `true` if any of them fetches its placeholder
     */
    fluid.withPlaceholder.any = (...isPlaceholders) => isPlaceholders.some(isPlaceholder => isPlaceholder);

    // A loader for a JSON file at `url`. Its `data` member is pending until the file has been loaded and parsed. It
    // fetches its `fetchUrl`, which is its `url` unless it bears fluid.withPlaceholder
    fluid.def("fluid.jsonReader", {
        $layers: "fluid.component",
        // url: String
        fetchUrl: "{self}.url",
        data: "$compute:fluid.fetchJSON({self}.fetchUrl)"
    });
'''
assert old in s
s=s.replace(old,new)
open(p,"w").write(s)

  ⎿  A single host page, whose elements bear `fluid-layers` as in the browser, can be rendered from the command line:
     
     ```
     node src/framework/server/hydrate.js page.html [-o out.html]
     ```
     
     This boots the page as a browser would, waits for the graph to settle, and writes the rendered page, by default to
     `page-hydrated.html`. If the graph settles with the page still unready, it exits with an error listing the pending
     effects. Data fetched by `fluid.fetch` and its relatives, or by any asynchronous `$compute`, is waited for, and a
     relative URL is resolved against the page.
     
     #### Minimal pages and placeholder data
     
     A page need hold no more than its framework scripts, a `<fluid-import>` of the Single File Component at the root of
     its tree, and an element bearing `fluid-layers`. The SFCs it imports, and those they import in turn, supply all of its
     scripts, stylesheets, symbols and markup. Booted in the browser, such a page discovers them as its components are
     instantiated. Rendered by `hydrate.js`, the page is written with all of them in place, and the browser shows its markup
     as soon as it is parsed.
     
     Data which only a live page needs to load in full is named with a placeholder, a short file of the same shape:
     
     ```html
     <fluid-placeholder for="data/observations.csv" src="data/placeholder/observations.csv"></fluid-placeholder>
     ```
     
     When the page is rendered under node, data fetched from `for` is fetched from `src` instead, and
     `fluid.renderingPlaceholders` is `true`, so that a component can show that it is still loading. In the browser the
     element has no effect.

● Placeholders are now named where the data is named. Each genuine file path appears once, in the driver, with its placeholder beside it. Pages, `hugo.yaml` and the Hugo layout no longer mention data files. All suites pass and lint is clean.
  
  **The mixin.** `fluid.withPlaceholder` lives in Infusion's `FluidView.js` and goes on any reader that fetches its `fetchUrl`:
  ```js
  obsLoader: {
      $component: {
          $layers: ["hortis.csvReader", "fluid.withPlaceholder"],
          url: "{vizLoader}.obsFile",
          placeholderUrl: "{vizLoader}.obsPlaceholderFile"
      }
  }
  ```
  - **What it gives the reader:**
    - `placeholderUrl` (null by default).
    - `fetchUrl`: the placeholder when rendering statically, otherwise the genuine `url`.
    - `isPlaceholder`.
  - **Rendering statically:** `fluid.loadAndBootDocument` sets a new `fluid.renderingStatically` flag before booting under node. It replaces the old `fluid.renderingPlaceholders`, which only became true when a page held `<fluid-placeholder>` elements.
  - **Generic discovery:** each live component bearing the mixin registers itself in `fluid.withPlaceholder.instances`. `fluid.documentPlaceholders(dokkument)` in server-support lists each one's genuine and placeholder URL. The hydrater uses this without knowing anything about the page:
    - `hydrate.js` reports which placeholders it rendered from, for example `Rendered app-4.recordsReader from placeholder …/data/placeholder/records.json in place of …/data/records.json`.
    - copyOut demands both files. The genuine one is never fetched under node, so it previously came from `<fluid-placeholder for>`.
  - **New core reader:** `fluid.jsonReader`, with the same `url`/`fetchUrl` shape, joins `fluid.fetchJSON`. bagatelle's `hortis.csvReader` now fetches `fetchUrl` too.
  - **Removed:** `<fluid-placeholder>`, `fluid.acquirePlaceholders`, the URL substitution in `fluid.resolveServerFetchUrl`, and `fluid.renderingPlaceholders`.
  
  **Uses:**
  - **Readers with the mixin:**
    - `hortis.vizLoader`'s observation and taxa readers, and the region-indirection reader in all three loaders (Blitz/Diatoms, BBEA, story page).
    - Defaults are `obsPlaceholderFile`, `taxaPlaceholderFile` and `regionIndirectionPlaceholderFile`, all null.
  - **Loading state:** each loader's `loaded` is now computed from its readers' `isPlaceholder`, instead of the global flag.
  - **Drivers:** I moved the placeholder paths from the pages into the five drivers (the three bagatelle ones, howe-story, saanich-story), beside their genuine files.
  - **Pages:** `<fluid-placeholder>` is gone from the bagatelle pages, both `index-dev.html` pages and `baseof.html`, and `storyPlaceholders` from both `hugo.yaml` files.
  - **Infusion's round-trip fixture:** it now loads its records through `fluid.jsonReader` with the mixin.
  
  **Tests:**
  
  | Suite | Result |
  |---|---|
  | Infusion | 2195/2195 |
  | copyout-test | pass |
  | hydrate round trip (now checks the hydrater's placeholder report) | pass |
  | bagatelle QUnit suites | 65, 25, 49, 26 |
  | BBEA and Blitz/Diatoms round trips | pass |
  | Story navigation and round trip, both projects | pass |
  
  copyOut still finds the same 97 files for howe-sound, including the genuine data now located through the mixin.
  
  **Docs:** ponder's "Minimal pages and placeholder data" section now describes the mixin.
  
  **Watch out:** the `built` bootstrap bundle, `dist/fluid.boot.min.js`, goes stale whenever Infusion's core changes. copyout-test failed until I rebuilt it after this change. It's rebuilt by `node build.js` or by `makeJSBundle` for `bootSource`, and copyOut doesn't check whether it's current.

         $component: {
             $layers: "fluid.component",
             $for: {source: "{page}.stylesheets", valueAs: "sheet"},
             view: {
                 $component: {
                     $layers: "fluid.templateViewComponent",
                     template: `<link rel="stylesheet" href="@{sheet.href}">`
                 }
             }
         }
     }
     ```
     
     A layer may contribute a **partial template**, a fragment of markup composited into the template of any component
     bearing it, without replacing that template. This lets independent layers each add to, or take away from, a shared
     page structure such as a header. The component's view must bear `fluid.partialViewComponent` alongside its template
     layer:
     
     ```js
     fluid.def("my.header", {
         $layers: "fluid.component",
         view: {
             $component: {
                 $layers: ["fluid.templateViewComponent", "fluid.partialViewComponent"],
                 template: `<header><h1 class="title">@{title}</h1><nav @id="navbar"></nav><p class="strapline">...</p></header>`
             }
         }
     });
     
     fluid.def("my.header.post", {

                 relativeContainer: "after: h1.title",
                 partialTemplate: `<span class="date">@{date}</span>`

● Each of the six filter sections is now a `hortis.filterFacet` component. `views.js`, `valueFilter.js`, `resizeBar.js` and `shell.js` are broken up as you asked. All suites pass: the four bagatelle QUnit suites, the BBEA and Blitz round trips, the story navigation and round trips in both projects, all of Infusion's tests, and lint. Nothing is committed.
  
  **Facets**
  - **New file:** `sfc/bbea/hortis-filterFacet.vue` holds the section markup once. It takes three options:
    - `facet`, which sets `data-facet` and the body id `mf-f-<facet>`;
    - `name`, the heading text;
    - `body`, a plain component whose markup is supplied as its `template` option, with the section's filters as its own subcomponents.
  - **No separate SFCs for bodies:** each body is a small template option, e.g. `` `<div><div class="imerss-region-filter" @id="regionFilter"></div></div>` ``. Its root element merges onto the section's body element, so the collector section can hold both its filter and the report linker.
  - **The badge** is now computed by each facet from the filters inside it (`{self hortis.summarisedFilter}`). So filters no longer need a `facet` option, and I removed every one.
  - **The concertina** now only collapses everything: it finds all the facets and sets `open = false` on each. It moved out of the shell code into the facet SFC.
  - **The loader's template** now just has six `<section @id="...Facet">` slots. The loader file itself is only slightly shorter (441 → 419 lines), because the copied markup has become nested configuration.
  
  **Paths that changed**
  - **Filter paths:** filters now sit under their facet, e.g. `that.beeFacet.body.pollChecklist` and `that.regionFacet.body.regionFilter`. I updated the tests, `hortis-bipartite.vue` and the interactions wiring to match.
  - **Region filter grouping:** this is now a loader member, `regionLeadingFields`, so the BCBA driver and the tests just set that one value instead of overriding the nested filter.
  - **Body ids:** the shortened ids are now full names, e.g. `mf-f-coll` became `mf-f-collector`. No CSS used the old ids.
  
  **Where the JS went** (`src/client/js/i6`)
  
  | From | To |
  |---|---|
  | View-specific functions in `views.js` | Into their own SFCs: drawInteractions, bipartite, taxonListView, beeAbundance, seedMix. A duplicated `seedMix.keySet` was dropped. |
  | `resizeBar.js` | Into `hortis-resizeBar.vue` |
  | General helpers in `imerss-core.js`, plus the generic parts of `views.js` (image loading, SVG style inlining, reducers, `querySelectorIn`, bar charts) | New `utils.js`, loaded before `imerss-core.js` everywhere, including the story SFCs in both projects |
  | Taxon helpers from `views.js` and `valueFilter.js` (`ancestorAtRank`, `taxonLabel`, `idToTaxonLink`, `renderTaxonImage`, etc.) | The taxon-row section of `imerss-core.js` |
  | `bbeaView`, `pollColours`, `plantColours`, `computeRankColours` | `bbea/imerss-bbea.js` |
  | `shell.js`, minus the concertina | Renamed `bbea/mfShell.js`; it keeps `mfShell` and `downloadableView` |
  | `valueFilter` | Into `filters.js` |
  | The graminoid functions | `imerss-plants.js`, which the story page SFC now loads because the story configs name `hortis.graminoidValue` |
  
  **Also worth knowing**
  - **Judgement call:** I put the taxon helpers in `imerss-core.js` rather than `utils.js`, so that `utils.js` stays free of anything taxon-specific.
  - **Vendored copies:** copyOut never deletes files. The deleted `resizeBar.js` and `valueFilter.js` were still in both projects' `static/vendor`, so I removed them there, since nothing refers to them.
  - **Not moved:** `dataTable.js` still sits beside its SFC as a separate file, because you didn't mention it. It could be folded in the same way.

● Bash: cd /home/amb26/Source/gits; cat > /tmp/claude-1000/-home-amb26-Source-gits-bagatelle/dba32247-779e-45e2-b98b-d63581d4b6b6/scratchpad/sfcmove.py <<'EOF'
import os, re, glob, shutil
G = "/home/amb26/Source/gits/"
BAG = G + "bagatelle/"
SFC = BAG + "src/client/sfc/"
dest = {
 "components": ["core/hortis-autocomplete", "core/hortis-dataTable", "core/hortis-resizeBar", "bbea/hortis-dualRangeInput", "standard/hortis-pageTabs", "standard/hortis-pageTabs-tab"],
 "filters": ["core/hortis-collectorFilter", "core/hortis-filterControls", "core/hortis-standardFilterControls", "core/hortis-taxonSearchFilter",
   "core/hortis-valueFilter", "core/hortis-valueFilter-row", "standard/hortis-regionFilter", "standard/hortis-regionFilter-row",
   "bbea/hortis-groupedRegionFilter", "bbea/hortis-phenologyFilter", "bbea/hortis-phenologyFilter-row", "bbea/hortis-elevationFilter",
   "bbea/hortis-sexFilter", "bbea/hortis-filterFacet"],
 "core": ["standard/hortis-blitzRecords", "standard/hortis-blitzVizLoader", "standard/hortis-standardVizLoader", "standard/hortis-vizLibreMap", "bbea/hortis-taxonListView"],
}
moves = {}
for d, fs in dest.items():
    for f in fs:
        moves[SFC + f + ".vue"] = SFC + d + "/" + os.path.basename(f) + ".vue"
moves[SFC + "bbea/hortis-viewTabs.vue"] = SFC + "bbea/hortis-bbeaViewTabs.vue"
files = glob.glob(SFC + "**/*.vue", recursive=True) + glob.glob(BAG + "drivers/*.vue") + glob.glob(BAG + "test/i6/html/*.html") + glob.glob(BAG + "*.html")
for P in ["howe-sound-mapping-2026", "saanich-peninsula-flora"]:
    files += glob.glob(G + P + "/static/bioreportr/**/*.vue", recursive=True) + glob.glob(G + P + "/static/local/**/*.vue", recursive=True) + glob.glob(G + P + "/static/story/*.html") + glob.glob(G + P + "/layouts/**/*.html", recursive=True)
attr = re.compile(r'((?:src|href)=")([^"]+)(")')
for f in files:
    newf = moves.get(f, f)
    t = open(f).read()
    def fix(m):
        ref = m.group(2)
        if ref.startswith("%imerss-bioinfo/"):
            tgt = BAG + ref[len("%imerss-bioinfo/"):]
            nt = moves.get(tgt)
            return m.group(1) + ("%imerss-bioinfo/" + os.path.relpath(nt, BAG) if nt else ref) + m.group(3)
        if re.match(r"^(https?:|%|/|#|\{|@|data:)", ref) or ref.startswith("{{"):
            return m.group(0)
        tgt = os.path.normpath(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(f), ref))
        nt = moves.get(tgt, tgt)
        if nt == tgt and newf == f:
            return m.group(0)
        trail = "/" if ref.endswith("/") else ""
        return m.group(1) + os.path.relpath(nt, os.path.dirname(newf)) + trail + m.group(3)
    t2 = attr.sub(fix, t)
    if t2 != t:
        open(f, "w").write(t2)
for o, n in moves.items():
    shutil.move(o, n)
os.rmdir(SFC + "standard")
EOF

❯ Move dataTable.js into its SFC too - remove the "mf" from name of mfIcons and from its ids because this suggests it is bbea-specific. In general remove the prefix mf- from anything not in bbeas and use imerss instead, check that every SVG symbol's id has some kind of prefix since these are dumped in a global namespace. New functionality: use the new hashManager system to make sure that every active filter pushes its filter state into the URL. Try to do this without intruding on them with references the hashManager - one can just derive them from a fresh layer name such as "urlMappedFilter", each one can default to deriving a url key from its last path segment nickname minus the text "Filter" and in most cases the filterState will be sufficient to serialise directly into the URL. Some will need special treatment such as taxon filters, try to economise on URL space by writing a codec which accepts comma-separated taxon ids. The polygon filter can use a scheme such as WKT to encode its polygon compactly. The hashManager, if it is instantiated, can then broadcast a $linkage to every urlMappedFilter, which then produces the actual reactive connection with it. We'll have problems with filters such as hortis.elevationFilter which already have their filterState slot used up by a $compute. There's enough functionality in the signals system to represent the kind of graph we want, but it is currently hard to address it via the existing $compute syntax. What we're going to have to do is construct a new $lens construct which can accept matching forward and backward arcs of a relation in one spot. This will then let us shift, for example in elevationFilter, the responsibility for maintaining both arcs synchronising with dualRangeInput onto a $lens def written overlaying elevationFilter.dualRangeinput.range - this then leaves the filterState slot itself free for connecting, via the linkage, to {hashManager}.hash.elevation - this scheme still isn't fully open but should be enough to get us out of immediate trouble. This eventually paves the way to "follow fish upstream" across other reactive relations other than simply references. This work might already require some tinkering with the "identity" system used to distinguish amongst multiple edges at a site, which currently uses a somewhat ad hoc system derived from the first staticSource in the edge - the stable notion of this would be derived from the cell's path in the component tree, but perhaps we can make a system continue to work through the current semantic and just expect that these edges will be torn down and reconstructed when the component turns over in a way which allocates a new compute cell at a site.

import re, glob, os
B = "/home/amb26/Source/gits/bagatelle/"
C = B + "src/client/"
nonBbea = glob.glob(C+"sfc/core/*.vue")+glob.glob(C+"sfc/components/*.vue")+glob.glob(C+"sfc/filters/*.vue")+glob.glob(C+"js/i6/*.js")
tok = re.compile(r"(?<![\w-])mf-[a-zA-Z0-9]+(?:-[a-zA-Z0-9]+)*")
names = set()
for f in nonBbea:
    for m in tok.finditer(open(f).read()):
        names.add(m.group(0))
names.discard("mf-f-")
# all files to rewrite
targets = glob.glob(C+"sfc/**/*.vue", recursive=True)+glob.glob(C+"js/i6/**/*.js", recursive=True)+[C+"css/imerss-bbea.css", C+"css/imerss-i6.css", C+"css/imerss-core.css"]+\
   glob.glob(B+"test/i6/**/*.js", recursive=True)+glob.glob(B+"test/i6/*.js")+glob.glob(B+"drivers/*.vue")+glob.glob(B+"*-6.html")
for P in ["howe-sound-mapping-2026", "saanich-peninsula-flora"]:
    targets += glob.glob("/home/amb26/Source/gits/"+P+"/static/bioreportr/**/*.*", recursive=True)+glob.glob("/home/amb26/Source/gits/"+P+"/static/local/**/*.vue", recursive=True)
targets = sorted(set(t for t in targets if os.path.isfile(t) and t.endswith((".vue",".js",".css",".html"))))
alltext = "".join(open(t).read() for t in targets)
# whole-token rename: mf-foo -> imerss-foo, also mf-foo-bar where mf-foo in names covers prefix families
rename = {n: "imerss-" + n[3:] for n in names}
clash = [v for v in rename.values() if re.search(r"(?<![\w-])"+re.escape(v)+r"(?![\w-])", alltext)]
print("renaming", len(rename), "clashes", clash)
# symbols
symIds = set(re.findall(r'<symbol id="([^"]+)"', alltext))
symRename = {s: ("imerss-i-" + s[5:] if s.startswith("mf-i-") else "imerss-i-" + s.replace("-icon", "")) for s in symIds}
print(symRename)
def apply(t):
    for s, n in symRename.items():
        t = re.sub(r'(<symbol id=")' + re.escape(s) + '"', r"\g<1>" + n + '"', t)
        t = re.sub(r'#' + re.escape(s) + r'(?![\w-])', "#" + n, t)
    t = tok.sub(lambda m: rename.get(m.group(0), m.group(0)), t)
    t = t.replace('"mf-f-@{facet}"', '"imerss-facet-@{facet}"')
    t = t.replace("hortis.mfIcons", "hortis.icons").replace("hortis-mfIcons.vue", "hortis-icons.vue")
    return t
for f in targets:
    t = open(f).read(); n = apply(t)
    if n != t:
        open(f, "w").write(n)
os.rename(C+"sfc/core/hortis-mfIcons.vue", C+"sfc/core/hortis-icons.vue")
print(sorted(names))
EOF
