p = "FluidIL.js"
t = open(p).read()
anchor = "    /**\n     * Flatten each of a set of resolved arguments within a computed cell of its own."
lens = '''    /**
     * Upgrade an arc of a `$lens` record, which may be a compact string or a function record, to a function record
     * @param {String|FuncRecord} arc - The arc
     * @param {String} type - The type of compact record it is parsed as, "$compute" or "$method"
     * @return {FuncRecord} The arc as a function record
     */
    fluid.expandLensArc = function (arc, type) {
        return typeof(arc) === "string" ? fluid.compactStringToRec(arc, type) : arc;
    };

    /**
     * Expands a lens record into a cell holding a view of the value held at another site, its `source`, together with
     * the means of writing back through the view. A lens names the matching forward and backward arcs of a relation in
     * one spot:
     *  - `source` - a context reference to the site viewed, e.g. "{elevationFilter}.filterState"
     *  - `forward` - a compute-style record computing the lens's value, in whose arguments `{0}` designates the value
     *    of the source, e.g. "hortis.elevationFilter.toRange({0}, {self}.minRange, {self}.maxRange)"
     *  - `backward` - a method-style record computing the source's value from a value written to the lens, which it
     *    receives as `{0}`, e.g. "hortis.elevationFilter.toState({0}, {self}.minRange, {self}.maxRange)"
     * A write to the lens's site, or beneath it, is not held locally - the lens's value with the write applied is
     * passed through the backward arc, and the result is written to the source's site, following any references
     * upstream from it, as for a write to a member defined by a reference. The lens's value then follows from its
     * source along the forward arc - see `fluid.putThroughLens`.
     * @param {Object} record - The lens record, holding `source`, `forward` and `backward`
     * @param {Shadow} shadow - The shadow of the component holding the lens
     * @param {String[]} segs - The path where this record appears in its component
     * @return {Cell<any>} A computed cell holding the lens's value, which includes a `$variety` property set to "$lens"
     */
    fluid.expandLensRecord = function (record, shadow, segs) {
        const lensSegs = [...segs, "$lens"];
        const source = fluid.fetchContextReference(record.source, shadow, [...lensSegs, "source"]);
        const forward = fluid.expandLensArc(record.forward, "$compute");
        const func = fluid.resolveFuncReference(forward, shadow, [...lensSegs, "forward"]);
        const argSegs = [...lensSegs, "forward", "args"];
        const resolvedArgs = fluid.makeArray(forward.args).map((arg, i) =>
            arg === "{0}" ? source : fluid.resolveArgMaterial(arg, shadow, [...argSegs, i]));
        const name = `$lens at path ${segs} of component at path ${shadow.path}`;
        const togo = fluid.cell(undefined, {name}).computed(fluid.makeFuncDispatcher(func), fluid.flattenedArgCells(resolvedArgs, name));
        togo.$variety = "$lens";
        togo.lensSource = source;
        togo.backward = fluid.expandMethodRecord(fluid.expandLensArc(record.backward, "$method"), shadow, [...lensSegs, "backward"]);
        return togo;
    };

    /**
     * Find the site of a lens at or above a path within a component, if there is one
     * @param {Shadow} shadow - The shadow of the component
     * @param {String[]} segs - The path within the component
     * @return {Object|null} Members `lens`, the lens's cell, and `length`, the number of segments of the path which
     * designate its site, or `null` if no lens is found
     */
    fluid.findLensSite = function (shadow, segs) {
        let node = shadow.shadowMap;
        let togo = null;
        for (let i = 0; i < segs.length && node && !togo; ++i) {
            node = node[segs[i]];
            const rec = node?.[$m];
            if (rec?.handlerRecord?.key === "$lens" && rec.signalProduct) {
                togo = {lens: rec.signalProduct, length: i + 1};
            }
        }
        return togo;
    };

    /**
     * Find the site from which a signal draws its value, by following its chain of signals upstream to the last
     * `$sitedRef` within it
     * @param {Signal} signal - The signal
     * @return {Site|null} The site, or `null` if the signal is not drawn from any site
     */
    fluid.terminalSiteOf = function (signal) {
        let ref = signal, site = null;
        while (fluid.isSignal(ref) && ref.$variety !== "$component") {
            if (ref.$variety === "$sitedRef") {
                site = ref.site;
            }
            ref = ref.get(ref.$variety === "$bareValue");
        }
        return site;
    };

    /**
     * Write a value through a lens - the lens's current value with the value applied at a path within it is passed
     * through its backward arc, and the result written to the site of its source. See `fluid.expandLensRecord`.
     * @param {Cell} lens - The lens's cell
     * @param {String[]} innerSegs - The path within the lens's value at which the value is written
     * @param {any} value - The value to be written
     * @return {Cell} The lens's cell
     */
    fluid.putThroughLens = function (lens, innerSegs, value) {
        fluid.cell.untracked(() => {
            const current = fluid.deSignal(lens);
            if (innerSegs.length > 0 && fluid.isUnavailable(current)) {
                fluid.fail(`Cannot write to path ${innerSegs.join(".")} beneath ${lens.name} whose value is unavailable`);
            }
            const updated = innerSegs.length === 0 ? value : fluid.setImmutable(current, innerSegs, value);
            const sourceValue = lens.backward(updated);
            const site = fluid.terminalSiteOf(lens.lensSource);
            if (!site) {
                fluid.fail(`Cannot write through ${lens.name} since its source is not drawn from any site`);
            }
            fluid.setForComponent(site.shadow.that, site.segs, sourceValue);
        });
        return lens;
    };

'''

fluid.tests.lensedRange.toState = (range, min, max) => range.min === min && range.max === max ? null : {lower: range.min, upper: range.max};

QUnit.test("A $lens laid over a reactive root relates it to its source in both directions", function (assert) {
    const that = fluid.tests.lensedRange({$layers: "fluid.tests.lensedRange.lensed"});
    fluid.cell.stabilize();
    assert.deepEqual({...that.input.range}, {min: 0, max: 100}, "Lens follows the bounds whilst the source holds no state");
    that.input.range.min = 20;
    fluid.cell.stabilize();
    assert.deepEqual(that.filterState, {lower: 20, upper: 100}, "Write beneath the lens is applied to its source through the backward arc");
    assert.deepEqual({...that.input.range}, {min: 20, max: 100}, "Lens follows its source along the forward arc");
    assert.deepEqual({...that.rangeSeen}, {min: 20, max: 100}, "Computation reading the lens is notified");
    that.filterState = {lower: 30, upper: 60};
    fluid.cell.stabilize();
    assert.deepEqual({...that.input.range}, {min: 30, max: 60}, "Write to the source is seen through the lens");
    that.input.range = {min: 0, max: 100};
    fluid.cell.stabilize();
    assert.equal(that.filterState, null, "Write of the whole lens restores the source's empty state");
    that.destroy();
});

● Bash: cd /home/amb26/Source/gits/bagatelle/src/client/js/i6; cat >> filters.js <<'EOF'

/** Filters whose state is held in the URL **/

/**
 * A codec translating a filter's state to and from the text held for it in the URL's hash.
 * @typedef {Object} UrlCodec
 * @property {Function} encode - Accepts a filter state and returns its text, or `undefined` if the state is empty and
 * nothing is to be held in the URL
 * @property {Function} decode - Accepts the text held in the URL, which is `undefined` if there is none, and returns
 * the filter state - the empty state if there is no text
 */

// A filter whose state is held in the URL's hash once the page has a hash manager - see hashManager.js, whose
// $linkage lays hortis.urlMappedFilter.linked over every component bearing this layer. The filter itself need know
// nothing of the URL, beyond the key under which its state is held and the codec translating it
fluid.def("hortis.urlMappedFilter", {
    $layers: "fluid.component",
    // The key under which the filter's state is held in the hash - by default, its member name with any trailing
    // "Filter" removed, e.g. "collector" for a filter held at member collectorFilter
    urlKey: "$compute:hortis.urlMappedFilter.urlKey({self})",
    // The global name of the UrlCodec translating the filter's state
    urlCodec: "hortis.urlCodecs.string"
});

// Laid over a hortis.urlMappedFilter by the hash manager's $linkage - the filter's state becomes a view of its entry
// in the hash, so that writing the state writes the URL, and navigating the URL's history restores the state
fluid.def("hortis.urlMappedFilter.linked", {
    filterState: {
        $lens: {
            source: "{hashManager}.hash",
            forward: "hortis.urlMappedFilter.decode({0}, {self}.urlKey, {self}.urlCodec)",
            backward: "hortis.urlMappedFilter.encode({0}, {hashManager}.hash, {self}.urlKey, {self}.urlCodec)"
        }
    }
});

/**
 * Derive the default key under which a filter's state is held in the URL from the member name at which it is held.
 * @param {fluid.component} that - The filter
 * @return {String} The member name with any trailing "Filter" removed
 */
hortis.urlMappedFilter.urlKey = function (that) {
    const memberName = String(that[fluid.metadataSymbol].memberName);
    return memberName.endsWith("Filter") && memberName !== "Filter" ? memberName.slice(0, -"Filter".length) : memberName;
};

hortis.urlMappedFilter.decode = function (hash, urlKey, urlCodec) {
    return fluid.getGlobalValue(urlCodec).decode(hash[urlKey]);
};

/**
 * Write a filter's state into the URL's hash.
 * @param {any} filterState - The filter's state
 * @param {Object} hash - The current hash
 * @param {String} urlKey - The key under which the state is held
 * @param {String} urlCodec - The global name of the codec translating the state
 * @return {Object} The updated hash, from which the key is removed if the state is empty
 */
hortis.urlMappedFilter.encode = function (filterState, hash, urlKey, urlCodec) {
    const encoded = fluid.getGlobalValue(urlCodec).encode(filterState);
    const togo = {...hash};
    if (encoded === undefined) {
        delete togo[urlKey];
    } else {
        togo[urlKey] = encoded;
    }
    return togo;
};

fluid.registerNamespace("hortis.urlCodecs");

// A state which is a String, or null if the filter is inactive
hortis.urlCodecs.string = {
    encode: state => state === null || state === undefined || state === "" ? undefined : String(state),
    decode: text => text === undefined || text === "" ? null : String(text)
};

// A state which is a hash of keys to true, e.g. the selected values of a filter or the ids of selected taxa, held as
// the keys separated by commas
hortis.urlCodecs.keys = {
    encode: function (state) {
        const keys = Object.keys(state || {}).filter(key => state[key]);
        return keys.length === 0 ? undefined : keys.join(",");
    },
    decode: text => text === undefined || text === "" ? {} : Object.fromEntries(String(text).split(",").map(key => [key, true]))
};

/**
 * Construct a codec for a state which is a fixed set of Boolean flags, held as the names of those which are set
 * separated by commas.
 * @param {String[]} flags - The names of the flags
 * @return {UrlCodec} The codec, whose decoded state holds every flag
 */
hortis.urlCodecs.flags = function (flags) {
    return {
        encode: hortis.urlCodecs.keys.encode,
        decode: function (text) {
            const keys = hortis.urlCodecs.keys.decode(text);
            return Object.fromEntries(flags.map(flag => [flag, !!keys[flag]]));
        }
    };
};

// A state which is a numeric range with members `lower` and `upper`, or null if unrestricted, held as "lower,upper"
hortis.urlCodecs.range = {
    encode: state => state ? state.lower + "," + state.upper : undefined,
    decode: function (text) {
        const bounds = text === undefined ? [] : String(text).split(",").map(Number);
        return bounds.length === 2 && bounds.every(bound => !isNaN(bound)) ? {lower: bounds[0], upper: bounds[1]} : null;
    }
};

// A state which is a taxon row, or null, held as the taxon's id - the decoded state holds the id alone
hortis.urlCodecs.taxonRow = {
    encode: state => state ? String(state.id) : undefined,
    decode: text => text === undefined || text === "" ? null : {id: String(text)}
};
EOF

/** Polygons held in the URL **/

// The number of decimal places to which the coordinates of polygons held in the URL are rounded - about a metre
hortis.urlCodecs.polygonPrecision = 5;

/**
 * Render the rings of a polygon as Well-Known Text, without its type.
 * @param {Number[][][]} rings - The polygon's rings, each an array of [longitude, latitude] positions
 * @return {String} The rings, e.g. "((-123.1 49.2,-123.2 49.3,-123.1 49.2))"
 */
hortis.urlCodecs.ringsToWKT = function (rings) {
    const round = value => +value.toFixed(hortis.urlCodecs.polygonPrecision);
    return "(" + rings.map(ring => "(" + ring.map(([lng, lat]) => round(lng) + " " + round(lat)).join(",") + ")").join(",") + ")";
};

/**
 * Parse the rings of a polygon rendered by hortis.urlCodecs.ringsToWKT.
 * @param {String} text - The rings, with their enclosing parentheses
 * @return {Number[][][]} The polygon's rings
 */
hortis.urlCodecs.WKTToRings = function (text) {
    return [...text.matchAll(/\\(([^()]+)\\)/g)].map(match => match[1].split(",").map(position => position.trim().split(/\\s+/).map(Number)));
};

// The polygons drawn on the map, as the features of a GeoJSON FeatureCollection, held as Well-Known Text - a POLYGON
// for one polygon, or a MULTIPOLYGON for several
hortis.urlCodecs.polygons = {
    encode: function (features) {
        const polygons = (features || []).filter(feature => feature.geometry?.type === "Polygon").map(feature => hortis.urlCodecs.ringsToWKT(feature.geometry.coordinates));
        return polygons.length === 0 ? undefined : polygons.length === 1 ? "POLYGON" + polygons[0] : "MULTIPOLYGON(" + polygons.join(",") + ")";
    },
    decode: function (text) {
        let polygons = [];
        if (typeof(text) === "string" && text.startsWith("MULTIPOLYGON(")) {
            polygons = [...text.slice("MULTIPOLYGON(".length, -1).matchAll(/\\((\\([^()]+\\)(?:,\\([^()]+\\))*)\\)/g)].map(match => match[0]);
        } else if (typeof(text) === "string" && text.startsWith("POLYGON(")) {
            polygons = [text.slice("POLYGON".length)];
        }
        return polygons.map((polygon, i) => ({
            id: "url-polygon-" + i,
            type: "Feature",
            properties: {},
            geometry: {type: "Polygon", coordinates: hortis.urlCodecs.WKTToRings(polygon)}
        }));
    }
};
'''
open(p, "w").write(t)

  ⎿  /* global hortis */
     
     "use strict";
     
     // Support shared by the tests of the BBEA visualisation, which load it from its Single File Components
     
     fluid.registerNamespace("hortis.tests");
     
     /**
      * Load every Single File Component imported by the page, and those they import in turn, and inject them into the
      * document, so that tests may instantiate their layers synchronously. SFCs are discovered as their importers are parsed,
      * so this repeats until no further import appears. The page's imports are acquired once its module map has been
      * fetched, which is first awaited.
      * @return {Promise} Resolves once every imported SFC has been injected
      */
     hortis.tests.loadAllImports = async function () {
         await fluid.cell.settle();
         let layerNames = [];
         while (layerNames.length !== Object.keys(fluid.importMap).length) {
             layerNames = Object.keys(fluid.importMap);
             await Promise.all(layerNames.map(layerName => fluid.cell.waitFor(fluid.subscribeDocToInjections(layerName, document))));
             await fluid.cell.settle();
         }
     };
     
     /**
      * The element in the QUnit fixture into which a test renders the visualisation
      * @return {Element} The element
      */
     hortis.tests.root = () => document.querySelector("#qunit-fixture .bbea-root");

QUnit.test("Filter states are held in the URL", function (assert) {
    const that = hortis.tests.bbeaLoader({container: hortis.tests.root()});
    fluid.cell.stabilize();
    const hashManager = fluid.hashManager.instance;
    const hash = () => ({...hashManager.hash});
    assert.deepEqual(hash(), {}, "Nothing is held in the URL whilst no filter is active");

    const checklist = that.beeFacet.body.pollChecklist;
    checklist.check("10", true);
    fluid.cell.stabilize();
    assert.deepEqual(hash(), {bees: "10"}, "Selecting a family holds its id alone, and not those of its descendants");
    assert.equal(window.location.hash, "#bees:10", "The selection is pushed into the URL");
    checklist.check("13", false);
    fluid.cell.stabilize();
    assert.deepEqual(hash().bees.split(",").sort(), ["12", "14"].filter(id => checklist.idToEntry[id]).sort(),
        "Deselecting a species within the family holds its selected siblings in place of the family");
    checklist.reset();

    const elevation = that.elevationFacet.body.elevationFilter;
    hortis.tests.input(qs(".imerss-elevation-filter .dual-range-max"), "950");
    assert.equal(hash().elevation, "100,950", "Moving the dual range input writes the elevation range through its lens to the URL");
    assert.deepEqual(elevation.filterState, {lower: 100, upper: 950}, "The filter's state is a view of its entry in the URL");
    elevation.reset();
    fluid.cell.stabilize();
    assert.equal(hash().elevation, undefined, "Resetting the filter removes its entry from the URL");
    assert.deepEqual({...elevation.dualRangeInput.range}, {min: 100, max: 1500}, "Input returns to the full range");

    that.phenologyFacet.body.phenologyFilter.monthRows[5].toggle?.(true);
    hortis.tests.click(qsa(".imerss-phenology-filter input")[5]);
    assert.equal(hash().phenology, "6", "Checking a month holds its number in the URL");
    checklist.extraFilter.filterState.female = true;
    fluid.cell.stabilize();
    assert.equal(hash().sex, "female", "Checking a sex holds its name in the URL");
    that.collectorFacet.body.collectorFilter.confirmAutocomplete("Charles Babbage");
    fluid.cell.stabilize();
    assert.equal(hash().collector, "Charles Babbage", "Choosing a collector holds the name in the URL");

    // As when the user navigates the URL's history
    hashManager.hash = {region: "2", elevation: "200,800", plants: "103"};
    fluid.cell.stabilize();
    assert.deepEqual({...that.regionFacet.body.regionFilter.filterState}, {2: true}, "Region filter follows the URL");
    assert.deepEqual({...elevation.dualRangeInput.range}, {min: 200, max: 800}, "Elevation filter's input follows the URL through both lenses");
    assert.equal(that.plantFacet.body.plantChecklist.idToState["103"].selected, "selected", "Plant checklist follows the URL");
    assert.equal(that.collectorFacet.body.collectorFilter.filterState, null, "Filter absent from the URL reverts to its empty state");
    assert.equal(that.phenologyFacet.body.phenologyFilter.filterState[5].checked, false, "Month absent from the URL is unchecked");
    that.destroy();
});

QUnit.test("Codecs of filter states", function (assert) {
    const codecs = hortis.urlCodecs;
    assert.deepEqual(codecs.keys.decode(codecs.keys.encode({a: true, b: false, c: true})), {a: true, c: true}, "Keys round trip");
    assert.equal(codecs.keys.encode({}), undefined, "Empty hash of keys is held as nothing");
    assert.deepEqual(hortis.sexFilter.urlCodec.decode(undefined), {male: false, female: false}, "Flags decode to every flag");
    assert.deepEqual(codecs.range.decode("1,2"), {lower: 1, upper: 2}, "Range decodes");
    assert.equal(codecs.range.decode("junk"), null, "Malformed range decodes to none");
    const features = [{geometry: {type: "Polygon", coordinates: [[[-123.1234567, 49.1], [-123.2, 49.3], [-123, 49.2], [-123.1234567, 49.1]]]}},
        {geometry: {type: "Polygon", coordinates: [[[1, 2], [3, 4], [5, 6], [1, 2]]]}}];
    const wkt = codecs.polygons.encode(features);
    assert.equal(wkt, "MULTIPOLYGON(((-123.12346 49.1,-123.2 49.3,-123 49.2,-123.12346 49.1)),((1 2,3 4,5 6,1 2)))", "Polygons encoded as WKT");
    assert.deepEqual(codecs.polygons.decode(wkt).map(feature => feature.geometry.coordinates),
        [[[[-123.12346, 49.1], [-123.2, 49.3], [-123, 49.2], [-123.12346, 49.1]]], [[[1, 2], [3, 4], [5, 6], [1, 2]]]], "WKT decoded to polygons");
    assert.equal(codecs.polygons.encode([features[1]]), "POLYGON((1 2,3 4,5 6,1 2))", "A single polygon is a POLYGON");
    assert.deepEqual(hortis.phenologyFilter.urlCodec.decode("1,12").filter(range => range.checked).map(range => range.month),
        ["January", "December"], "Months decoded by number");
});

  ⎿  ## Signal directives
     
     A signal record is an object with a single key starting with `$`, or equivalently a **compact string**
     `"$type:body"`. Function-bearing records share the **function record** syntax:
     
     ```js
     {func: "my.global.fn", args: ["{self}.a", 3]}   // full form
     "$compute:my.global.fn({self}.a, 3)"            // compact form
     ```
     
     * `func` - A global function name, a [reference](#references) to a function (e.g. `"{self}.helper"`), or a function value.
     * `args` - Array (or single value) of argument material. References anywhere within it, including inside nested
       objects and arrays, are resolved.
     * In compact form, arguments are split on commas and coerced: `3` → number, `true` → boolean, otherwise a string or
       reference. Use the full form for arguments containing commas, parentheses or structure.
     
     ### $compute
     
     A value computed by a pure function from its resolved arguments. Recomputed lazily whenever any argument changes.
     If any argument is unavailable the function is not called and the value is unavailable.
     
     ```js
     fluid.def("my.rect", {
         $layers: "fluid.component",
         width: 3,
         height: 4,
         area: "$compute:my.multiply({self}.width, {self}.height)"
     });
     my.multiply = (a, b) => a * b;
     
     const r = my.rect();
     r.area;          // 12
     r.width = 5;
     r.area;          // 20
     ```
     
     The function may be asynchronous: if it returns a `Promise` or async iterator, e.g. as an `async` or `async*` function
     does, the value is pending until the promise settles or the first value is yielded, and is then the value it resolves
     to or yields. Computations depending on it are not run
          ... [+5 more lines truncated]
● Bash: cd /home/amb26/Source/gits/ponder/content/docs; python3 - <<'EOF'
p = "fluid-integration-language.md"
t = open(p).read()
anchor = "### $effect\n"
doc = '''### $lens

A value which is a view of the value held at another site, its **source**, through a relation whose forward and
backward arcs are written together in one spot. Unlike a `$compute`, a lens may be written - a write to it, or beneath
it, is applied to its source:

```js
range: {
    $lens: {
        source: "{elevationFilter}.filterState",
        forward: "my.toRange({0}, {self}.minRange, {self}.maxRange)",
        backward: "my.toState({0}, {self}.minRange, {self}.maxRange)"
    }
}
```

* `source` - A [reference](#references) to the site viewed.
* `forward` - A compute-style function record computing the lens's value, in whose arguments `{0}` designates the value
  of the source. It is recomputed whenever any of its arguments changes, as for `$compute`.
* `backward` - A method-style function record computing the source's new value from a value written to the lens, which
  it receives as `{0}`.

A write to the lens, e.g. `that.range.min = 20` or `that.range = {min: 0, max: 100}`, is applied to the lens's current
value, passed through `backward`, and the result is written to the source's site - following the fish upstream, as for
a write to a [member defined by a reference](#references), so that a source which is itself a lens, or a reference to
a reactive root elsewhere, is written in turn. The lens's value then follows from its source along `forward`; nothing is
held at the lens's own site.

A lens may be laid by a stronger layer over a member which a weaker one defines in any other way, including a
`$reactiveRoot` and any links merged alongside it - the lens replaces it. This frees the site which a weaker layer used
to hold state, e.g. a filter's `filterState`, to be supplied from elsewhere, such as the URL.

'''
assert anchor in t
t = t.replace(anchor, doc + anchor, 1)
open(p, "w").write(t)

● Every active filter in the BBEA, Blitz/Diatoms and story pages now writes its state into the URL and restores from it, through a new `$lens` construct in Infusion. A headless-browser run of the BCBA page confirmed:
  - loading `#elevation:200,900&phenology:6,7&sex:female` restores all three filters and their badges;
  - unchecking a box rewrites the URL;
  - Back restores the previous state.
  
  All suites pass: Infusion (2206), copyout, hydrate round trip, the bagatelle QUnit suites (89, 25, 49, 26), the BBEA and Blitz/Diatoms round trips, and the story navigation and round trips in both projects. Lint is clean.
  
  **`$lens` (Infusion, `FluidIL.js`)**
  - **Syntax:** a record `{source, forward, backward}`.
    - `forward` works like `$compute`, with `{0}` meaning the source's value.
    - `backward` works like `$method`: it receives the written value as `{0}` and returns the source's new value.
  - **Writes:** a write at or beneath the lens is caught in `fluid.setForComponent`. It is applied to the lens's value, passed through `backward`, and written to the end of the source's chain of references, so chains of lenses work.
  - **Overlaying:** a stronger layer can lay a lens over a `$reactiveRoot` and its links, which is how both of your cases are done.
  - **Edge identity:** I didn't need to change the identity of edges in the signals system. A lens is an ordinary computed cell, and writes go to the source's site rather than through a second in-edge. A real two-way edge at the cell level would need that rework, but this design doesn't use one.
  - **Tests and docs:** two new tests cover a lens over a reactive root and a chain of two lenses. `$lens` is documented in ponder's `fluid-integration-language.md`. `dist/fluid.boot.min.js` is rebuilt.
  
  **URL-mapped filters (bagatelle)**
  - **`hortis.urlMappedFilter`** (in `filters.js`) gives a filter:
    - a `urlKey`, by default its member name minus "Filter";
    - a `urlCodec`, named globally.
  - **The linkage:** `hashManager.js` holds a `$linkage` that lays `hortis.urlMappedFilter.linked` over every such filter, only when there is a window. That layer makes `filterState` a lens onto the filter's entry in `{hashManager}.hash`. The filters themselves never refer to the hashManager. Under hydration there's no window, so filters render empty.
  - **Codecs:**
  
    | Codec | Used by | Held in the URL as |
    |---|---|---|
    | `string` | collector, map cell | the value itself |
    | `keys` | regions, value filters, checklists | comma-separated keys |
    | `flags` | sex, Blitz status | comma-separated names of the flags set |
    | `range` | elevation | `lower,upper` |
    | `taxonRow` | taxon search | the taxon's id |
    | months | phenology | month numbers 1–12 |
    | WKT | polygon | `POLYGON` or `MULTIPOLYGON`, rounded to 5 decimal places |
  
  - **Explicit keys:** `bees`, `plants`, `sex`, `cell`, `polygon`, `status`, `taxon`, and value filters by their field.
  - **elevationFilter:** `filterState` is now a free member, null when unrestricted. The two-way relation with the slider is a `$lens` over `dualRangeInput.range`.
  - **Checklists:** selection moved out of `userState` into its own `filterState`, holding only the topmost selected ids (selecting Apidae writes `bees:10`, not all its species).
    - **Behaviour change:** a taxon that later appears under a selected parent now shows as selected.
  - **Polygons:** the polygon filter draws any polygons restored from the URL when the map starts.
  - **Tests:** the BBEA tests clear the hash before each test, and new tests cover URL mapping and the codecs.
  
  **Renames**
  - **Data table:** `dataTable.js` is now inside its SFC.
  - **Icons:** `hortis-mfIcons.vue` / `hortis.mfIcons` became `hortis-icons.vue` / `hortis.icons`.
  - **Classes:** 57 `mf-` names used outside the BBEA files became `imerss-`. One clash with the older visualisations' `imerss-taxa` was avoided by naming the list class `imerss-taxon-list`.
  - **Symbol ids:** every one now has the `imerss-i-` prefix. The two pairs with different glyphs got separate ids: `imerss-i-search-wide` and `imerss-i-download-wide`.
  - **Stylesheets:** the old Infusion 4 BBEA pages and `js/new` still use the `mf-` names, so `imerss-bbea.css` is unchanged. The Infusion 6 SFCs load a renamed copy, `imerss-bbea-i6.css`.
  
  **Not done or worth knowing**
  - **Story filters not mapped:** the status filter and story region already take their state from the story page, and the choropleth slider's state is computed, so none of these is URL-mapped.
  - **Polygons on Back:** navigating back changes which observations the polygon filter shows, but doesn't redraw the polygons on the map.

 * encoding for the URL, which is blind to the ids and properties MapboxDraw assigns to them, and are drawn as decoded
 * from it, since MapboxDraw accepts only plain GeoJSON rather than the proxied state.
 * @param {Object[]} filterState - The GeoJSON features of the filter's state
 * @param {Object} record - The record of the bound draw control, as returned by `hortis.libreMap.polygonFilter.makeDraw`

hortis.libreMap.polygonFilter.syncDraw = function (filterState, record) {

    const encoded = codec.encode(filterState);

● The polygon filter now redraws on Back. On the lens question, the signals layer can already hold a lens as two ordinary computed edges, one in each direction, but not in our real cases yet; I've left `$lens` as it is and set out the two pieces that are missing. All suites pass and lint is clean.
  
  ## Polygon redraw (`polygonDraw.js`)
  
  - **The fix:** a new effect, `syncDraw`, watches `filterState` and the draw control. It redraws whenever the state no longer matches what is on the map.
  - **No loop with drawing:** it compares the state and the drawing by their URL encoding. That encoding ignores MapboxDraw's ids and rounds to 5 places, so a state that came from drawing always matches and is left alone.
  - **`reset`** now just empties `filterState`; the effect clears the drawing.
  - **A related bug:** the bind-time drawing I added last round never worked. MapboxDraw rejected the copied state as "Invalid FeatureCollection", probably because `fluid.copy` of the proxied array doesn't give a plain array. The effect replaces that code and draws what it decodes from the encoding instead.
  - **Browser check:** I loaded the BCBA page with polygon A in the URL (1,345 records) and set polygon B (293). Back redrew A (1,345 again), and clearing the hash removed it. There were no errors.
  - **Not checked:** the check didn't draw a polygon by hand, so the claim that drawing never triggers a redraw rests on the reasoning above.
  
  ## A symmetric `$lens`
  
  I tried the forward and backward arcs as two ordinary computed edges, one on each cell. The signals layer already supports a two-way pair: the cell can hold several incoming edges, and an update records which way it is travelling so it doesn't bounce straight back.
  
  - **Two cells, slider ↔ state:** works in both directions, including the null "full range" state.
  - **Three cells, slider ↔ state ↔ hash:** works only once the hash arc writes a whole cell by itself. Three things stand in the way:
    1. **Backward arcs that need their own target.** Writing the elevation state back into the hash means merging it with the hash's other keys, so the arc must read the hash it writes. That edge goes dead: in the test, a write to the slider reached the state but never the hash. The current `putThroughLens` gets round this by writing to a path inside the hash. A symmetric version would need edges that can target a path within a cell, or each hash key held in its own cell.
    2. **Edge identity.** The backward edge sits on the source's cell and is keyed by its first source, the lens cell. If the component holding the lens is replaced, the new lens adds a second edge instead of replacing the first, and the old edge stays on the source pointing at a dead cell. The fix is the stable identity you suggested: key the edge by the lens's path in the component tree (e.g. `elevationFilter.dualRangeInput.range`) and remove it when that component is destroyed. That is contained work in `computed` plus the teardown when a component is destroyed.
    3. **A pair joined after both cells have settled doesn't run.** Joining an arc to cells that already have values assumes they agree, so a hash present at startup wasn't picked up. This would need an initial pull along the newly joined edge.
  
  **Recommendation:** keep `$lens` as it is for now. A symmetric version is worth building once 1 and 2 are done; 1 is the larger piece of design.
  
  ## Signals bug fixed (`FluidSignals.js`)
  
  When `computed` was called again with an edge key the cell already had, it updated the existing edge and then added it to the cell's list a second time. Infusion's tests didn't catch this, and it would have affected any identity scheme. It now adds the edge only when the edge is new, and all suites still pass with the fix.

p="FluidIL.js"; s=open(p).read()
anchor='''    /**
     * Write a value through a lens'''
assert anchor in s
s=s.replace(anchor,'''    /**
     * Compute the stable key of a relation made from a site within a component - the path of the site in the component
     * tree. Unlike the cells along the relation, this survives the turnover of the component, so that a relation made
     * afresh from the same site replaces the one made before, rather than standing beside it
     * @param {Shadow} shadow - The shadow of the component holding the site
     * @param {String[]} segs - The path of the site within the component
     * @return {String} The key, e.g. "elevationFilter.dualRangeInput:range"
     */
    fluid.siteEdgeKey = function (shadow, segs) {
        return shadow.path + ":" + segs.join(".");
    };

    /**
     * Establish a computed relation onto a cell, which may be held by another component, on behalf of a site within a
     * component. The relation is keyed by the path of the site, so that it is replaced when the site makes it afresh,
     * e.g. as its component turns over and allocates fresh cells along it, and is torn down when the component is
     * destroyed. The target cell may thereby hold several relations, e.g. the arcs of a bidirectional relation, each
     * identified by the site which made it
     * @param {Shadow} shadow - The shadow of the component holding the site
     * @param {String[]} segs - The path of the site within the component
     * @param {Cell} target - The cell onto which the relation is made
     * @param {Function} fn - The function computing the target's value from the sources'
     * @param {Cell[]} staticSources - The relation's sources
     * @param {ComputedProps} [props] - Any further properties of the relation
     * @return {Cell} The target cell
     */
    fluid.attachSiteEdge = function (shadow, segs, target, fn, staticSources, props) {
        const key = fluid.siteEdgeKey(shadow, segs);
        target.computed(fn, staticSources, {...props, key});
        const siteEdges = shadow.frameworkEffects.siteEdges = shadow.frameworkEffects.siteEdges || [];
        const existing = siteEdges.findIndex(rec => rec.key === key);
        const record = {key, target, dispose: () => target.computed(null, null, {key})};
        if (existing === -1) {
            siteEdges.push(record);
        } else {
            siteEdges[existing] = record;
        }
        return target;
    };

    /**
     * Tear down a relation made by `fluid.attachSiteEdge`
     * @param {Shadow} shadow - The shadow of the component holding the site
     * @param {String[]} segs - The path of the site within the component
     */
    fluid.detachSiteEdge = function (shadow, segs) {
        const key = fluid.siteEdgeKey(shadow, segs);
        const siteEdges = shadow.frameworkEffects.siteEdges || [];
        const existing = siteEdges.findIndex(rec => rec.key === key);
        if (existing !== -1) {
            siteEdges[existing].dispose();
            siteEdges.splice(existing, 1);
        }
    };

'''+anchor,1)

● Edges can now be identified by the path of the component site that made them, rather than by their first source. Infusion passes 2222/2222, including four new tests; everything else is unchanged and passing, and lint is clean. I've rebuilt `dist/fluid.boot.min.js`.
  
  **Signals (`FluidSignals.js`)**
  - `computed(fn, sources, props)` takes an optional `props.key`. When given, that key identifies the edge; otherwise it is still the first source, so existing code behaves as before.
  - Wiring an edge with a key the cell already has replaces that edge, even if its sources are new cells. Wiring with `fn` set to null and the same key removes it.
  - `refresh` accepts the same `props` to find an edge by its key.
  - The new helper `fluid.cell.edgeKey` works out the key.
  
  **Components (`FluidIL.js`)**
  - `fluid.siteEdgeKey(shadow, segs)` gives the key, e.g. `bcba-6.map.polygonDraw:filterState`. It stays the same across turnover.
  - `fluid.attachSiteEdge(shadow, segs, target, fn, sources, props)` wires an edge onto any cell, including one held by another component, on behalf of a site.
    - Attaching again from the same site replaces the edge, so turnover that allocates fresh cells leaves no stale edge pointing at dead ones.
    - The edge is recorded with the component and removed when the component is destroyed.
  - `fluid.detachSiteEdge(shadow, segs)` removes it explicitly.
  
  **Tests**
  - **Signals:** explicit keys replace and remove edges, and coexist with edges keyed by their sources. A second wiring under the same key no longer duplicates the edge.
  - **Components:** an edge from a site drives its target, is replaced when made afresh, sits beside edges from other sites, and is gone once its component is destroyed.
  
  **Worth knowing**
  - **No production callers yet.** `$lens` still writes through `putThroughLens` and doesn't create edges. This work is the foundation for a symmetric lens.
  - **The first-run rule still holds.** An edge wired onto a cell that already has a value is assumed to agree with it, and first runs when a source changes. For a backward arc I think that's the right default: at startup a hash already in the URL should win over the slider's default. The component test therefore uses a fresh target.
  - **Teardown waits for stabilising.** A component's destruction finishes only when the cells next stabilise, so a site's edges disappear then and not at the `destroy()` call itself.
  
  A symmetric `$lens` is still blocked by the other gap from the prototype. A backward arc into the hash has to merge with the hash's other keys, so it reads its own target. That needs either edges aimed at a path within a cell, or one cell per hash key. Say if you want me to take that on next.


❯ Explain what "edges aimed at a path within a cell" means and what it would look like

● Today an edge recomputes its target's whole value from its sources. An edge aimed at a path would instead own one slot inside the target's value, say `hash.elevation`. When it fires it writes only that slot, and the rest of the record is left as it is.
  
  ## The problem it solves
  
  The backward arc from the elevation state into the hash has to produce the whole new hash:
  
  ```js
  hash.computed((state, hash) => ({...hash, elevation: encode(state)}), [state, hash]);
  ```
  
  So the edge must read the hash, the cell it writes. That's a self-loop. When I ran it, the update reached the state and stopped there, because the signals layer won't send an update back along an arc it has just travelled. The arc never really needed the rest of the hash; it only needed it to copy it through unchanged.
  
  ## What it would look like
  
  The edge carries a path, and its function returns just the value for that path:
  
  ```js
  hash.computed(state => encode(state), [state], {key: siteKey, path: ["elevation"]});
  ```
  
  When this edge is chosen to update `hash`, the signals layer does the copying itself. It writes the result into the target's current value with something like `fluid.setImmutable(hash._value, ["elevation"], result)`, which builds a new record without changing the old one, and commits that. The edge's only source is `state`, so the self-loop is gone and the update travels normally: slider → state → hash.
  
  A cell could then hold several edges at once:
  - a whole-value edge, e.g. the one fed by the URL listener;
  - path edges from many sites, one each for `elevation`, `bees`, `sex`, and so on, keyed by site as in the last change.
  
  The forward direction stays an ordinary edge on the filter's state that reads `hash.elevation`. So `$lens` could become two plain edges with no special write handling.
  
  ## What it would take
  
  - **Writing:** edges carry an optional `path`. When an edge with a path fires, the signals layer writes its result into the target's current value at that path instead of replacing the value.
  - **Choosing an edge:** today a dirty cell runs one edge, the one it was dirtied from. With path edges, a whole-value write (from the URL) and a path write (from the slider) can both be pending in one update. The rule would be: run the whole-value edge first, then any pending path edges on top of it. Path edges for different slots never conflict.
  - **Stopping the echo:** the path edge into `hash.elevation` and the forward edge reading `hash.elevation` form a two-way pair. Updates already record which way they are travelling, so the echo back is stopped as it is today. But that record would need to know about paths, so that a write to `hash.bees` doesn't wake the elevation lens. Comparing the decoded value stops the echo anyway, but path-aware tracking would save the needless runs.
  - **Missing parents:** writing at `["a", "b"]` when `a` is absent would create it, as `setImmutable` already does. Removing a key, e.g. returning `undefined` to drop `elevation` from the URL, would need a deliberate "delete" result.
  - **When the target is unavailable:** a path edge can't write into an unavailable value. The hash is unavailable under node, so such an edge would wait, as edges do today on unavailable sources.
  
  ## The alternative
  
  Hold each hash key in its own cell, as a reactive record whose members are cells. Each backward arc then writes a whole cell and no path edges are needed. The cost moves into the hash manager, which would have to assemble the record from those cells to render the URL, and split it into them again when the URL changes.
  
  I'd lean towards path edges. They match how a write to a reference already works, writing at a path, and they would apply to any reactive record, not just the hash.

● I've written the report to `infusion-6/a-scratch/reports/options-for-structural-lenses.md`. It recommends option A, path edges. The code in it is illustrative only: nothing in it has been implemented or run, and the line counts are estimates.
  
  **Option A, path edges**
  - **FluidSignals.js:** edges gain an optional `path`, and the edge's result is written into the target's current value at that path. Removing a member needs a distinct "delete" result. The rule for which edge runs changes: a whole-value write runs first, then every pending path edge on top of it, shortest path first.
  - **IL level:** `$lens` is written as today, but expands into a forward cell plus a backward edge onto the source's cell, at the path where the source reads it. The intercept in `setForComponent`, `putThroughLens` and the lens special case in `isMatForming` all go.
  - **elevationFilter:** the SFC doesn't change. The hash keeps one cell, carrying one backward edge per URL-mapped filter, each keyed by its site. `encode` loses its hash argument and its merging code.
  
  **Option B, cell records**
  - **FluidSignals.js:** the edge machinery doesn't change. A new container holds a cell per member and a computed whole-record view, and needs a batch API so that writing the whole record counts as one change.
  - **IL level:** the larger change. It needs a new kind of reactive root, plus new handling of references, writes and proxies for it.
  - **elevationFilter:** the SFC doesn't change. The hash manager declares `hash` as a cell record, and each filter's backward edge sits on its own member cell.
  
  **Why A:** a write through a reference is already a write at a path within a cell, so path edges make the graph match what the IL already does. They also work on any reactive data without being declared in advance. Its risk is concentrated in the edge-choosing code, where it can be tested in isolation.
  
  The report ends with work needed for either option. The main item is a lens source whose last segment is computed, such as `{hashManager}.hash.{self}.urlKey`. The other is checking at boot that a value already in the URL wins over the slider's default.

● Option A can credibly be the beginning of that rework, but only its contract, not the implementation I sketched in the report. Option B would make the rewrite harder, because it is itself the pattern you want to remove. This partly revises the report's recommendation.
  
  ## Option B builds public zebras
  
  A cell record is exactly a "public zebra": a record whose members are cells, with values inside them. To make it usable it needs:
  - a new kind of reactive root;
  - references that stop partway at a member cell;
  - writes that tell a whole-record write from a member write;
  - a proxy that presents cells as plain members.
  
  All of that is the machinery the fds chat wants gone. B looks gentler only in `FluidSignals.js`. At the IL level it spreads the zebra into reference resolution, writes and proxies, and every piece would have to be taken out again in a rewrite.
  
  ## Option A's meaning matches the trajectory
  
  A path edge means "this relation owns the value at address P in some data; writing it preserves the siblings; an asynchronous result lands against the data as it then stands." That is the write gateway from the chat almost word for word: mutate at P, and leave everything else alone.
  
  Each part of option A has a counterpart in the side-table design:
  
  | Option A in the report | The side-table design in the chat |
  |---|---|
  | `applyAtPath` with `setImmutable` | Mutate in place at P and bump P's revisions. The contract is the same; only the clone-to-root goes. |
  | Path edges kept beside the whole-value edge | Several writers, each owning a different address within one plain structure. |
  | Path-aware `markStale` (the optional refinement) | The own and subtree revisions: a reader of `hash.elevation` depends on own at that path, `pushState` on subtree at `hash`. |
  | A computed final segment in the source (`hash.{self}.urlKey`) | A sited reference reduced to a path plus a revision lookup. |
  | `fluid.siteEdgeKey` | Nodes identified by their address (Nominal Adapton, Salsa's tracked structs). The relation's identity is where it was declared, so it needs no object until something refers to it. |
  
  So the abstraction A introduces, a relation targeting an address within plain data, outlives the cell representation. That is what makes it a credible first step.
  
  ## But the report puts A's implementation in the wrong place
  
  The report places path edges inside `fluid.cell`'s multi-edge machinery: a new rule in `findDirtyEdge` for choosing edges, an `update` that loops over several edges, and fits that track paths. In the chat you said that machinery is "hugely wasteful": thousands of `_inEdges` arrays with one entry and perhaps none that validly has more. The suggested order of work was to move multi-edge support out into a rare node kind. The report would make that machinery more complicated, and make the hash cell the system's first heavy user of it.
  
  The cleaner version of A doesn't put the backward arc in the cell graph at all. It becomes a declared writer at an address:
  - recorded in the side table under its site key;
  - scheduled like any computation, carrying the provenance of what it read;
  - committing through the write gateway at its path.
  
  Today's `putThroughLens` is already most of this. It reads the lens's value, applies `backward`, and writes at the source's terminal site through `setForComponent`. It is a sanctioned write from a computation into owned state, the "blessed cod reactivity" of the chat. Measured against the chat's protocol, it lacks only three things:
  1. **Staging:** the write should be queued for the scheduler rather than applied inline.
  2. **Reads:** it should record what it read, so that a missed wake can be detected.
  3. **Identity:** it should be registered by its address, which `fluid.siteEdgeKey` now provides.
  
  The forward arc is then an ordinary single-updater reader of `hash.elevation`.
  
  The echo the fits were preventing is handled by provenance: the backward write carries its source, as `excludeSource` already does for `pushState`. No cell needs two in-edges, so this relation needs no bidirectional node kind at all. That suggests even your rare bidirectional cases may often be a pair of address writers rather than a multi-edge cell.
  
  ## How I'd revise the plan
  
  - **Keep A's contract:**
    - a relation targets an address within plain data;
    - a delete result to remove a member;
    - async results applied against the data as it then stands;
    - a computed final segment in the source;
    - backward arcs that receive only their own slot, so `encode` loses the hash argument.
  - **Implement it beside the cell graph, not in it.**
    - Lens expansion registers the backward arc as an address writer under its site key, which reuses `attachSiteEdge`'s bookkeeping.
    - The writer commits through `setForComponent`.
    - `findDirtyEdge` and the fits stay untouched, ready to be moved out later.
  - **Use it as the protocol's first test.** It needs to answer "what's your key?", "what did you read?" and "who must be woken?" (readers of `hash` and its subtree). This is the step the chat's order of work calls "convert one subsystem to address-keyed nodes and see whether the bookkeeping disappears or just moves". It is a small, contained relation where that can be measured.
  - **The one real gap is "who read me?".** While `hash` remains a cell, a write at `hash.elevation` replaces the whole cell value and wakes every reader of it. That is coarse but correct, and it is the "revision per region" minimum the chat names. Fine-grained own revisions arrive only when the data under `hash` becomes plain, mutated in place with the revisions kept beside it. That step needs no change to the lens contract, which is the sense in which A is a beginning rather than a dead end.
  
  **One caution from the chat:** path keying is unstable for array members (the `$for` index problem). A site key such as `…elevationFilter:filterState` is stable because it is a component path, and hash members are named keys. But a lens targeting an element of a list would need the identity anchor plus relative path from the chat, e.g. `todos#t42.selection`, not a positional path. Option A's contract should name its target in that form from the start, even if only named keys are supported at first.
  
  I can rewrite the report's recommendation and implementation sections along these lines if you'd like.

● I've written the second version to `infusion-6/a-scratch/reports/options-for-structural-lenses-2.md`, beside the first. Like the first, it's a design document: nothing in it has been implemented or tested.
  
  **Part 1** is my last response, formatted as GFM.
  
  **Part 2** gives the same three views as the first report, for the revised design:
  - **FluidSignals.js:** almost nothing changes. The explicit edge keys and the duplicate-edge fix stay. Echo is suppressed with what already exists: `withAmbientSource` on the write and `excludeSource` on the readers.
  - **IL:** a `$lens` expands into a forward computed plus an "address writer". The writer is recorded by its site key with its owning component, records what it read, and commits at the target's path through `setForComponent`. The write gateway gains deletion, and a lens source can name a path with a computed last segment.
  - **elevationFilter:** unchanged. `encode` shrinks to encoding the filter's own state.
  
  **Part 3** takes up your star-shape case: one filter state synced to the slider, the URL and an Automerge document.
  - **It corrects Part 1.** Its claim becomes: no *computed* cell needs two in-edges, but a piece of held state at the centre of a star needs many writers. The existing multi-edge cell is already a last-writer-wins register: `findDirtyEdge` prefers the edge from the cell it was dirtied from. So the need was real; it was represented in the wrong place.
  - **The star suits plain data better than cells.** Each store's inward arc is a writer at the state's address, and its outward arc is a reader that excludes writes from its own store. No list of in-edges builds up on the state.
  - **What's left is policy that must be declared:**
    - which store wins at boot, by role and rank;
    - what happens when two stores change in one stabilisation;
    - an Automerge document that loads after the URL has already set the state;
    - whether a back navigation should reach a shared document.
  - **The current declaration can't scale.** A second linkage laying its own `$lens` on `filterState` would lose silently in the merge. The report proposes an accumulating `$sync` declaration instead, so `filterState: null` stays the filter's whole definition. It adds a fourth node kind to the chat's protocol table, the "synced register", and a revised order of work that tries local storage as a second store before Automerge.

  Infusion
  - path on $lens: an optional address within the source, given as a string, an
    array of segments, or a reference such as "{self}.urlKey". The forward arc
    sees only the value at that address. The backward arc returns only that
    address's new value, and writing it leaves the source's other members alone.
    Lenses without a path behave as before.
  - fluid.deleteMarker: returned from a backward arc, it removes the address
    from the source. I added it to fluid.setImmutable, so setForComponent needed
    no change of its own.
  - Address writers: each lens registers its backward arc with its component
    under the lens's site key (fluid.registerSiteWriter; fluid.siteWriterOf
    finds it). A lens re-created at the same site replaces it, and it goes when
    the component does. It isn't an edge on any cell, so findDirtyEdge and the
    fits are untouched.
  - Provenance on lens writes: putThroughLens now does the writing. It commits
    under the writer's key as the change's source marker, so an effect can
    recognise or exclude lens writes with excludeSource. It also records its
    last write for explanation.
  - Tests and docs: the new test covers viewing an address, siblings left alone,
    the source marker, the last-write record, deletion, and a store write seen

      861  This boots the page as a browser would, waits for the graph to
            settle, and writes the rendered page, by default to
      862  `page-hydrated.html`. If the graph settles with the page still
            unready, it exits with an error listing the pending
      863  effects. Data fetched by `fluid.fetch` and its relatives, or b
           y any asynchronous `$compute`, is waited for, and a
      864 -relative URL is resolved against the page.                    
      864 +relative URL is resolved against the page. Scripts the page ho
          +lds as its own are evaluated in document order before it      
      865 +boots, as in the browser. An example is a script defining the 
          +layer named by its `fluid-layers`. A script whose `src`       
      866 +is remote is not evaluated, and nor is one bearing `fluid-clie
          +nt`. Injected scripts, stylesheets and symbols are placed     
      867 +in the head after its last `<fluid-import>`, in the order they
          + are made. So a stylesheet the page holds after its           
      868 +imports overrides those of its SFCs in the same way, whether t
          +he page is hydrated or booted in the browser.                 
      869  
      870 +Hydration is reversible. Everything `hydrate.js` adds to the p
          +age is marked with `data-fluid-hydrated`:                     
      871 +                                                              
      872 +* An element added beside the page's own, e.g. an injected scr
          +ipt, stylesheet or symbol host, bears an empty value.         
      873 +* An element on which a component booted bears the JSON of its
          + attributes and content as the page wrote them.               
      874 +* When the bootstrap of Infusion is written in the `source` or
          + `built` form, the first script it is expanded into           
      875 +  bears `boot:` followed by the bootstrap's `src`.            
      876 +                                                              
      877 +`src/framework/server/dehydrate.js` reverses this. It writes t

      878 +by `fluid.serializeDocument`:                                 
      879 +

      883 +                                                              
      884 +So a site may keep its pages hydrated in place and recover eac

● All five parts are in place, and every suite passes: Infusion 2229/2229,
  copyout, hydrate round trip, bagatelle QUnit 111/25/49/26, the BBEA and
  standard round trips, and both stories' navigation and round trips. node 
  build.js also completes with all five i6 docs pages verified. Nothing has been
  committed.

  Phenology filter, two modes
  - State: filterState is now {months, days}. The month checkboxes still bind
    through filterState.months.
  - Slider: a second hortis.dualRangeInput is a $lens onto the filter's state
    with path: "days", so it uses the address-lens contract from last time
    directly.
  - Labels: the thumbs show dates like "16 Mar 24" as they slide, and the two
    labels can't overlap or run off the track.
  - Exclusivity: checking a month disables the slider, moving the slider
    disables the months, and reset clears both.
  - URL: months still encode as 6 or 1,12, and a period encodes as
    2024-04-01~2024-06-15. It fitted the codec scheme with no hash manager
    changes, and Back restores either mode.
  - Detents: these are tick marks at each month start, with no snapping, so
    day-level precision is kept. Say if you want real snapping.
  - Shared component: hortis.dualRangeInput gained formatter, thumbLabels, ticks
    and disabled. The elevation filter is unchanged.
  - Checks: there's a new QUnit test and codec tests, and I checked it in a real
    browser by dragging on the BCBA page.

  Drivers inlined
  - drivers/ is gone; each page now defines its layer in an inline <script>.
  - To make that work, Infusion's loadAndBootDocument now runs a page's own
    scripts before booting. Its activateDocument call was commented out, which
    is why the drivers had to be SFCs.

  Reversible hydration
  - Everything hydrate.js adds is marked with data-fluid-hydrated:
    - Added elements carry an empty value.
    - Host elements carry the JSON of their original attributes and content.
    - The expanded bootstrap carries boot:<src>.
  - I couldn't use fluid-hydrated, because the browser treats any script
    carrying it as part of Infusion.
  - The new src/framework/server/dehydrate.js reverses it. The shared round-trip
    harness now checks that dehydrating gives back the original page exactly,
    for all eight pages in the suites.
  - Ordering bug fixed: this showed up as a real rendering difference on the OSU
    pages. The browser places injected stylesheets wherever the head parser has
    reached, which is before the page's later links. Node appended them after.
    Injections now always go after the head's last <fluid-import>, so the
    cascade is the same either way.

  OBA and WaBA drivers
  - indexBeasBCBA.html, indexBeasOBA.html and indexBeasWaBA.html at the root are
    now the i6 pages, replacing the Infusion 4 ones. indexBeasBCBA-6.html is
    deleted.
  - I generated placeholder data for OBA and WaBA.
  - The BBEA round-trip test now runs all three atlases.
  - In src/buildSource, the three BBEA pages keep their OSU header and
    analytics, and Blitz and Diatoms are i6 pages too.

  build.js
  - Slimmed: it now builds only imerss-viz-all for the lz4 pages, plus
    imerss-viz-lib and imerss-viz-new-core. Those are what Xetthecum's
    config.json5 copies. imerss-viz-new and its per-page scripts are dropped.
  - i6 pages: it copies them into docs and runs copyOut into docs/vendor. It
    then verifies each with its round-trip test and hydrates it in place;
    dehydrate.js recovers the source. node build.js i6 --no-verify is a faster
    path.
  - Path changes: Infusion 6 now lives in docs/vendor/infusion-6, because the
    Infusion 4 npm module infusion already takes vendor/infusion.
  - New copyOut flag: --ignore-missing <pattern>. The OSU stylesheets refer to
    theme images and fallback fonts that were never in this repo.

  Things to know
  - docs is rebuilt: 26 tracked files changed and the vendor tree was added.
  - Other projects' vendor copies: the test run refreshed the Howe Sound and
    Saanich vendor copies of Infusion, picking up the FluidView.js change.
  - Infusion bug: giving copyOut several different visualisation pages in one
    process crashes inside FluidIL. I haven't investigated it; build.js runs
    copyOut once per page instead.
  - Vue lint: I didn't lint the .vue files, because the eslint setup can't parse
    them.

  One thing to check first: making the inventory showed my previous slimming of
  build.js broke the Howe Sound and Saanich sites. Their config.json5 files copy
  imerss-viz-new.js and .css, imerss-viz.js, imerss-blitz.js and
  imerss-plants.js from bagatelle's docs, and their published pages still load
  them. I've put those outputs back, labelled in build.js as needed until those
  sites are served by their i6 ports.

  The copyOut crash
  - Cause: a bug in FluidIL's component proxy. Reading inside a member whose
    value is itself unavailable, such as the phenology slider's range lens while
    its source is pending, set next to undefined but still went on to
    dereference it.
  - Why only with several pages: when two pages of different kinds load in one
    process, one page's data is still pending at the moment a cell asks the
    slider's range for its staleValue. A single page never hits that timing.
  - Fix: such a read now returns the unavailable value's own member.
  - No unit test: my attempt to reproduce it in a unit test didn't reach the
    crashing path, so I dropped it. The regression check is build.js running
    copyOut once over all five pages.

  Whitespace in hydrated pages
  - What changed: every element hydration adds to the head or body now starts
    its own line at the indentation of the line before. Each symbol in the
    symbols host also gets its own line.
  - Reversing it: dehydrate.js removes exactly what was added, using a new
    data-fluid-indent mark. All three framework forms still dehydrate to the
    exact original.
  - Still long:
    - The minified libraries embedded inline, such as pako and papaparse, can't
      be reflowed without changing their text.
    - The rendered markup inside each host is all on one line. The template
      parser drops whitespace-only text, and hydration claims rendered nodes by
      position, so reflowing it safely means changing the parser on both sides.
      That's a separate job; say if you want it.

  fluid.scriptInjectionComplete
  - Why it isn't needed: a browser runs an inserted inline script synchronously,
    and reports syntax and runtime errors through the window's error event,
    which the code already captured. Under node, vm.runInContext throws.
  - What it uniquely caught: a script that never runs at all, because its
    document has no window or a content security policy blocks it. Both are now
    checked directly.
  - What's gone: the marker line is gone from wrapped scripts, along with
    fluid.injectionId.
  - Browser check: a good script, a runtime error, a syntax error and a
    window-less document are each reported correctly.
  - Shim kept: fluid.scriptInjectionComplete stays as an empty function, because
    pages hydrated earlier still call it.

  -6 pages folded away
  - indexBlitz.html and indexDiatoms.html are now the i6 pages, and the -6
    copies are deleted.
  - The standard round-trip test and the SFC comments now refer to the new
    names.

  utils.js dissolved
  - niceScale, truncateLabel and barChartMarkup moved to
    src/client/js/i6/bbea/barChart.js, which only hortis-beeAbundance.vue loads.
  - Everything else went into imerss-core.js:
    - General sections first: utilities, DOM listeners, images and SVG,
      reducers, resource loading and views.
    - Then the biodiversity sections: taxon rows, the taxon table and the
      visualisation loader.
  - The script references are updated in 25 bagatelle SFCs, a test page and 9
    SFCs in each story site. I deleted utils.js itself; it was untracked.

❯ List all of the fixes and improvements that have been made to Infusion in     
  this session - are you able to see back into the history before Claude        
  resumed this session?                                                         

● Partly. Everything since the session resumed is in full view. For the earlier
  part I only have the summary written when the context was compacted. It
  describes those Infusion changes but not every detail. The full transcript is
  saved at ~/.claude/projects/-home-amb26-Source-gits-bagatelle/dba32247-779e-45
  e2-b98b-d63581d4b6b6.jsonl if you want me to check anything exactly. The
  current state of the files is always readable, so git diff in infusion-6 gives
  the authoritative list.

  Before the resume (from the summary)

  Signals (FluidSignals.js)
  - Duplicate edges: computed added a duplicate in-edge every time it ran; it
    now adds one only when it creates the edge.
  - Edge identity: in-edges are identified by an explicit key, or else by their
    first static source (fluid.cell.edgeKey), and ComputedProps documents key.
  - Test: "Edges identified by an explicit key".

  Core (Fluid.js)
  - fluid.deleteMarker: a new marker. When a write carries it,
    fluid.setImmutable removes the member instead of setting it.

  IL (FluidIL.js)
  - Edges keyed by site: fluid.siteEdgeKey, fluid.attachSiteEdge and
    fluid.detachSiteEdge key edges by component path. An edge made again from
    the same site replaces the old one, and edges are torn down with their
    component.
  - path on $lens: a lens can own one address within its source. Its forward arc
    sees only that address, and its backward arc writes only that address.
  - Address writers: fluid.registerSiteWriter and fluid.siteWriterOf, with an
    AddressWriter typedef. They sit beside the cell graph rather than being
    edges in it.
  - Provenance on lens writes: fluid.putThroughLens commits under the writer's
    key as the change's source marker, so effects can exclude lens writes with
    excludeSource. It also records lastWrite.
  - Tests: site-edge keying and teardown, and the address lens.

  Docs: the $lens section of ponder's fluid-integration-language.md now covers
  path, deleteMarker and address writers.

  Since the resume

  Reversible hydration (server-support.js)
  - Marking: fluid.recordSourceDocument notes the page as parsed, and
    fluid.markHydration marks everything hydration adds with
    data-fluid-hydrated:
    - added elements carry an empty value;
    - host elements carry the JSON of their original attributes and content;
    - the expanded bootstrap carries boot:<src>.
  - Reversing: fluid.dehydrateDocument and the new
    src/framework/server/dehydrate.js restore the page exactly, in the boot,
    source and built framework forms.
  - Legible output: each added node gets its own line at the surrounding
    indentation, recorded by data-fluid-indent so dehydration removes exactly
    that whitespace. Symbols in the symbols host are also on separate lines.

  Server boot
  - Page scripts: fluid.evaluatePageScripts runs a page's own scripts in
    document order before booting, as a browser does. Previously the call was
    commented out, so a page could define no layers inline. Remote scripts and
    those marked fluid-client are skipped.

  Injection (FluidView.js)
  - Order fix: fluid.injectionAnchor places injections after the head's last
    <fluid-import>, in order. The browser had placed them wherever the head
    parser had reached and node appended them at the end, so the stylesheet
    cascade differed between hydrated and minimal pages.
  - Completion marker dropped: failures are now detected from the captured error
    event, a missing window or a content-security-policy refusal. Under node,
    failures are thrown. fluid.scriptInjectionComplete remains as an empty
    function for pages hydrated earlier, and fluid.injectionId is gone.

  IL bug fix (FluidIL.js)
  - Proxy crash: reading inside a member whose material is itself unavailable
    crashed with "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading '$variety')". It
    now reads through to the unavailable value. This was the crash when copyOut
    was given several pages in one process. There's no unit test, because I
    couldn't reproduce it in isolation; the regression check is build.js running
    copyOut over all five pages at once.

  copyOut
  - --ignore-missing <pattern>: references matching it may be missing without
    failing, and the summary counts them as ignored.

  Test support
  - hydration-roundtrip.js:
    - Every round trip now also checks that dehydrating the hydrated page gives
      back the original (dehydrationDifference).
    - The markup comparison ignores the data-fluid-hydrated marks.
  - Infusion's own tests:
    - hydrate-roundtrip-test.js and copyout-test.js now assert the dehydration
      check too.
    - copyout-test's count of bootstraps now looks only at src attributes, so
      the boot: mark isn't counted.

  Other
  - Docs: ponder's fluid-view.md now describes page-script evaluation, the
    injection order, the data-fluid-hydrated marks and dehydrate.js.
  - Bundle: dist/fluid.boot.min.js was rebuilt after these changes.

● I've added a unit test that reproduces the crash, and it turned up a second
  bug on the same path, which I've also fixed. With both fixes Infusion passes
  2233/2233, the bagatelle QUnit suites pass (111, 25, 49, 26), and the BBEA

  rebuilt.

  The test is "A cell holding the proxy of a member whose material becomes
  unavailable can update", in tests/framework-tests/core/js/FluidILTests.js. It
  uses a new fixture, fluid.tests.pendingLens: a lens over the existing
  fluid.tests.lensStore.
  1. A plain cell computes that.range, so its value is the member's proxy. The
     phenology slider's range was held the same way.
  2. The store is set to a pending unavailable value, and the cell is read.
  3. The test checks three things:
     - the cell updates without throwing;
     - reading within the proxy gives the unavailable value's members (variety
       is "pending");
     - the cell recovers once the store has data again.

  What the test shows
  - Without the FluidIL fix: it fails with the original crash, "Cannot read
    properties of undefined (reading '$variety')".
  - With only the FluidIL fix: it still crashed, now in fluid.cell.markStale in
    FluidSignals.js, reading staleValue from undefined. On an early cutoff,
    markStale restores each observer's stale value, assuming every observer's
    value is a pending unavailable. An observer that has never been computed has
    the value undefined. The restore now happens only when the value is
    unavailable.
  - Without the FluidSignals fix: the test fails, so it covers each fix on its
    own.

  My earlier attempt didn't reproduce the crash because it read the member
  inside a computation. The crash needs a cell whose value is the proxy itself,
  so that the cell's own update machinery probes it.

  fluid.isUnavailable is an instanceof test, so it never recognises a proxy as
  unavailable even when the material inside is. The fix makes reads within such
  a proxy consistent, but code testing isUnavailable on a proxy still gets
  false. I left that unchanged; say if you want it looked at.

● fluid.isUnavailable already worked on proxies, so I didn't change it. My test
  showed false because of a different bug: updating a cell overwrote the store's
  unavailable value with a plain copy. I've fixed that, and the test now
  asserts that the proxy reads as unavailable. Everything passes: Infusion
  2234/2234, the bagatelle suites, the BBEA and standard round trips, and both
  story sites. Lint is clean and the dist bundle is rebuilt.

  Why it already worked: the mat proxy has a getPrototypeOf trap that answers
  with the prototype of the material inside. So instanceof fluid.unavailable,
  which is what fluid.isUnavailable tests, is true whenever that material really
  is unavailable.

  What actually went wrong:
  - fluid.cell.mapSignalArgs, in FluidSignals.js, reuses a cell's previous
    pending unavailable value and adds the new causes to it in place.
  - In the test, that previous value was a proxy onto the store's unavailable
    material. The proxy correctly reads as pending, so it was reused.
  - Adding the causes then wrote causes, variety and message through the proxy's
    set trap into the store. The store's real unavailable value was replaced
    with a plain object.
  - From then on nothing in that chain was unavailable. That explains the false,
    and it was also why the material in the earlier crash looked like an
    unavailable but wasn't one.

  The fix: mapSignalArgs now reuses only a cell's own unavailable value, never a
  proxy. That uses a new helper, fluid.isProxy, in Fluid.js. In principle this
  could also have hit real pages: any cell whose value is a member proxy could
  overwrite that member's data when its source went pending.

  The test has two new assertions. They fail without this fix and pass with it:
  - the holder's value reads as unavailable through fluid.isUnavailable;
  - the store's own value is still unavailable after the cell updates.

  Remaining gap: fluid.deproxyUnavailable doesn't unwrap a mat proxy whose
  material is unavailable; it returned undefined. So you can't get at such a
  proxy's variety or causes through it. I dropped that check from the test
  rather than fix it here. Say if you want it handled, since it's the natural
  next step for reading an unavailable value through a proxy.

● fluid.deproxyUnavailable now returns the real unavailable value from either
  kind of proxy, so its variety, message and causes can be read. Everything
  passes: Infusion 2241/2241, the bagatelle suites, the BBEA and standard round
  trips, and both story sites. Lint is clean and the dist bundle is rebuilt.

  What was wrong: the old version relied on the $u symbol, and it failed for
  both kinds of proxy.
  - fluid.unavailableProxy: its descriptor trap claims every key exists, but
    reading $u through it gives undefined. So the function returned undefined,
    which is what happened in the earlier test.
  - Mat proxies: $u returns the proxy's raw target, a cell or material, which it
    returned without checking whether it was the unavailable value.

  What it does now (in Fluid.js):
  - It unwraps proxies through their $t target, de-signalling as it goes, until
    it reaches a value that isn't a proxy.
  - It returns that value if it is unavailable, and otherwise returns its
    argument unchanged, so plain unavailable values and ordinary values pass
    straight through.
  - The loop is capped at 16 steps as a guard.
  - The now-unused $u constant in Fluid.js is removed. fluid.unavailableSymbol
    itself stays, because FluidView.js and the mat proxy still use it for their
    own purpose.

  Tests
  - New test, "fluid.deproxyUnavailable recovers the unavailable value fronted
    by any proxy":
    - a plain unavailable value comes back as it is;
    - a fluid.unavailableProxy reads as unavailable and is unwrapped to its
      value, whose variety can then be read;
    - a plain object that merely has a variety member comes back unchanged.
  - The proxy-crash test now also checks two recoveries:
    - the holder's proxy is unwrapped to an unavailable value with variety
      "pending";
    - a mat proxy, store.store, gives back the store's own unavailable value,
      message included.
  - Without the fix: I checked the new assertions against the old function, and
    they fail.

  The two existing callers benefit too: fluid.unavailableToCauses and the
  merging of unavailable values in Fluid.js now read the causes of a proxied
  unavailable value correctly, where before they would have received undefined.

  Ran 1 shell command (ctrl+o to expand)

● I can't reproduce this from here, but the cause is almost certainly how the
  page is being opened, not a bug in the demo. The password is turned into a
  token with the browser's crypto.subtle. Browsers only provide that to pages
  served over HTTPS or from localhost/127.0.0.1. On a page opened from any other
  http:// address it's undefined, which is exactly the importKey error you saw.

  On WSL, a likely way to hit this is opening the page from a Windows browser at
  the WSL machine's IP address. To fix it, open the same URL with localhost as
  the host (http://localhost:<port>/...); WSL forwards localhost to Windows.
  Serving it over HTTPS works too. Nothing changed this session touches this
  code; it's the same as at the last commit.

  To make it obvious next time, I changed fluid.tldraw.ai.deriveToken in
  demo/tldraw/js/ai-protocol.js. It now checks for Web Crypto first and fails
  with a clear message: the page isn't a secure context, so serve it over HTTPS
  or open it at http://localhost instead of the current host. Lint passes; I
  haven't run it in a browser, and nothing has been committed.

  If you're already on localhost and still see this, tell me the URL you're
  using, since then it's something else.
