● My earlier change caused this, and it's fixed: npm run hydrate in Saanich now
  completes and writes the hydrated docs/story/index.html.

  Why it broke: to let pages define their layers inline, I made the server run a
  page's own scripts before booting it (fluid.evaluatePageScripts in Infusion's
  server-support.js). The Hugo-built page also holds the theme's browser-only
  scripts. One of them, the colour-theme script, reads localStorage, which
  doesn't exist under node, and the error stopped hydration. My tests missed it
  because they hydrate index-dev.html, which has none of the theme's scripts.

  The fix: as in a browser, a page script that throws no longer stops the ones
  after it. Each failure is logged, naming the script, and hydration continues.
  With the theme's script failing that way, the hydrated page also dehydrated
  cleanly.

  Infusion's suite (2241/2241), its hydrate round-trip test and both story
  sites' round trips pass. Nothing has been committed.

  I haven't run the full npm run build (that needs Hugo), only the hydrate step.
  Howe Sound hydrates the same kind of Hugo page, so it had the same problem
  and is fixed by the same change. Its hydrate step should now log the theme's
  script failure and carry on too; I didn't run it, to avoid overwriting its
  built docs.

  Infusion 6 package.json
  - Your guess was close: linkedom isn't the only hard dependency, but nearly.
    The server code requires linkedom, he, minimist and json5, so those four
    stay in dependencies.
  - Two latent bugs this fixed:
    - minimist, which all the command-line tools need, was only a devDependency.
    - json5, used by copyOut's --sources, wasn't declared at all.
    - A site installing Infusion 6 would have hit both.
  - Moved to devDependencies: preact, codemirror, jshint, acorn and the linters.
    They're only sources for the deps:* copy scripts, whose output is already
    in src/lib.
  - node-fetch removed: the fetch wrapper now uses node's built-in fetch and
    Response, so engines is now node 18 or later.
  - Checked: a dry-run install of the packed checkout into an empty project adds
    19 packages: Infusion 6 itself, linkedom and its small tree, he, minimist
    and json5.

  The boot step
  - New commands: fluid-hydrate, fluid-dehydrate and fluid-copyout, declared in
    Infusion 6's package.json as bin entries and implemented in its new bin/
    directory.
  - How they find Infusion: each reads the site's moduleOverrides.json5 if it
    has one. An infusion-6 entry runs the tool from that checkout; otherwise the
    installed copy is used.
  - fluid-copyout also gets the overrides file as its --sources, so every
    overridden module is copied from its checkout.
  - Version independence: bin/boot.js reaches the tools only by their fixed
    paths within Infusion, so any version keeping them there works with it.
  - Why not a separate infusion-6-boot package: a site couldn't depend on one
    without either publishing it or using a relative path again. bin/ can move
    into its own package unchanged when you want one.
  - Checks:
    - fluid-copyout gives the same result as the old explicit command line.
    - Running the Saanich story page through fluid-dehydrate, then
      fluid-hydrate, then fluid-dehydrate again gives back an identical page.
  - Usage messages: hydrate.js and dehydrate.js now print their usage when given
    no file. Before, hydrate.js crashed and dehydrate.js failed obscurely.

  Saanich
  - dependencies now holds only what the build needs:
    - infusion 4, which storyBuild.js still requires;
    - infusion-6 6.1.0;
    - imerss-bioinfo and @imerss/inat-components, which copyOut copies from;
    - js-yaml, json5 and linkedom, for storyBuild.js.

  src/lib. It lists the four hard dependencies under node:

  It also notes the node 18 requirement, and describes the fluid-hydrate,

● Since your last commit (25d7124, 12:30 today), these changes to Infusion are
  uncommitted. The tldraw error message is already in that commit, so it isn't
  listed here.

  Fixes

  1. Page scripts that fail no longer stop hydration (server-support.js).
     fluid.evaluatePageScripts now catches a page script that throws, reports
     it, and carries on with the rest, as a browser does. This was what broke
     Saanich's npm run hydrate: the Hugo theme's script reads localStorage,
     which doesn't exist under node.
  2. Injections are placed after the page's last <fluid-import>, wherever it is
     (FluidView.js). Previously only the head was searched, so a page whose
     bootstrap and import sit in the body got its injected scripts at the end of
     the head. When hydrated, those scripts ran before Infusion had loaded and
     failed with "fluid is not defined". That was the case for every Hugo-built
     story page, including the Saanich page.
  3. copyOut copies Infusion's own files from the Infusion it runs from
     (copyOut.js), unless another checkout is named. Without that, a site with
     Infusion installed from npm and no override had all twelve of its browser
     files reported missing.
  4. hydrate.js and dehydrate.js print their usage when given no file. Before,
     hydrate.js crashed and dehydrate.js failed obscurely.

  Packaging and boot

  5. Runtime dependencies cut to four (package.json): linkedom, he, minimist and
     json5.
     - minimist used to be only a devDependency, and json5 wasn't declared at
       all; both are needed by the command-line tools.
     - The client-library sources (preact, codemirror, the linters and so on)
       moved to devDependencies. A site installing Infusion now gets 19
       packages.
  6. node-fetch dropped. node-fetch-wrapper.js uses node's built-in fetch and
     Response, so engines now requires node 18 or later.
  7. New command-line tools fluid-hydrate, fluid-dehydrate and fluid-copyout, in
     bin/ and declared as bin entries.
     - Each honours the site's moduleOverrides.json5: an infusion-6 entry runs
       that checkout's tool.
     - fluid-copyout is also given the file as its --sources.
     - The tools reach Infusion only by fixed paths, so they serve any version
       that keeps its tools there.
  8. .npmignore now excludes a-scratch/ and 31-fixes.md, so your working notes
     aren't published.

  Tests and docs

  9. hydrate-roundtrip-test.js runs on two pages:
     - the existing index.html;
     - a new roundtrip/body-boot.html, laid out like a Hugo page with its
       bootstrap in the body.

     It checks that every injected script follows Infusion's bootstrap. It fails
     on the old injection placement with exactly the live error.
  10. README: the "Dependencies" section lists the four runtime dependencies,
      the node 18 requirement and the fluid-* tools.

  Not mine

  - the debug console.log lines removed from FluidIL.js, sfc-parser.js and
    server/fluid.js;
  - the "failed on the server" report in server-support.js switched to
    fluid.log.

  dist/ and the mirrored docs/src copies are regenerated to match.
